label: lem:eq-gap
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The variational gap at equilibrium

title: Proof
body_md:
The measure $\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}|_{(Q,1]}+\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}([0,Q])\delta_Q$ has distribution function
$\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ on $[Q,1]$, so $\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)=\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}+\varepsilon h$ with
$h=\mathbf{1}_{[0,Q)}$. Here $\|h\|_{L^1}=Q\le1$ and the glued coefficient takes values in
$[0,2]$. By \eqref{eq:eq-second}, \eqref{eq:eq-firstvar} and Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero},
\[
 P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\varepsilon\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)\bigr)+K\varepsilon^2
 =f_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\bigr)+K\varepsilon^2 .
\]
The claims about $\mathsf{x}$ are clear.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The containment $\{0\}\cup\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\subsetC_{\mathrm{P}}$ was proved in Section~\ref{sec:eq-obstacle}. The
probability bound has a localization part and a field-law part. We prove them in Steps~1 and~2
by the shell argument of Section~\ref{sec:loc-proof} and Appendix~\ref{app:var-field}, with
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-gap} as the source of the gain. Step~3 combines them, and Step~4 deduces the
fixed-radius statement. Convexity of $\xi$ on $[-1,1]$ enters only through the Slepian step of
Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison}; the toolbox of Appendix~\ref{app:pde-toolbox} and
the proofs of Lemmas~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle} and~\ref{lem:eq-zero} use only \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.

\emph{Shells and the comparison.} For $\rho\in(0,1]$ let $Q_j=j\rho$ and
$I_j=[Q_j,\min(Q_j+\rho,1)]$ for the integers $j\ge0$ with $Q_j<1$. There are at most
$\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1$ such shells, and they cover $[0,1]$. We use \eqref{eq:loc-glued-general}
with $s=0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison} with the approximation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-majorant}): if $\theta\in(0,1)$, $Q\in[0,1)$, $\rho'\in(0,1-Q]$,
$\mathsf{x}:[0,Q)\to[\theta,2]$ is nondecreasing (there is no cascade part if $Q=0$) and
$\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$, then for every $\varepsilon_A>0$ there is a random
variable $\mathcal T$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-majorant}
\begin{aligned}
 \sup\bigl\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m):\ m\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho']\bigr\}
 &\le N P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)+N\varepsilon_A+\mathcal T,\\
 \mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}&\le(N+1)\,e^{N\theta C_R\rho'},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with $C_R=5\xi''(1)$. The events below that involve all $m$ in the cube are contained in finite
unions of events $\{\mathcal T\ge a\}$, which is how their outer probabilities are bounded.

\emph{Step 1: localization.} Fix $\kappa>0$ and let
$A_\kappa=\{Q\in[0,1]:\operatorname{dist}(Q,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa/2\}$. If $A_\kappa$ is empty, no $m$ has $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa$, so the event of
\eqref{eq:eq-step1} is empty and there is nothing to prove; set $c_1:=c_2$ in Step~3. Otherwise $A_\kappa$ is compact and disjoint from $C_{\mathrm{P}}$, and
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$ is continuous, so
\[
 \gamma:=\min\bigl\{\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}:\ Q\in A_\kappa\bigr\}>0 .
\]
Put $\varepsilon=\min\{1,\gamma/(2K)\}$ and $\theta=\varepsilon/2$, choose $\rho\in(0,\kappa/2)$
with $C_R\rho\le\varepsilon\gamma/16$, and put $\varepsilon_A=\varepsilon\gamma/16$ and
$t=\varepsilon\gamma/8$.

If $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa$, then $q_m\in I_j$ for some $j$ with
$\operatorname{dist}(Q_j,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa-\rho>\kappa/2$. Such an anchor lies in $A_\kappa$; it satisfies
$Q_j>\kappa/2>0$ because $0\inC_{\mathrm{P}}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero}), and $Q_j<1$. So
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-gap} applies at $Q=Q_j$, and since $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q_j)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\ge\gamma$ and
$K\varepsilon\le\gamma/2$, its data satisfy
\[
 P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\gamma+K\varepsilon^2\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\gamma/2 .
\]
The cascade coefficient takes values in $[\varepsilon,2]\subset[\theta,2]$, so
\eqref{eq:eq-majorant} applies on $I_j$ and gives a random variable $\mathcal T_j$ with
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T_j}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho}$ and
\[
 \bigl\{\exists m:\ q_m\in I_j,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)\bigr\}
 \subset\bigl\{\mathcal T_j\ge N(\varepsilon\gamma/2-\varepsilon_A-t)\bigr\}
 =\bigl\{\mathcal T_j\ge\tfrac5{16}N\varepsilon\gamma\bigr\}.
\]
By Markov's inequality applied to $e^{\theta\mathcal T_j}$, this event has probability at most
\[
 (N+1)\exp\Bigl\{N\theta\Bigl(C_R\rho-\frac5{16}\varepsilon\gamma\Bigr)\Bigr\}
 \le(N+1)\,e^{-N\theta\varepsilon\gamma/4}.
\]
A union bound over the at most $\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1$ shells gives, for all large $N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-step1}
 \mathbb{P}^{*}\bigl(\exists m\in[-1,1]^N:\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t),\ \operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa\bigr)
 \le e^{-c_1N},
\end{equation}
where $c_1:=\theta\varepsilon\gamma/8=\varepsilon^2\gamma/16\le t$.

\emph{Step 2: field law.} Fix $\kappa>0$. Let $\tilde g_1,\dots,\tilde g_J$ be the smooth test
functions of Lemma~\ref{lem:var-net} for the accuracy $\kappa$: they satisfy
$\|\tilde g_j'\|_\infty\le1$, $\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty<\infty$, and for probability measures
$\mu,\mu'$ on $[-1,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-net}
 W_1(\mu,\mu')\ge\kappa\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \int\tilde g_j\,d(\mu-\mu')\ge\kappa/2\ \text{ for some } j .
\end{equation}
The map $q\mapsto\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{q}$ is uniformly continuous on $[0,1]$, because
$q\mapsto u(q,X_q)$ is almost surely continuous and bounded by $1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}); let $\omega_{\mathrm P}$ be a common modulus of continuity for
$j=1,\dots,J$.

We need the perturbed comparison at a base point other than a minimizer. Let
$\zeta'\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $\theta\in(0,1)$ with $\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\theta$,
let $L'_Q=\operatorname{Law}(\partial_x\Phi_{\zeta'}(Q,X'_Q))$ be the field law of $\zeta'$ ($X'$ its
Auffinger--Chen process), and let $Q\in[0,1)$, $\rho'\in(0,1-Q]$,
$0<s\le(2\max_j\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty)^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon_A>0$. Then for each $j$ there is a
random variable $\mathcal T$ with $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho'}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-perturbed}
 \sup\Bigl\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^N\tilde g_j(m_i):\ q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho']\Bigr\}
 \le N\bigl[P_{\zeta'}+s\int\tilde g_j\,dL'_Q+C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A\bigr]+\mathcal T,
\end{equation}
where $C_2=1+L_\psi$, with $L_\psi$ as in~\eqref{eq:pde-constants}, depends only on $\xi'(1)$
and $\xi''(1)$. This is
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-tangent}\ref{lem:var-tangent-b} with $g=\tilde g_j$: the comparison of
Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison} at the base point $(\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta')$,
with the terminal condition perturbed by $s\tilde g_j$. Its proof uses only
$\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\theta$, which makes this base point admissible, and not any minimality of
$\zeta'$; so it applies to the measure $\zeta'$ chosen below.

Let $L_M$ be the Lipschitz constant of the field law in the coefficient
(Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}\ref{cor:pde-step-d} and Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}): under the
coupling by a common Brownian motion,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl|\partial_x\Phi_{\zeta_1}(t,X^{(1)}_t)-\partial_x\Phi_{\zeta_2}(t,X^{(2)}_t)\bigr|\le
 L_M\|\bar{\zeta_1}-\bar{\zeta_2}\|_{L^1}.
\]
Choose, in this order,
\[
 s=\min\Bigl\{\frac{\kappa}{8C_2},\ \bigl(2\max_j\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty\bigr)^{-1}\Bigr\},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon'\in(0,1]\ \text{with}\ K\varepsilon'^2+sL_M\varepsilon'\le\frac{s\kappa}{16},
\]
then $\rho\in(0,1]$ with $C_R\rho\le s\kappa/16$ and $\omega_{\mathrm P}(\rho)\le\kappa/16$, and
put $\varepsilon_A=s\kappa/32$, $t=s\kappa/16$ and $\theta=\varepsilon'/2$. The base point is
\[
 \zeta'=(1-\varepsilon')\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}+\varepsilon'\delta_0,\qquad
 \bar{\zeta'}=\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}+\varepsilon'(1-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}),\qquad
 \zeta'(\{0\})\ge\varepsilon'>\theta .
\]
It costs little, because the first variation in its direction vanishes. With
$h=1-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}=\bar{\delta_0}-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$, \eqref{eq:eq-firstvar}, \eqref{eq:eq-fubini},
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero} and Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle}\ref{lem:eq-obstacle-a} give
$DP(\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}})[h]=\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(0)-\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}=0$, so by \eqref{eq:eq-second}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-basecost}
 P_{\zeta'}\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+K\varepsilon'^2 .
\end{equation}
Since $\|\bar{\zeta'}-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}\|_{L^1}\le\varepsilon'$ and $\|\tilde g_j'\|_\infty\le1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-lawshift}
 \Bigl|\int\tilde g_j\,dL'_Q-\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{Q}\Bigr|\le L_M\varepsilon'
 \qquad\text{for every } Q\in[0,1] .
\end{equation}

Now let $m$ satisfy $q_m\in I_i$, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)$ and
$W_1(\mu_m,L^{\mathrm{P}}_{q_m})\ge\kappa$. By \eqref{eq:eq-net} there is $j$ with
$\int\tilde g_j\,d\mu_m\ge\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{q_m}+\kappa/2
\ge\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{Q_i}-\omega_{\mathrm P}(\rho)+\kappa/2$, and since
$\sum_k\tilde g_j(m_k)=N\int\tilde g_j\,d\mu_m$,
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{k=1}^N\tilde g_j(m_k)
 \ge N\Bigl[f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t+s\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{Q_i}-s\,\omega_{\mathrm P}(\rho)+\frac{s\kappa}2\Bigr].
\]
Compare with \eqref{eq:eq-perturbed} on $I_i$, bounded through \eqref{eq:eq-basecost} and
\eqref{eq:eq-lawshift}: the corresponding random variable $\mathcal T_{ij}$ satisfies
\[
 \mathcal T_{ij}\ge N\Bigl[\frac{s\kappa}2-t-s\,\omega_{\mathrm P}(\rho)-K\varepsilon'^2-sL_M\varepsilon'
 -C_2s^2-\varepsilon_A\Bigr]
 \ge N s\kappa\Bigl(\frac{16}{32}-\frac2{32}-\frac2{32}-\frac2{32}-\frac4{32}-\frac1{32}\Bigr)
 =\frac5{32}Ns\kappa ,
\]
using $C_2s^2\le s\kappa/8$. Markov's inequality, with $C_R\rho\le\frac2{32}s\kappa$, bounds the
probability of this event by $(N+1)e^{-\frac3{32}N\theta s\kappa}$. A union bound over the
finitely many pairs $(i,j)$ gives, for all large $N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-step2}
 \mathbb{P}^{*}\bigl(\exists m\in[-1,1]^N:\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t),\ W_1(\mu_m,L^{\mathrm{P}}_{q_m})\ge\kappa\bigr)
 \le e^{-c_2N},
\end{equation}
where $c_2:=\theta s\kappa/16=\varepsilon's\kappa/32\le t$.

\emph{Step 3: conclusion.} Let $c=\min\{c_1,c_2\}/2$. In each of Steps~1 and~2 the constant
$c_k$ does not exceed the threshold parameter $t$ of that step, so the event in
Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} at the threshold $N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c)$ is contained in the union of the events of
\eqref{eq:eq-step1} and \eqref{eq:eq-step2}. Its outer
probability is therefore at most $e^{-c_1N}+e^{-c_2N}\le2e^{-2cN}\le e^{-cN}$ for all large $N$.

\emph{Step 4: a fixed radius.} Let $Q\in[0,1]\setminusC_{\mathrm{P}}$ and apply the bound of Step~3 with
$\kappa=\operatorname{dist}(Q,C_{\mathrm{P}})$, which is positive because $C_{\mathrm{P}}$ is closed; call the resulting constant
$c(Q)$. If $\sup\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m):q_m=Q\}>N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c(Q))$, some $m$ with $q_m=Q$ has
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c(Q))$ and $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})=\kappa$, so this event has outer probability at
most $e^{-c(Q)N}$. It is measurable, since $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}-H_N$ is deterministic and the supremum is a
$1$-Lipschitz function of $H_N$ in the uniform norm. So for all large $N$,
$\sup\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m):q_m=Q\}\le N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c(Q))$ with probability at least $1-e^{-c(Q)N}$.
head: environment

label: rem:eq-checks
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:eq-checks}
\emph{Replica symmetry at high temperature.} Let $\xi''(1)<1$. For $\zeta=\delta_0$ the
coefficient is $1$, $\Phi_{\delta_0}(t,x)=\log\cosh x+\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi'(t))$, and $\tanh X_t$
is a martingale with $d\tanh X_t=\sqrt{\xi''}\operatorname{sech}^2X_t\,dB_t$. Hence
$\Gamma_{\delta_0}(t)=\int_0^t\xi''\mathbb{E}\operatorname{sech}^4X_r\,dr\le\xi'(t)\le\xi''(1)t<t$ for $t\in(0,1]$, so
$\mathcal{O}_{\delta_0}$ is strictly increasing on $[0,1]$. By \eqref{eq:loc-first-order} and
\eqref{eq:loc-moving-mass}, $P_\mu-P_{\delta_0}\ge\int\mathcal{O}_{\delta_0}\,d(\mu-\delta_0)\ge0$ for
every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, so $\delta_0$ is a Parisi measure, with $C_{\mathrm{P}}=\{0\}$ and
$L^{\mathrm{P}}_{0}=\delta_0$. Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} then says that, outside an event of outer probability at
most $e^{-cN}$, every $m$ with
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c)$ has $q_m<\kappa$, so that most of its coordinates are small, in agreement
with \eqref{eq:eq-tapzero}.

\emph{One step of replica symmetry breaking.} If $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=a\delta_0+(1-a)\delta_q$ with
$a\in(0,1)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle} gives $C_{\mathrm{P}}\supset\{0,q\}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero}
adds nothing. Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} localizes near $C_{\mathrm{P}}$, consistently with \eqref{eq:eq-tapzero}
at $0$ and, for $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, with \cite[Theorem~2]{CPS} at $q$.
head: environment
name: Two consistency checks

label: rem:eq-cps
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:eq-cps}
\emph{The representation theorems.} For $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, the TAP representation at equilibrium,
\cite[Theorem~2]{CPS} and \cite[Theorems~2, 3 and~5]{CPS2}, concerns radii $q\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$; at
every radius the maximum of the TAP functional on the sphere is at most the free energy up to
$o(N)$, with probability tending to one \cite[Section~5]{CPS}. Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} makes this
comparison strict off $C_{\mathrm{P}}\supset\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$: there the maximum is smaller by a linear amount,
with an exponential bound uniform over the cube. At massless contacts, radii in
$C_{\mathrm{P}}\setminus\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$, it does not decide whether the representation holds, although its field-law
clause applies there (Section~\ref{sec:open}). Section~\ref{sec:intro-results}
compares it with Subag's characterization for spherical models \cite[Theorems~5 and~10]{Sub24}.

\emph{An exact formula at every radius.} For $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and every radius $Q$,
\cite[Theorem~36]{CPS}, which Chen, Panchenko and Subag import from \cite[Theorem~5]{CP18},
gives an exact variational formula, over a
Lagrange multiplier $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ and a coefficient on $[0,Q]$, for the limit of the expected
maximum over $\{q_m=Q\}$ of the TAP functional with its order parameter frozen at $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$; this
maximum bounds that of $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ on the sphere from above. They use the formula at $\lambda=0$
with the coefficient $\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ on $[0,Q]$. Moving $\lambda$ away from $0$ changes the formula
at first order by $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(Q)-Q$ per unit of $\lambda$; moving the coefficient toward that
of $\delta_0$ changes it by $(1-\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}([0,Q)))(\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}-\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q))$, which is negative for
$Q\notinC_{\mathrm{P}}$ below $\max\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ by Lemmas~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle}\ref{lem:eq-obstacle-a}
and~\ref{lem:eq-zero}. With the Borell--TIS inequality, as in \cite[Section~5]{CPS}, and the
normalization shift of Section~\ref{sec:intro-setting}, this gives, for $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, the
fixed-radius clause of
Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} in a few lines at every radius with $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(Q)\ne Q$ and at every
$Q\notinC_{\mathrm{P}}$ below $\max\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$. Neither these first-order moves nor the field-law clause
alone reach the remaining radii off $C_{\mathrm{P}}$, those above $\max\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ with
$\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(Q)=Q$, if there are any: since $\int y^2\,\mu_m(dy)=q_m$,
$\int y^2\,L^{\mathrm{P}}_{q}(dy)=\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(q)$ and $y\mapsto y^2$ is $2$-Lipschitz on $[-1,1]$, that
clause gives only $|\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(q_m)-q_m|\le2W_1(\mu_m,L^{\mathrm{P}}_{q_m})<2\kappa$, which places
$q_m$ near the set where $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(q)=q$, that is, where $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}'$ vanishes. Excluding
stationary points of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$ that are not minima is the work of the glued comparison, through the
downward jump of Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-gap}, which at those radii goes from $1+\varepsilon$ to $1$.

\emph{The field law.} In our normalization $L^{\mathrm{P}}_{q}$ is the law that \cite[(1.29)]{CPS2},
recalling \cite[Chapter~4]{Pan13} and \cite{AJ19a,AJ19b}, attaches informally to ancestor states
at $q\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$. The field-law clause of Corollary~\ref{cor:eq} is a precise statement of this
kind for every $m$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-c)$, at any radius; it concerns empirical laws of TAP
near-maximizers, not the Gibbs spin distributions of \cite{AJ19b}.
head: environment
name: Relation to the TAP representation

title: Standing assumption
body_md:
Throughout, $\xi$ satisfies \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. Appendix~\ref{app:pde-toolbox} uses $\xi$ only through the
following facts on $[0,1]$, which hold because $\xi\not\equiv0$ has nonnegative coefficients:
$\xi'(0)=0$; $\xi''$ and $\xi'''$ are continuous and nonnegative; $\xi''>0$ on $(0,1]$; so $\xi'$ is
strictly increasing and $\xi''\le\xi''(1)$. Among the facts on the Parisi equation, only
Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-majorant} (Appendix~\ref{app:glued-approx}) assumes \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, since convexity
of $\xi$ on $[-1,1]$ enters only through Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison}, by way of
Slepian's lemma. In Appendices~\ref{app:var-constrained}--\ref{app:var-gap},
Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}, Remark~\ref{rem:var-level} and Proposition~\ref{prop:loc-gap} assume
\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, as Section~\ref{sec:loc} does. Appendix~\ref{app:pde-standing} assumes in addition that
$\xi\in\mathcal{C}$.
head: manual

label: lem:pde-class
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-class}
Let $c$ be a step coefficient on $[t_0,t_1)$ with values in $[0,G]$, let $\psi\in\mathcal T_G$ and
$W=W[c,\psi]$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-class-a} $W(t,\cdot)\in\mathcal T_G$ for every $t\in[t_0,t_1]$; in particular
 $|v|<1$ and $0\le\partial_yv\le G(1-v^2)\le G$. If $\psi''>0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, then $\partial_yv>0$.
\item\label{lem:pde-class-b} On each closed step $[\tau_{j-1},\tau_j]$, $W$ is of class $C^{1,2}$,
 with one-sided $t$-derivatives at the ends, and
 $\partial_tW+\frac{\xi''}2\bigl(\partial_{yy}W+c_j(\partial_yW)^2\bigr)=0$.
\item\label{lem:pde-class-c} On each open step $v$ is of class $C^{1,2}$ and
 $\partial_tv+\frac{\xi''}2\partial_{yy}v+\xi''c_j\,v\,\partial_yv=0$. Moreover, $v$ is continuous
 on $[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}$.
\item\label{lem:pde-class-d} $|W(t,y)-W(t,0)|\le|y|$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Class preservation and regularity

title: Proof
body_md:
Work on one step $[\tau_{j-1},\tau_j)$, write $c=c_j$, $\sigma=\sigma_j$ and
$\psi_j=W(\tau_j,\cdot)$, and assume $\psi_j\in\mathcal T_G$. This holds for $j=J$, and once (a)
is proved on the step it holds for $j-1$; so backward induction covers every step. Since
$|\psi_j'|<1$, we have $|\psi_j(z)-\psi_j(0)|\le|z|$.

\emph{The case $c>0$.} Let $p_s(z)=(2\pi s)^{-1/2}e^{-z^2/(2s)}$ and
\[
 \Theta(t,y)=\mathbb{E} e^{c\psi_j(y+\sigma(t)Z)}=\int e^{c\psi_j(z)}p_{\sigma(t)^2}(z-y)\,dz .
\]
The integrand is at most $e^{c(\psi_j(0)+|z|)}p_{\sigma(t)^2}(z-y)$, and $\sigma(t)>0$ for
$t<\tau_j$. So differentiation under the integral is legitimate on
$[\tau_{j-1},\tau_j)\times\mathbb{R}$: there $\Theta$ is positive, $C^1$ in $t$ and $C^\infty$ in $y$, and,
since $\partial_sp_s=\frac12\partial_{zz}p_s$ and $\frac{d}{dt}\sigma(t)^2=-\xi''(t)$, it solves
$\partial_t\Theta=-\frac{\xi''}2\partial_{yy}\Theta$. Hence $W=c^{-1}\log\Theta$ satisfies
$\partial_tW=-\frac{\xi''}2(\partial_{yy}W+c(\partial_yW)^2)$ on the half-open step.
Differentiating $\Theta(t,y)=\mathbb{E} e^{c\psi_j(y+\sigma Z)}$ in $y$ under the expectation, which is
legitimate because $\psi_j'$ and $\psi_j''$ are bounded and continuous, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pde-tilt}
 \partial_yW(t,y)=\mathbb{E}_{\mu}\psi_j'(y+\sigma\,\cdot),\qquad
 \partial_{yy}W(t,y)=\mathbb{E}_{\mu}\psi_j''(y+\sigma\,\cdot)+c\operatorname{Var}_{\mu}\psi_j'(y+\sigma\,\cdot),
\end{equation}
where $\mu=\mu_{t,y}$ is the probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ whose density with respect to the
standard Gaussian measure is proportional to $e^{c\psi_j(y+\sigma(t)z)}$.

\emph{Continuity at $t=\tau_j$.} This density equals
$e^{c(\psi_j(y+\sigma z)-\psi_j(y))}/\mathbb{E} e^{c(\psi_j(y+\sigma Z)-\psi_j(y))}$, whose numerator is at
most $e^{c\sigma|z|}$ and whose denominator is at least $\mathbb{E} e^{-c\sigma|Z|}\ge e^{-G}$ for
$\sigma\le1$; so these densities are uniformly integrable for $\sigma\le1$. Since
$\psi_j,\psi_j',\psi_j''$ are continuous and $\psi_j',\psi_j''$ are bounded, dominated convergence
gives $W\to\psi_j$, $\partial_yW\to\psi_j'$ and $\partial_{yy}W\to\psi_j''$ as
$(t,y')\to(\tau_j,y)$, locally uniformly in $y$. By the equation, $\partial_tW$ extends
continuously to $t=\tau_j$, and since $W(\tau_j,y)-W(t,y)=\int_t^{\tau_j}\partial_tW(s,y)\,ds$,
the left $t$-derivative at $\tau_j$ exists and equals this extension. This proves (b) when $c>0$.

\emph{The case $c=0$.} Then $W(t,y)=\mathbb{E}\psi_j(y+\sigma(t)Z)$ is a heat flow, and the same argument
without the tilt gives (b), with $\partial_tW=-\frac{\xi''}2\partial_{yy}W$; the formulas
\eqref{eq:pde-tilt} hold with $c=0$ and $\mu$ the standard Gaussian measure.

\emph{(c).} On the open step $W$ is $C^\infty$ in $y$, and the $t$-derivatives of its
$y$-derivatives are continuous (differentiate $\Theta$ under the integral). Differentiating the
equation in $y$ gives the equation for $v$. At $\tau_j$ the left limit of $v$ is
$\psi_j'=v(\tau_j,\cdot)$, which is the value used on the next step; so $v$ is continuous on
$[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}$.

\emph{(a).} By \eqref{eq:pde-tilt}, $\psi_j''\le G(1-\psi_j'^2)$, $c\le G$ and Jensen's inequality,
\[
 \partial_{yy}W\le G-(G-c)\mathbb{E}_\mu\psi_j'^2-c\,(\mathbb{E}_\mu\psi_j')^2
 \le G\bigl(1-(\mathbb{E}_\mu\psi_j')^2\bigr)=G\bigl(1-(\partial_yW)^2\bigr).
\]
Both terms of $\partial_{yy}W$ in \eqref{eq:pde-tilt} are nonnegative, and the first is positive
if $\psi_j''>0$. Finally $|\partial_yW|<1$, since it is a $\mu$-average of values of $\psi_j'$ in
$(-1,1)$. Hence $W(t,\cdot)\in\mathcal T_G$, and $\partial_{yy}W>0$ if $\psi_j''>0$.

\emph{(d)} follows from $|\partial_yW|<1$.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-ac
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-ac}
Let $c$, $\psi$, $W$ and $v$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}, let
$(t,y)\in[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}$, and let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion with filtration
$(\mathcal F_r)$. The equation
\begin{equation}\label{eq:pde-ac}
 dX_r=\xi''(r)c(r)v(r,X_r)\,dr+\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r,\qquad X_t=y,
\end{equation}
has a unique strong solution on $[t,t_1]$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-ac-a} For $r\in[t,t_1]$,
 \[
  v(r,X_r)=v(t,y)+\int_t^r\sqrt{\xi''(s)}\,\partial_yv(s,X_s)\,dB_s .
 \]
 In particular $v(r,X_r)=\mathbb{E}[\psi'(X_{t_1})\mid\mathcal F_r]$ and $v(t,y)=\mathbb{E}\psi'(X_{t_1})$.
\item\label{lem:pde-ac-b} \textup{(Verification.)} Let $u$ be a bounded progressively
 measurable process, and let $X^u$ solve $dX^u_r=\xi''(r)c(r)u_r\,dr+\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r$,
 $X^u_t=y$. Then
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:pde-verification}
  \mathbb{E}\psi(X^u_{t_1})=W(t,y)+\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_t^{t_1}\xi''c\,u_r^2\,dr
  -\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_t^{t_1}\xi''c\,\bigl(u_r-v(r,X^u_r)\bigr)^2\,dr .
 \end{equation}
 Hence $W(t,y)\ge\mathbb{E}\psi(X^u_{t_1})-\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_t^{t_1}\xi''c\,u_r^2\,dr$, with equality for
 $u_r=v(r,X_r)$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Auffinger--Chen process and verification

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a}, $c\le G$ and $\xi''\le\xi''(1)$, the drift in
\eqref{eq:pde-ac} is bounded and $G^2\xi''(1)$-Lipschitz in the space variable, so strong existence
and uniqueness are standard.

(a) On $[\tau_{j-1}+\epsilon',\tau_j-\epsilon]$ the function $v$ is $C^{1,2}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-c}), and It\^o's formula together with the equation
for $v$ gives $dv(r,X_r)=\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,\partial_yv(r,X_r)\,dB_r$: the drift terms cancel. Let
$\epsilon,\epsilon'\downarrow0$, using the continuity of $v$ and of the paths of $X$ and the bound
$|\partial_yv|\le G$, and chain over the steps. The stochastic integral is a bounded martingale,
and $v(t_1,\cdot)=\psi'$; this gives the conditional expectations.

(b) On each closed step, Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-b}, It\^o's formula and the
equation for $W$ give
\[
 dW(r,X^u_r)=\tfrac12\xi''(r)c(r)\bigl[u_r^2-\bigl(u_r-v(r,X^u_r)\bigr)^2\bigr]dr
 +\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,v(r,X^u_r)\,dB_r .
\]
The stochastic integral is a true martingale because $|v|<1$, and $\psi$ grows at most linearly
while $X^u_{t_1}$ has Gaussian tails. Taking expectations and summing over the steps gives
\eqref{eq:pde-verification}; the inequality follows from $c\ge0$.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-coef
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Coefficient sandwich

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-b} to the system with coefficient $c_2$, with the
control $u_r=v_1(r,X^1_r)$ and the Brownian motion that drives $X^1$. Then
$X^u_{t_1}=X^1_{t_1}+Y$ with $Y=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\xi''(c_2-c_1)u_r\,dr$, and convexity of
$\psi$ gives
\[
 W_2(t_0,y)\ge\mathbb{E}\psi(X^1_{t_1})+\mathbb{E}\bigl[\psi'(X^1_{t_1})Y\bigr]
 -\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\xi''c_2u_r^2\,dr .
\]
The equality case of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-b} for the first system gives
$W_1(t_0,y)=\mathbb{E}\psi(X^1_{t_1})-\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\xi''c_1u_r^2\,dr$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a} and Fubini's theorem,
$\mathbb{E}[\psi'(X^1_{t_1})u_r]=\mathbb{E} u_r^2=\Gamma_1(r)$, so
$\mathbb{E}[\psi'(X^1_{t_1})Y]=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\xi''(c_2-c_1)\Gamma_1\,dr$. Subtracting gives the left
inequality in \eqref{eq:pde-coef}; exchanging the two systems gives the right one. The last claim
follows from $0\le\Gamma_i\le1$ and $\xi''\le\xi''(1)$, applied on $[t,t_1]$ for every $t$.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-terminal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-terminal}
Let $c$ be a step coefficient on $[t_0,t_1)$ with values in $[0,G]$, let $\psi_1,\psi_2\in\mathcal T_G$,
$W_i=W[c,\psi_i]$, and let $X^i$ solve \eqref{eq:pde-ac} for $(c,\psi_i)$ from $(t_0,y)$. Then
\[
 \mathbb{E}[\psi_2-\psi_1](X^1_{t_1})\ \le\ W_2(t_0,y)-W_1(t_0,y)\ \le\ \mathbb{E}[\psi_2-\psi_1](X^2_{t_1}).
\]
In particular $\sup|W_2-W_1|\le\sup|\psi_2-\psi_1|$.
head: environment
name: Terminal sandwich

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-b} to the second system with the control
$u_r=v_1(r,X^1_r)$. The coefficient is the same, so $X^u=X^1$, and the equality case for the first
system gives the lower bound. Exchanging the systems gives the upper bound.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-stability}
For $i=1,2$ let $c_i$ be a step coefficient on $[t_0,t_1)$ with values in $[0,G]$, let
$\psi_i\in\mathcal T_G$, $W_i=W[c_i,\psi_i]$ and $v_i=\partial_yW_i$, and put $E_0=e^{G^2\xi'(1)}$.
Then
\[
 D:=\sup_{[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}}|v_1-v_2|
 \le e^{G^2E_0\xi'(1)}\bigl(\|\psi_1'-\psi_2'\|_\infty+GE_0\xi''(1)\|c_1-c_2\|_{L^1}\bigr),
\]
and the solutions $X^1,X^2$ of \eqref{eq:pde-ac} for $(c_i,\psi_i)$, started at a common point and
driven by the same Brownian motion, satisfy almost surely
\[
 \sup_r|X^1_r-X^2_r|\le E_0\bigl(\xi''(1)\|c_1-c_2\|_{L^1}+G\xi'(1)D\bigr).
\]
head: environment
name: Stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $D(t)=\sup_y|v_1-v_2|(t,y)$, which is lower semicontinuous, hence measurable, and let
$e(r)=|X^1_r-X^2_r|$ for solutions started at $(t,y)$. Since $|v_1|\le1$, $c_2\le G$ and
$|\partial_yv_2|\le G$,
\[
 |c_1v_1(r,X^1_r)-c_2v_2(r,X^2_r)|\le|c_1-c_2|(r)+G\,D(r)+G^2e(r).
\]
Hence $e(r)\le a+G^2\int_t^r\xi''e$ with $a=\int_t^{t_1}\xi''(|c_1-c_2|+GD)$, and Gronwall's lemma
with $\int_0^1\xi''=\xi'(1)$ gives $e\le E_0a$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a},
$v_i(t,y)=\mathbb{E}\psi_i'(X^i_{t_1})$, and $\psi_2'$ is $G$-Lipschitz, so
$|v_1-v_2|(t,y)\le\|\psi_1'-\psi_2'\|_\infty+G\,\mathbb{E} e(t_1)$. Therefore
$D(t)\le\|\psi_1'-\psi_2'\|_\infty+GE_0\int_t^{t_1}\xi''(|c_1-c_2|+GD)$, and the backward Gronwall
lemma gives the bound on $D$, since $\int\xi''|c_1-c_2|\le\xi''(1)\|c_1-c_2\|_{L^1}$. Inserting it
into $e\le E_0a$ gives the bound on the processes.
head: environment

label: cor:pde-step
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: The Parisi functional on step coefficients

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef} with $[t_0,t_1]=[0,1]$, $\psi=\log\cosh$ and $y=0$, minus the
linear terms of $P$. (b) follows from the left half of (a), which gives an affine minorant of $P$
touching it at $c_1$. (c) follows from (a) and $|\Gamma-t|\le1$. (d) is the paragraph on constants.
For (e), the right half of (a) gives
$P(c+\varepsilon h)-P(c)\le\varepsilon\,DP(c)[h]
+\frac\varepsilon2\int_0^1\xi''h\,(\Gamma_{c+\varepsilon h}-\Gamma_c)\,dt$, and by (d) the last term is
at most $\frac12\xi''(1)L_\Gamma\varepsilon^2\|h\|_{L^1}^2$.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-measurable
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-measurable}
Let $c\in\mathcal B_G$ and $\psi\in\mathcal T_G$, and let $c_k$ be step coefficients with values in
$[0,G]$ such that $\|c_k-c\|_{L^1}\to0$. Put $W_k=W[c_k,\psi]$ and $v_k=\partial_yW_k$.
\begin{romanlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-measurable-i} \textup{(Extension.)} $W_k$ and $v_k$ converge uniformly on
 $[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}$ to limits $W[c,\psi]$ and $v_c$ that do not depend on the sequence. The
 function $v_c$ is continuous, $v_c=\partial_yW[c,\psi]$, $|v_c|\le1$, and $v_c(t,\cdot)$ is
 nondecreasing and $G$-Lipschitz; it is $1$-Lipschitz if $c\le1$ and $\psi\in\mathcal T_1$. If
 $\psi$ is even, then $W[c,\psi](t,\cdot)$ is even, $v_c(t,\cdot)$ is odd and $v_c(t,0)=0$.
\item\label{lem:pde-measurable-ii} \textup{(Auffinger--Chen process.)} For
 $(t,y)\in[t_0,t_1]\times\mathbb{R}$ the equation
 $dX_r=\xi''(r)c(r)v_c(r,X_r)\,dr+\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r$, $X_t=y$, has a unique strong solution
 $X^c$, and the solutions $X^k$ for $c_k$, driven by the same Brownian motion, satisfy
 \[
  \sup_r|X^k_r-X^c_r|\le E_0\bigl(\xi''(1)\|c_k-c\|_{L^1}+G\xi'(1)\|v_k-v_c\|_\infty\bigr)\to0,
 \]
 uniformly in the sample point.
\item\label{lem:pde-measurable-iii} \textup{(Consequences.)} $v_k(r,X^k_r)\to v_c(r,X^c_r)$
 uniformly in $r$ and in the sample point. Hence $\Gamma_c(r):=\mathbb{E}\,v_c(r,X^c_r)^2$ is the uniform
 limit of $\Gamma_{c_k}$ and is continuous, and $\operatorname{Law}(v_c(r,X^c_r))$ is the $W_1$-limit of
 $\operatorname{Law}(v_k(r,X^k_r))$. When $[t_0,t_1)=[0,1)$, $\psi=\log\cosh$ and $(t,y)=(0,0)$, define $P(c)$,
 $\mathcal{O}_c$ and $DP(c)$ by \eqref{eq:pde-P}; then $P(c)=\lim_kP(c_k)$,
 $\mathcal{O}_c\in C^1([0,1])$ with $\mathcal{O}_c'(t)=-\frac12\xi''(t)(\Gamma_c(t)-t)$, and
 Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step} holds for coefficients in $\mathcal B_G$ (with $h$ measurable in
 \ref{cor:pde-step-e}).
\item\label{lem:pde-measurable-iv} \textup{(Identification.)} Let $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. Then
 $W[\bar{\zeta},\log\cosh]$ on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ is the solution $\Phi_\zeta$ of the Parisi equation in
 the sense of \cite[p.~7]{AC15a}, $v_{\bar{\zeta}}=\Phi_{\zeta,x}$, the process $X^{\bar{\zeta}}$ started
 at $(0,0)$ is the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta$, and
 \[
  P(\bar{\zeta})=P_\zeta,\qquad\Gamma_{\bar{\zeta}}=\Gamma_{\zeta},\qquad\mathcal{O}_{\bar{\zeta}}=\mathcal{O}_\zeta .
 \]
 For $Q\in[0,1)$ and $\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$, the same construction on $[Q,1]$ with the
 coefficient $\bar{\eta}(t)=\eta([Q,t])$ defines $\Phi_\eta=W[\bar{\eta},\log\cosh]$.
\end{romanlist}
head: environment
name: Measurable coefficients

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef}, $\sup|W_k-W_l|\le\frac12\xi''(1)\|c_k-c_l\|_{L^1}$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-stability} with $\psi_1=\psi_2$, $\sup|v_k-v_l|\le L_v\|c_k-c_l\|_{L^1}$. Both
sequences are therefore uniformly Cauchy, and interleaving two approximating sequences shows that
the limits do not depend on the sequence. The function $v_c$ is continuous as a uniform limit of
continuous functions (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-c}), and letting $k\to\infty$
in $W_k(t,y)-W_k(t,0)=\int_0^yv_k(t,z)\,dz$ gives $v_c=\partial_yW[c,\psi]$. Monotonicity, the
bound $|v_c|\le1$ and the Lipschitz constants pass to the limit from
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a}; for the $1$-Lipschitz clause choose the $c_k$ with
values in $[0,1]$, which does not change the limit. If $\psi$ is even, every $W_k(t,\cdot)$ is even,
because the Gaussian convolutions in \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} preserve evenness, and so is the
limit.

(ii) The drift is bounded, measurable in $r$ and $G^2\xi''(1)$-Lipschitz in the space variable by
(i), so the strong solution exists and is unique. With $e_k(r)=|X^k_r-X^c_r|$,
$|c_kv_k(r,X^k_r)-cv_c(r,X^c_r)|\le|c_k-c|(r)+G\|v_k-v_c\|_\infty+G^2e_k(r)$, and Gronwall's lemma
gives the bound.

(iii) $|v_k(r,X^k_r)-v_c(r,X^c_r)|\le\|v_k-v_c\|_\infty+G\,e_k(r)$, which tends to zero uniformly.
The statements on $\Gamma_c$ and on the laws follow, the latter because the $W_1$ distance of
two laws is at most the expected distance of a coupling. $P(c_k)\to P(c)$ by (i). Since $\Gamma_c$
is continuous, $\mathcal{O}_c\in C^1$. The quantities in Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}, namely $P(c)$,
$DP(c)[h]$, $\Gamma_c$ and the coupled variables $v_c(t,X^c_t)$, are continuous in $c$ (and $DP(c)[h]$
in $h$) for the $L^1$ distance, by (i) and (iii). Approximating $c$, $c_1$, $c_2$ and
$c+\varepsilon h$ by step coefficients with values in $[0,G]$, the statements of the corollary pass
from step coefficients to $\mathcal B_G$.

(iv) For finitely supported $\zeta$ the two definitions agree, by \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf}. For
general $\zeta$, Auffinger and Chen \cite[p.~7]{AC15a} define $\Phi_\zeta$ as the continuous
extension, in the supremum norm, of the map $\zeta\mapsto\Phi_\zeta$ from finitely supported
measures, with the distance $\int_0^1|\bar{\zeta}-\bar{\zeta'}|\,dt$; the Lipschitz property on which
this definition rests is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef}. Hence $\Phi_\zeta=W[\bar{\zeta},\log\cosh]$ by (i),
and $\Phi_{\zeta,x}=v_{\bar{\zeta}}$. By strong uniqueness, $X^{\bar{\zeta}}$ is the Auffinger--Chen
process of $\zeta$, and the three identities are the definitions of $P_\zeta$, $\Gamma_{\zeta}$ and
$\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ in Sections~\ref{sec:intro-setting}--\ref{sec:intro-structure}.

label: lem:pde-fenchel
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-fenchel}
Let $Q\in[0,1)$, let $\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ have a step distribution function, and put
$\Phi=\Phi_\eta(Q,\cdot)$. As in Section~\ref{sec:intro-setting}, let
$\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}}\{\Phi(y)-my\}$ for $m\in(-1,1)$, extended continuously to
$m=\pm1$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-fenchel-a} $\Phi\in\mathcal T_1$, and $\Phi'$ is a strictly increasing $C^1$
 bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $(-1,1)$ with $0<\Phi''\le1-\Phi'^2$.
\item\label{lem:pde-fenchel-b} Let $b$ be the inverse of $\Phi'$ and $h=-\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,\cdot)$.
 Then $h$ is $C^2$ on $(-1,1)$, with $h'(m)=b(m)\to\pm\infty$ as $m\to\pm1$ and
 $h''(m)=1/\Phi''(b(m))\ge1/(1-m^2)\ge1$.
\item\label{lem:pde-fenchel-c} Let $g_0\in C^2([-1,1])$ and $s\in\mathbb{R}$ with
 $|s|\,\|g_0''\|_\infty\le\frac12$, and put
 \[
  \Psi_s(z)=\sup_{|m|\le1}\bigl[zm+\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m)+s\,g_0(m)\bigr],\qquad z\in\mathbb{R} .
 \]
 The supremum is attained at a unique point $m^*_s(z)\in(-1,1)$, $\Psi_s'=m^*_s$,
 $\Psi_s''>0$, and $\Psi_s\in\mathcal T_2$. Moreover $\Psi_0=\Phi$ and $m^*_0=\Phi'$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Perturbed Fenchel terminal values

title: Proof
body_md:
(a) By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a} with $G=1$ (the coefficient $\bar{\eta}$ takes
values in $[0,1]$ and $\log\cosh''>0$), $\Phi\in\mathcal T_1$ and $\Phi''>0$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a}, $\Phi'(y)=\mathbb{E}\tanh(X_1)$ for the solution $X$ of
\eqref{eq:pde-ac} from $(Q,y)$, and $X_1\ge y-\xi'(1)+\int_Q^1\sqrt{\xi''}\,dB$; so $\Phi'(y)\to1$ as
$y\to\infty$, and $\Phi'(y)\to-1$ as $y\to-\infty$ in the same way.

(b) For $|m|<1$ the infimum defining $\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m)$ is attained at $y=b(m)$, by convexity, so
$h(m)=mb(m)-\Phi(b(m))$. Since $b$ is $C^1$ with $b'=1/\Phi''(b)$, differentiation gives
$h'=b$ and $h''=b'=1/\Phi''(b)$, and $\Phi''(b(m))\le1-\Phi'(b(m))^2=1-m^2$.

(c) Put $k=h-sg_0$. By (b), $k''(m)\ge(1-m^2)^{-1}-\frac12\ge\frac12$, and $k'(m)\to\pm\infty$ as
$m\to\pm1$ because $g_0'$ is bounded. So $k'$ is an increasing $C^1$ bijection of $(-1,1)$ onto
$\mathbb{R}$, and the strictly concave function $m\mapsto zm-k(m)$ has a unique maximizer
$m^*_s(z)=(k')^{-1}(z)$ in $(-1,1)$; it is strictly monotone on either side of $m^*_s(z)$, so the
continuous extension of $\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,\cdot)$ to $m=\pm1$ does not change the supremum. Hence
$\Psi_s(z)=zm^*_s(z)-k(m^*_s(z))$, and since $k'(m^*_s(z))=z$ and $m^*_s$ is $C^1$ with
$(m^*_s)'=1/k''(m^*_s)$, we get $\Psi_s'=m^*_s\in(-1,1)$ and $\Psi_s''=1/k''(m^*_s)>0$. The bound
$k''(m)\ge(1+m^2)/(2(1-m^2))$ gives
$\Psi_s''\le2(1-m_s^{*2})/(1+m_s^{*2})\le2(1-\Psi_s'^2)$, so $\Psi_s\in\mathcal T_2$. For $s=0$,
$m^*_0=(h')^{-1}=\Phi'$, and $b(m^*_0(z))=z$ gives
$\Psi_0(z)=zm^*_0(z)-h(m^*_0(z))=\Phi(z)$.

label: lem:var-dual
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:var-dual}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For every $\theta\in[0,1]$, $P$ attains its infimum over $\mathcal Z_\theta$. The
function $\overline{\Lambda}$ is convex and continuous on $[0,1]$, $\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}\le\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)\le\theta
P_{\delta_0}$ there, and
\[
 \overline{\Lambda}(1)=\lim_{\theta\uparrow1}\Lambda(\theta)=P_{\delta_0}=\frac{\xi(1)}2,\qquad
 \overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}},\qquad P_{\delta_0}\lef_1\le P_{\delta_0}+L_\xi .
\]
head: environment
name: The dual function

title: Proof
body_md:
Minimizers exist because $\mathcal Z_\theta$ is compact and $P$ is continuous by (V2). Since
$\delta_0\in\mathcal Z_\theta$ and $P\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}$, we have $\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}\le\Lambda(\theta)\le\theta
P_{\delta_0}$ for $\theta\in[0,1)$.

\emph{The endpoint $1$.} If $0<h\le1$ and $\mu\in\mathcal Z_{1-h}$, then $\bar{\mu}\ge1-h$, so
$d(\mu,\delta_0)=\int_0^1(1-\bar{\mu})\le h$ and $P_\mu\ge P_{\delta_0}-L_\xi h$ by (V2). Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-endpoint}
 (1-h)\bigl(P_{\delta_0}-L_\xi h\bigr)\le\Lambda(1-h)\le(1-h)P_{\delta_0},\qquad 0<h\le1,
\end{equation}
so $\Lambda(\theta)\to P_{\delta_0}$ as $\theta\uparrow1$, and $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=P_{\delta_0}$.

\emph{Convexity.} Let $\theta_1,\theta_2\in[0,1]$, $t\in(0,1)$ and $\theta=t\theta_1+(1-t)\theta_2$;
the cases $\theta=0$ and $\theta=1$ are trivial. Let $\zeta^{(i)}$ minimize $P$ over
$\mathcal Z_{\theta_i}$, so that $\theta_iP_{\zeta^{(i)}}=\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_i)$ (for $\theta_i=1$ this
is $\zeta^{(i)}=\delta_0$ and $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=P_{\delta_0}$). The probability measure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-mixture}
\begin{split}
 &\tilde\mu=\frac{t\theta_1\zeta^{(1)}+(1-t)\theta_2\zeta^{(2)}}{\theta}\quad\text{satisfies}\\
 &\tilde\mu(\{0\})\ge\frac{t\theta_1^2+(1-t)\theta_2^2}{\theta}
 =\theta+\frac{t(1-t)(\theta_1-\theta_2)^2}{\theta}\ge\theta,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
so $\tilde\mu\in\mathcal Z_\theta$, and convexity of $P$ with the weights $t\theta_1/\theta$ and
$(1-t)\theta_2/\theta$ gives
$\Lambda(\theta)\le\theta P_{\tilde\mu}\le t\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_1)+(1-t)\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_2)$.

\emph{Continuity and slopes.} The convex function $\overline{\Lambda}$ is continuous on $(0,1)$, at $1$
by~\eqref{eq:var-endpoint}, and at $0$ because $|\Lambda(\theta)|\le\theta\max|P|$. Let $\zeta'$
minimize $P$ over $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. For $s\in(0,1)$ the measure $(1-s)\zeta'+s\delta_0$ lies in
$\mathcal Z_s$ at distance at most $s$ from $\zeta'$, so $f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le p(s)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+L_\xi s$ and
$\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=\lim_{s\downarrow0}p(s)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The left derivative $f_1$ at $1$ is at least the
chord slope $\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\overline{\Lambda}(0)=P_{\delta_0}$, and it is the limit of the chord slopes
$(\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\Lambda(1-h))/h$, which are at most $P_{\delta_0}+L_\xi$
by~\eqref{eq:var-endpoint}.

\emph{The value $P_{\delta_0}$.} For $\zeta=\delta_0$ the coefficient $\zeta([0,t])$ equals one,
and $\Phi(t,x)=\log\cosh x+\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi'(t))$ solves the Parisi equation, because
$\Phi_{xx}+\Phi_x^2=1$. With $\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\,dt=\xi'(1)-\xi(1)$ this gives
$P_{\delta_0}=\frac12\xi'(1)-\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi(1))=\frac12\xi(1)$.
head: environment

label: lem:var-basic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:var-basic}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. Recall that $\theta_*=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})$, where $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ is the minimizer of $P$ over
$\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, unique by~\ref{lem:var-basic-a}.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:var-basic-a} For every $\theta\in[0,1]$, $P$ has exactly one minimizer
 $\zeta_\theta$ on $\mathcal Z_\theta$. In particular the Parisi measure $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\zeta_0$ is unique, and
 $\zeta_1=\delta_0$.
\item\label{lem:var-basic-b} If $\theta\le\theta_*$ and $\theta<1$, then $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ and
 $\Lambda(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$. If $\theta_*<\theta<1$, then $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta$.
\item\label{lem:var-basic-c} The functions $p$ and $\Lambda$ are continuously differentiable on
 $(0,1)$, with
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:var-pprime}
  p'(\theta)=\frac{\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}(0)-\int\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}\,d\zeta_\theta}{1-\theta},
  \qquad \Lambda'(\theta)=p(\theta)+\theta p'(\theta).
 \end{equation}
 The derivative $\Lambda'$ is nondecreasing, and it equals $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ on $(0,\theta_*]\cap(0,1)$.
\item\label{lem:var-basic-d} $\overline{\Lambda}$ is strictly convex on $[\theta_*,1]$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Constrained minimizers

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:var-basic-a} Existence is Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual}, and uniqueness follows from (V1)
because $\mathcal Z_\theta$ is convex.

\ref{lem:var-basic-b} If $\theta\le\theta_*$, then $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\in\mathcal Z_\theta$ minimizes $P$ over all
of $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, so $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ by uniqueness, and $p(\theta)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Let
$\theta_*<\theta<1$ and suppose that $a=\zeta_\theta(\{0\})>\theta$. For $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$
and $0<s\le1-\theta/a$, the measure $(1-s)\zeta_\theta+s\mu$ has mass at least $(1-s)a\ge\theta$
at $0$, so it lies in $\mathcal Z_\theta$, and minimality and convexity give
$P_{\zeta_\theta}\le(1-s)P_{\zeta_\theta}+sP_\mu$, that is, $P_{\zeta_\theta}\le P_\mu$. So
$\zeta_\theta$ minimizes $P$ over $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, hence $\zeta_\theta=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$; but
$\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})=\theta_*<\theta<\zeta_\theta(\{0\})$, a contradiction.

\ref{lem:var-basic-c} Fix $\theta\in[0,1)$ and let $D_\theta$ denote the right side of the first
identity in~\eqref{eq:var-pprime}. For $\theta'\in[0,1)$ put $\lambda=(\theta'-\theta)/(1-\theta)$
and consider
\[
 \zeta_\theta+\lambda(\delta_0-\zeta_\theta)
 =\theta'\delta_0+\frac{1-\theta'}{1-\theta}\bigl(\zeta_\theta-\theta\delta_0\bigr).
\]
Since $\zeta_\theta(\{0\})\ge\theta$, the right side is a probability measure with mass at least
$\theta'$ at the origin, so it lies in $\mathcal Z_{\theta'}$. Its distribution function differs from
$\bar{\zeta_\theta}$ by $\lambda(1-\bar{\zeta_\theta})$, and
$\int_0^1(1-\bar{\zeta_\theta})\le1-\zeta_\theta(\{0\})\le1-\theta$, so its distance from
$\zeta_\theta$ is at most $|\theta'-\theta|$; and $\lambda\int\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_\theta}\,d(\delta_0-\zeta_\theta)
=(\theta'-\theta)D_\theta$. Comparing $p(\theta')$ with the value of $P$ at this measure and
applying~\eqref{eq:var-quadratic} at $\mu=\zeta_\theta$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-semiconcave}
 p(\theta')\le p(\theta)+(\theta'-\theta)D_\theta+C_\xi(\theta'-\theta)^2,
 \qquad \theta,\theta'\in[0,1).
\end{equation}
Now let $\theta\in(0,1)$. The convex function $\Lambda$ has one-sided derivatives
$\Lambda'_-(\theta)\le\Lambda'_+(\theta)$, so $p=\Lambda/\theta$ has one-sided derivatives
$p'_\pm(\theta)=(\Lambda'_\pm(\theta)-p(\theta))/\theta$ with $p'_-(\theta)\le p'_+(\theta)$.
Taking $\theta'=\theta\pm h$ in~\eqref{eq:var-semiconcave} and letting $h\downarrow0$ gives
$p'_+(\theta)\le D_\theta\le p'_-(\theta)$. Hence $p$ is differentiable at $\theta$ with
$p'(\theta)=D_\theta$, and so is $\Lambda=\theta p$, with $\Lambda'=p+\theta p'$. The derivative
of the convex function $\Lambda$ is nondecreasing, and as a derivative it has the intermediate
value property, so it has no jumps: $\Lambda\in C^1(0,1)$, and then $p=\Lambda/\theta$ is
$C^1$ as well. By~\ref{lem:var-basic-b}, $\Lambda(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ on $[0,\theta_*]\cap[0,1)$,
so $\Lambda'=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ on $(0,\theta_*)$ and, by continuity, at $\theta_*$ if $\theta_*<1$.

\ref{lem:var-basic-d} Let $\theta_*\le\theta_1<\theta_2\le1$, $t\in(0,1)$ and
$\theta=t\theta_1+(1-t)\theta_2\in(\theta_*,1)$. Form $\tilde\mu$ from $\zeta_{\theta_1}$ and
$\zeta_{\theta_2}$ as in~\eqref{eq:var-mixture}. Since $\theta_1\ne\theta_2$,
\eqref{eq:var-mixture} and~\ref{lem:var-basic-b} give
$\tilde\mu(\{0\})>\theta=\zeta_\theta(\{0\})$, so $\tilde\mu\in\mathcal Z_\theta$ and
$\tilde\mu\ne\zeta_\theta$. Uniqueness of the minimizer gives $p(\theta)<P_{\tilde\mu}$, and convexity of $P$ gives
$\Lambda(\theta)<\theta P_{\tilde\mu}\le t\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_1)+(1-t)\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_2)$.
head: environment

label: prop:var-regular
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:var-regular}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:var-regular-a} If $\theta_*=1$, then $\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ on $[0,1]$ and
 $f_1=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. If $\theta_*<1$, then $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_*)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_1$, and $\Lambda'$ is a
 strictly increasing homeomorphism of $(\theta_*,1)$ onto $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.
\item\label{prop:var-regular-b} Every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ is regular, and its dual minimizer is
 $\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)\in(\theta_*,1)$. In particular $\Lambda'(\theta_f)=f$ and
 $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta_f)-\theta_f f$.
\item\label{prop:var-regular-c} The function $\Sigma$ is finite, concave, nonincreasing and
 $1$-Lipschitz on $\mathbb{R}$. It vanishes on $(-\infty,f_{\mathrm{eq}}]$, is strictly decreasing on
 $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$, and equals $\xi(1)/2-f$ for $f\gef_1$. It is continuously differentiable on
 $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ with $\Sigma'(f)=-\theta_f$, and strictly concave on $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1]$.
\item\label{prop:var-regular-d} The right derivative of $\Sigma$ at $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ equals $-\theta_*$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Every level is regular

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{prop:var-regular-a} If $\theta_*=1$, then $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\delta_0$, so $f_{\mathrm{eq}}=P_{\delta_0}=\overline{\Lambda}(1)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual}, and with Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-b},
$\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ on $[0,1]$; hence $f_1=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Let $\theta_*<1$. If $\theta_*=0$,
then $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual}; if $0<\theta_*<1$, then
$\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_*)=\Lambda'(\theta_*)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-c}. Let
$\theta_m=(1+\theta_*)/2$ be the midpoint of $[\theta_*,1]$. Convexity and the strict convexity of
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-d} give
\[
 f_{\mathrm{eq}}=\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_*)\le\frac{\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_m)-\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_*)}{\theta_m-\theta_*}
 <\frac{\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\overline{\Lambda}(\theta_m)}{1-\theta_m}\le\overline{\Lambda}'_-(1)=f_1 .
\]
On $(\theta_*,1)$ the derivative $\Lambda'$ is continuous and strictly increasing, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-c}--\ref{lem:var-basic-d}. Its limit $L_0$ at
$\theta_*+$ is at least $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_*)$; and for small $h>0$ the mean value theorem, together
with the continuity of $\overline{\Lambda}$ at $\theta_*$, writes the chord slope of $\overline{\Lambda}$ on
$[\theta_*,\theta_*+h]$ as a value of $\Lambda'$ in $(\theta_*,\theta_*+h)$, hence at least $L_0$. Letting
$h\downarrow0$ gives $L_0\le\overline{\Lambda}'_+(\theta_*)$, so $L_0=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. In the same way
$\Lambda'(\theta)\le(\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\overline{\Lambda}(\theta))/(1-\theta)\lef_1$ for $\theta<1$, and the mean
value theorem on $[1-h,1]$, with the continuity of $\overline{\Lambda}$ at $1$, shows that the limit of
$\Lambda'$ at $1-$ is $f_1$. So $\Lambda'$ maps $(\theta_*,1)$ onto $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.

\ref{prop:var-regular-b} Let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, so $\theta_*<1$, and put
$G_f(\theta)=\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$, a convex continuous function on $[0,1]$. By~\ref{prop:var-regular-a},
$\theta_f=(\Lambda')^{-1}(f)\in(\theta_*,1)$ is an interior critical point of $G_f$, hence a minimizer.
For $0\le\theta<\theta_*$, Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-b} gives
$G_f(\theta)=\theta(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)>\theta_*(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)=G_f(\theta_*)\ge G_f(\theta_f)$. On $[\theta_*,1]$ the
function $G_f$ is strictly convex, so it has at most one minimizer there. Hence $\theta_f$ is the
unique minimizer.

\ref{prop:var-regular-c} As an infimum over $\theta\in[0,1]$ of affine functions of $f$ with slopes
$-\theta\in[-1,0]$, $\Sigma$ is concave, nonincreasing and $1$-Lipschitz once it is finite; and
$0=\overline{\Lambda}(0)\ge\Sigma(f)\ge\min_{[0,1]}\overline{\Lambda}-\max\{0,f\}$. If $f\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}$, then
$\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f\ge\theta(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)\ge0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual}, with equality at
$\theta=0$, so $\Sigma(f)=0$. If $f\gef_1$, then the supporting line
$\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)\ge\overline{\Lambda}(1)+f_1(\theta-1)$ gives
$\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f\ge\overline{\Lambda}(1)-f+(1-\theta)(f-f_1)\ge\overline{\Lambda}(1)-f$, with equality at
$\theta=1$, so $\Sigma(f)=\overline{\Lambda}(1)-f=\xi(1)/2-f$. For $f,f+h\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$,
\[
 \Sigma(f+h)\le G_{f+h}(\theta_f)=\Sigma(f)-h\theta_f,\qquad
 \Sigma(f)\le G_f(\theta_{f+h})=\Sigma(f+h)+h\theta_{f+h},
\]
and $f\mapsto\theta_f$ is continuous by~\ref{prop:var-regular-a}; hence $\Sigma'(f)=-\theta_f$. This
derivative is continuous, negative and strictly decreasing on $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, so $\Sigma$ is
strictly decreasing and strictly concave there. Since $\Sigma$ is continuous, it is strictly
decreasing on $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1]$, and strictly concave there as well: if it were affine on a chord of
$[f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1]$, $\Sigma'$ would be constant on a nondegenerate subinterval of $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. With
the slope $-1$ on $[f_1,\infty)$, $\Sigma$ is strictly decreasing on $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$.

\ref{prop:var-regular-d} If $\theta_*=1$, then $\Sigma(f)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f$ for $f\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}=f_1$ by~\ref{prop:var-regular-c}, and the
right derivative is $-1$. If $\theta_*<1$, then $\theta_f\downarrow\theta_*$ as $f\downarrowf_{\mathrm{eq}}$
by~\ref{prop:var-regular-a}, and the mean value theorem writes
$(\Sigma(f)-\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}))/(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})$ as $-\theta_{f'}$ for some $f'\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f)$; this tends to
$-\theta_*$.

head: environment
name: The rate at the equilibrium level

title: Proof
body_md:
The arguments follow \cite[Lemma~3.2]{Bou26b}
and its proof, except for the uniqueness of $\theta_f$. We give them in full because under
\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ they rest only on the calculus of Appendix~\ref{app:pde-toolbox}, which provides the
convexity of $P$, the inequalities \eqref{eq:loc-first-order} and~\eqref{eq:loc-second-order},
and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta\in C^1([0,1])$ with $\mathcal{O}_\zeta'=-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma_{\zeta}-t)$ and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta(1)=0$
(Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step} and Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}). We use neither the strict
convexity of $P$ nor the uniqueness of the constrained minimizer. Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and fix $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.

\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-a} The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual} uses only the convexity of $P$
and (V2), so it applies: $\overline{\Lambda}$ is convex and continuous on $[0,1]$, in particular lower
semicontinuous, $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and $f_1=\overline{\Lambda}'_-(1)$ is finite. The convex continuous
function $G_f(\theta)=\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$ has right derivative $f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f<0$ at $0$ and left
derivative $f_1-f>0$ at $1$, so its minimizers form a nonempty compact subset of $(0,1)$, on
which $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$. Uniqueness is proved after~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-b}.

\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-b} Let $\theta$ be any minimizer of $G_f$. By compactness and continuity,
$P$ attains its infimum over $\mathcal Z_\theta$; let $\zeta$ be any minimizer. Suppose that
$\theta'=\zeta(\{0\})>\theta$. For $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $0<\lambda\le1-\theta/\theta'$,
the measure $(1-\lambda)\zeta+\lambda\mu$ lies in $\mathcal Z_\theta$, so minimality and convexity
give $P_\zeta\le P_\mu$. Thus $P_\zeta=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and for $s\in[\theta,\theta']\cap[0,1)$ the measure
$\zeta$ is admissible at $s$, so $\Lambda(s)=sf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $G_f(s)=s(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)$, which is strictly
decreasing in $s$ because $f>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. This contradicts the minimality of $\theta$. Hence
$\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$, and $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f=\theta(P_\zeta-f)$.

\emph{Uniqueness of $\theta_f$.} Suppose that $\theta_1<\theta_2$ both minimize $G_f$. By convexity
$G_f$ is constant on $[\theta_1,\theta_2]$, so $\bar\theta=(\theta_1+\theta_2)/2$ is a minimizer
and $\Lambda(\bar\theta)=\frac12(\Lambda(\theta_1)+\Lambda(\theta_2))$. Let $\zeta_i$ minimize $P$
over $\mathcal Z_{\theta_i}$; by the saturation just proved, $\zeta_i(\{0\})=\theta_i$. The
probability measure $\tilde\mu=(\theta_1\zeta_1+\theta_2\zeta_2)/(2\bar\theta)$ has
$\tilde\mu(\{0\})=(\theta_1^2+\theta_2^2)/(2\bar\theta)>\bar\theta$, and by convexity
$\bar\theta P_{\tilde\mu}\le\frac12(\theta_1P_{\zeta_1}+\theta_2P_{\zeta_2})=\Lambda(\bar\theta)$.
So $\tilde\mu$ minimizes $P$ over $\mathcal Z_{\bar\theta}$ at the minimizer $\bar\theta$ of $G_f$, while
$\tilde\mu(\{0\})>\bar\theta$, which contradicts saturation. Hence the minimizer $\theta_f$ is unique.

\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c} Let $\theta=\theta_f$, let $\zeta=\zeta_f$ be a minimizer of $P$ over
$\mathcal Z_\theta$, and write $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ and $o=\inf_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}$. The regularity of $\mathcal{O}$
was recalled above.

\emph{First-order condition.} For $\zeta'\in\mathcal Z_\theta$ and $\lambda\in(0,1]$ the measure
$(1-\lambda)\zeta+\lambda\zeta'$ lies in $\mathcal Z_\theta$, and its distribution function is
$\bar{\zeta}+\lambda(\bar{\zeta'}-\bar{\zeta})$, with $\|\bar{\zeta'}-\bar{\zeta}\|_{L^1}\le1$. By
minimality, \eqref{eq:loc-second-order} and~\eqref{eq:loc-moving-mass},
$0\le\lambda\int\mathcal{O}\,d(\zeta'-\zeta)+K\lambda^2$, and letting $\lambda\downarrow0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-first-order}
 \int\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta'\ge\int\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta\qquad\text{for every }\zeta'\in\mathcal Z_\theta .
\end{equation}
With $\zeta'=\theta\delta_0+(1-\theta)\delta_t$, $t\in(0,1]$, and $\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$, this reads
$(1-\theta)\mathcal{O}(t)\ge\int_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta$. Taking the infimum over $t$,
$o\ge(1-\theta)^{-1}\int_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta\ge o$, because $\zeta((0,1])=1-\theta$. Hence
$\mathcal{O}=o$ $\zeta$-almost everywhere on $(0,1]$, and by continuity on $\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$; also
$\mathcal{O}(0)\ge o$ by continuity.

\emph{The strict inequality at the origin.} Suppose that $\mathcal{O}(0)=o$. Then $\mathcal{O}\ge o$ on
$[0,1]$ and $\int\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta=\theta\mathcal{O}(0)+(1-\theta)o=o$, so $\int\mathcal{O}\,d(\mu-\zeta)\ge0$ for
every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, and~\eqref{eq:loc-first-order} with~\eqref{eq:loc-moving-mass}
gives $P_\mu\ge P_\zeta$. Thus $P_\zeta=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $\Lambda(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$. For $s\in(\theta,1)$,
the measure
\[
 \zeta_s=\frac{s-\theta}{1-\theta}\,\delta_0+\frac{1-s}{1-\theta}\,\zeta
\]
has mass exactly $s$ at the origin, and
$\bar{\zeta_s}=\bar{\zeta}+\frac{s-\theta}{1-\theta}(1-\bar{\zeta})$. Since
$\int\mathcal{O}\,d(\delta_0-\zeta)=\mathcal{O}(0)-o=0$, \eqref{eq:loc-second-order}
and~\eqref{eq:loc-moving-mass} give $P_{\zeta_s}\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+K(s-\theta)^2/(1-\theta)^2$, and therefore
\[
 G_f(s)\le sf_{\mathrm{eq}}-sf+sK\frac{(s-\theta)^2}{(1-\theta)^2}
 =G_f(\theta)+(s-\theta)(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f)+O\bigl((s-\theta)^2\bigr)<G_f(\theta)
\]
for $s-\theta>0$ small, because $f>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. This contradicts the minimality of $\theta$. Hence
$\mathcal{O}(0)>o$.

\emph{The contact set.} The continuous function $\mathcal{O}$ attains its minimum over $[0,1]$, and not at
$0$, because $\mathcal{O}(0)>o$; so $o$ is attained in $(0,1]$, that is, $o=\mathcal{O}_{\min}$. Next,
$\Gamma_{\zeta}(1)=\mathbb{E}\tanh^2(X_1)<1$, so $\mathcal{O}'(1)=\frac12\xi''(1)(1-\Gamma_{\zeta}(1))>0$; since $\mathcal{O}(1)=0$,
$\mathcal{O}<0$ just below $1$, and $\mathcal{O}_{\min}<0=\mathcal{O}(1)$. Therefore
$C_f=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}=\{t\in[0,1]:\mathcal{O}(t)=\mathcal{O}_{\min}\}$ (as $\mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$) is a nonempty compact
subset of $(0,1)$, and it contains $\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$.

label: rem:var-level
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:var-level}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}, $\zeta_f(\{0\})=\theta_f$ and
$\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ on $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_f\cap(0,1]$, so $\int\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta_f=\theta_f\mathcal{O}(0)+(1-\theta_f)\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ and the right
side of~\eqref{eq:var-pprime} at $\theta=\theta_f$ equals $\mathcal{O}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}$. Since $\Lambda'(\theta_f)=f$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-c} gives
\[
 f=P_{\zeta_f}+\theta_f\bigl(\mathcal{O}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}\bigr),\qquad
 \Sigma(f)=\theta_f\bigl(P_{\zeta_f}-f\bigr)=-\theta_f^2\bigl(\mathcal{O}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}\bigr).
\]
So the strict inequality $\mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}
is equivalent to $\Sigma(f)<0$, and the height of the obstacle at the origin above its minimum,
together with $\theta_f$, determines the rate.
head: environment
name: The level and the height of the obstacle at the origin

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q\in[0,1)\setminusC_f$ and assume that $C_f$ has no point in $[0,Q)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}, $C_f$ is a nonempty subset of $(0,1)$, so it
contains a point $r\in(Q,1)$. Put $d=\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}$, which is positive because $Q\notinC_f$ when
$Q>0$, and because $\mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ when $Q=0$.

\emph{The data.} For $0<\varepsilon\le\theta$ let $\mathsf{x}=\bar{\zeta}|_{[0,Q)}$ (there is no cascade
coefficient if $Q=0$) and
\[
 \eta_\varepsilon=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta-\varepsilon\delta_Q+\varepsilon\delta_r .
\]
The measure $\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta$ has an atom of mass $\zeta([0,Q])\ge\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta\ge\varepsilon$
at $Q$, so $\eta_\varepsilon$ is a probability measure on $[Q,1]$; only the constraint
$\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta$ is used here, not the saturation of Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}. The cascade
coefficient $\mathsf{x}$ is nondecreasing with values in $[\theta,1]$, so $(\mathsf{x},\eta_\varepsilon)\in
\mathcal A_Q$ (for $Q=0$, $\eta_\varepsilon=\zeta-\varepsilon\delta_0+\varepsilon\delta_r\in
\mathcal{P}([0,1])=\mathcal A_0$). The distribution function of $\eta_\varepsilon$ on $[Q,1]$ is
$\bar{\zeta}-\varepsilon\mathbf{1}_{[Q,r)}$, so
\[
 \mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta_\varepsilon)=\bar{\zeta}+\varepsilon h,\qquad h=-\mathbf{1}_{[Q,r)},\qquad
 \|h\|_{L^1}=r-Q\le1,
\]
and $\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta_\varepsilon)\ge\theta-\varepsilon\ge0$ on $[Q,r)$, so it is a coefficient. If
$Q>0$, the measure $\zeta$ has no atom at $Q\notinC_f\supset\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$, so the glued
coefficient jumps down by $\varepsilon$ at $Q$, as Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-monotone} requires of any gain.

\emph{The gain.} The first variation is
\[
 DP(\bar{\zeta})[h]=-\int_0^1h\,\mathcal{O}'\,dt=\int_Q^r\mathcal{O}'(t)\,dt=\mathcal{O}(r)-\mathcal{O}(Q)=-d,
\]
and~\eqref{eq:loc-second-order} gives $P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta_\varepsilon))\le
P_\zeta-\varepsilon d+K\varepsilon^2$. If $d\le2K\theta$, the choice $\varepsilon=d/(2K)\le\theta$
gives the gain $d^2/(4K)$. Otherwise take $\varepsilon=\theta$; then $K\theta<d/2$ and the gain
is at least $\theta d-K\theta^2\ge\theta d/2$. In both cases
$P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta_\varepsilon))\le P_\zeta-\varphi(d)$, with $\varphi$ as
in~\eqref{eq:loc-gap-function}.
head: environment

label: lem:pde-standing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pde-standing}
Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and let $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-standing-a} \textup{(Derivative bounds.)} For every $j\ge0$, $\partial_x^j\Phi$
 exists and is continuous on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$, and for all $(t,b)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$,
 \[
  \underline c\,e^{-2|b|}\le\Phi_{xx}(t,b)\le\overline C\,e^{-2|b|},\qquad
  |\Phi_{xxx}(t,b)|+|\Phi_{xxxx}(t,b)|\le C_{34}\,\Phi_{xx}(t,b).
 \]
\item\label{lem:pde-standing-b} \textup{(Inverse field.)} For every $t\in[0,1]$, $\Phi_x(t,\cdot)$ is
 an odd, strictly increasing bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $(-1,1)$. Its inverse $b_\alpha(t,m)$ is jointly
 continuous on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$, and
 \[
  |b_\alpha(t,m)|\le\tfrac12\log(\overline C/2)+\tfrac12\log\frac1{1-|m|}.
 \]
 The function $u_\alpha(t,m)=\Phi_{xx}(t,b_\alpha(t,m))$, extended by $u_\alpha(t,\pm1)=0$, is
 jointly continuous on $[0,1]\times[-1,1]$, and $0\le u_\alpha(t,m)\le(2\overline C/\underline c)(1-|m|)$.
\item\label{lem:pde-standing-c} \textup{(Obstacle.)} $M_t=\int_0^t\sqrt{\xi''(s)}\,U_s\,dB_s$, the
 function $\Gamma_{\alpha}$ is in $C^1([0,1])$ with $\Gamma_{\alpha}'=\xi''\,\mathbb{E} U_t^2$, and
 $\mathcal{O}_\alpha\in C^2([0,1])$ with
 \[
  \mathcal{O}_\alpha'(t)=-\tfrac12\xi''(t)\bigl(\Gamma_{\alpha}(t)-t\bigr),\qquad
  \mathcal{O}_\alpha''(t)=-\tfrac12\xi'''(t)\bigl(\Gamma_{\alpha}(t)-t\bigr)-\tfrac12\xi''(t)\bigl(\Gamma_{\alpha}'(t)-1\bigr).
 \]
 Every $Q\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\alpha$ lies in $(0,1)$ and satisfies $\Gamma_{\alpha}(Q)=Q$ and
 $\mathcal{O}_\alpha''(Q)=\frac12\xi''(Q)\bigl(1-\xi''(Q)\mathbb{E} U_Q^2\bigr)\ge0$. In particular, for
 $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ and $\alpha=\zeta_f$, one has $\Delta=2\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''/\xi''\ge0$ on $C_f$.
\item\label{lem:pde-standing-d} \textup{(Field laws.)} The maps $t\mapsto\operatorname{Law}(M_t)$ and
 $t\mapsto\operatorname{Law}(U_t)$ are $W_1$-continuous on $[0,1]$, and $u_\alpha(t,\cdot)$ pushes $\operatorname{Law}(M_t)$
 forward to $\operatorname{Law}(U_t)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$.
\end{thmlist}
The constants $\underline c$, $\overline C$ and $C_{34}$ depend only on $\xi'(1)$; the bounds in
(a)--(b) are uniform in $\alpha$ and $t$.
head: environment
name: Regularity at the contact set

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $a_t=\xi''(t)$.

\emph{(a), finitely supported $\alpha$.} Then $\bar{\alpha}$ is a step coefficient with values in
$[0,1]$, and $\Phi$ is given by \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf}. On each step of $\bar{\alpha}$,
differentiating \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} under the Gaussian expectation shows that $\Phi$ is
$C^\infty$ in $x$ with $\partial_x^j\Phi$ bounded for $j\ge1$ (all derivatives of $\log\cosh$ of
order at least one are bounded, and the derivatives produced by \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} are
polynomials in tilted moments of the derivatives of the terminal value), and that
$\partial_t\partial_x^j\Phi$ is obtained by differentiating the Parisi equation; by dominated
convergence, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-b}, these functions
extend continuously to the closed step. Put $L=\frac12a\,\partial_{xx}+a\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_x\partial_x$.
Differentiating $\partial_t\Phi+\frac12a(\Phi_{xx}+\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_x^2)=0$ in $x$ once, twice, three
and four times gives, on each step,
\begin{gather*}
 (\partial_t+L)\Phi_x=0,\qquad(\partial_t+L)\Phi_{xx}+a\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_{xx}^2=0,\qquad
 (\partial_t+L)\Phi_{xxx}+3a\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_{xx}\Phi_{xxx}=0,\\
 (\partial_t+L)\Phi_{xxxx}+4a\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_{xx}\Phi_{xxxx}+3a\bar{\alpha}\,\Phi_{xxx}^2=0 .
\end{gather*}
Let $\tilde X$ be the Auffinger--Chen process of $\alpha$ started at $(t,b)$, whose generator is $L$, and
let $I_{ts}=\int_t^sa_r\bar{\alpha}(r)\Phi_{xx}(r,\tilde X_r)\,dr$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a} with $G=1$, $0<\Phi_{xx}\le1$, so
$0\le I_{ts}\le\int_0^1a=V_*$. It\^o's formula on each step, chained over the steps as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a}, gives the Feynman--Kac formulas
\begin{gather*}
 \Phi_x(t,b)=\mathbb{E}\tanh(\tilde X_1),\qquad
 \Phi_{xx}(t,b)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Phi_{xx}(s,\tilde X_s)e^{I_{ts}}\bigr]\quad(t\le s\le1),\\
 \Phi_{xxx}(t,b)=-2\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\tanh(\tilde X_1)e^{3I_{t1}}\bigr],\\
 \Phi_{xxxx}(t,b)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[z(\tilde X_1)e^{4I_{t1}}\bigr]
 +3\,\mathbb{E}\int_t^1a_s\bar{\alpha}(s)\Phi_{xxx}(s,\tilde X_s)^2e^{4I_{ts}}\,ds,
\end{gather*}
where $z(y)=4\operatorname{sech}^2y\tanh^2y-2\operatorname{sech}^4y$ is the third derivative of $\tanh$.
Write $\tilde X_1=b+D+J$ with $D=\int_t^1a_s\bar{\alpha}(s)\Phi_x(s,\tilde X_s)\,ds$ and $J=\int_t^1\sqrt{a_s}\,dB_s$;
then $|D|\le V_*$, and $J$ is centred Gaussian with variance $\xi'(1)-\xi'(t)\le V_*$. We use
$e^{-2|y|}\le\operatorname{sech}^2y\le4e^{-2|y|}$ and $|b|-|D|-|J|\le|\tilde X_1|\le|b|+|D|+|J|$. Since $I\ge0$, Jensen's
inequality and $\mathbb{E}|J|\le\sqrt{V_*}$ give
\[
 \Phi_{xx}(t,b)\ge\mathbb{E}\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\ge e^{-2|b|-2V_*}\,\mathbb{E} e^{-2|J|}\ge\underline c\,e^{-2|b|},
\]
and since $\mathbb{E} e^{2|J|}\le2\mathbb{E} e^{2J}\le2e^{2V_*}$,
\[
 \Phi_{xx}(t,b)\le e^{V_*}\mathbb{E}\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\le4e^{3V_*}e^{-2|b|}\,\mathbb{E} e^{2|J|}\le\overline C\,e^{-2|b|}.
\]
Next, $e^{3I_{t1}}\le e^{2V_*}e^{I_{t1}}$ gives
$|\Phi_{xxx}(t,b)|\le2e^{2V_*}\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)e^{I_{t1}}]=2e^{2V_*}\Phi_{xx}(t,b)$. For the fourth
derivative, $|z|\le6\operatorname{sech}^2$ bounds the first term by $6e^{3V_*}\Phi_{xx}(t,b)$. In the second,
$\Phi_{xxx}^2\le4e^{4V_*}\Phi_{xx}^2\le4e^{4V_*}\Phi_{xx}$ and
$\mathbb{E}\Phi_{xx}(s,\tilde X_s)\le\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{xx}(s,\tilde X_s)e^{I_{ts}}]=\Phi_{xx}(t,b)$, so it is at most
$12e^{8V_*}\int_t^1a_s\,ds\,\Phi_{xx}(t,b)\le12V_*e^{8V_*}\Phi_{xx}(t,b)$. Together these give (a)
for finitely supported $\alpha$.

\emph{(a), general $\alpha$.} Take finitely supported $\alpha_n$ converging weakly to $\alpha$, so
that $\|\bar{\alpha_n}-\bar{\alpha}\|_{L^1}\to0$. By
\cite[Proposition~1(i)]{AC15a}, $\partial_x^j\Phi_\alpha$ exists and is continuous on
$[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ for every $j$, and $\partial_x^j\Phi_{\alpha_n}\to\partial_x^j\Phi_\alpha$ uniformly;
here $\Phi_\alpha$ of \cite{AC15a} is ours, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}. The inequalities proved above have
constants independent of $n$, so they pass to the limit.

\emph{(b).} For finitely supported $\alpha$ and $b\ge0$, $\Phi_x(t,b)=\mathbb{E}\tanh(\tilde X_1)\ge
\mathbb{E}\tanh(b-V_*+J)\to1$ as $b\to\infty$, so $1-\Phi_x(t,b)=\int_b^\infty\Phi_{xx}(t,y)\,dy$, and (a)
gives
\[
 \tfrac12\underline c\,e^{-2b}\le1-\Phi_x(t,b)\le\tfrac12\overline C\,e^{-2b}\qquad(b\ge0);
\]
by uniform convergence the same holds for every $\alpha$. The function $\Phi_x(t,\cdot)$ is odd
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}) and strictly increasing
($\Phi_{xx}>0$), and by the display its limits at $\pm\infty$ are $\pm1$; so it is a bijection onto
$(-1,1)$. For $m\in[0,1)$, $b=b_\alpha(t,m)\ge0$ satisfies $1-m=1-\Phi_x(t,b)$, and the display
gives $\tfrac12\log\frac{\underline c}{2(1-m)}\le b\le\tfrac12\log\frac{\overline C}2+\tfrac12\log\frac1{1-m}$,
with $\overline C/2>1$; oddness gives the bound for $m<0$. If $(t_n,m_n)\to(t,m)$ in
$[0,1]\times(-1,1)$, the numbers $b_\alpha(t_n,m_n)$ are bounded, and every limit point $b'$
satisfies $\Phi_x(t,b')=m$ by joint continuity of $\Phi_x$, so $b'=b_\alpha(t,m)$. Hence $b_\alpha$,
and with it $u_\alpha$, is continuous on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$. Finally, with $b=b_\alpha(t,m)$,
$e^{-2|b|}\le2(1-|m|)/\underline c$ by the display and the evenness of $\Phi_{xx}(t,\cdot)$, so
$0<u_\alpha(t,m)\le\overline C e^{-2|b|}\le(2\overline C/\underline c)(1-|m|)$, and the extension by
zero at $m=\pm1$ is continuous on $[0,1]\times[-1,1]$.

\emph{(c).} Take $\alpha_n$ as in the proof of (a), with Auffinger--Chen processes $X^n$
started at $(0,0)$ and driven by the same Brownian motion as $X$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a} and $\Phi_{\alpha_n,x}(0,0)=0$ (oddness),
$\Phi_{\alpha_n,x}(t,X^n_t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{a_s}\,\Phi_{\alpha_n,xx}(s,X^n_s)\,dB_s$. As $n\to\infty$,
the left side tends to $M_t$ uniformly, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iii}. The integrands tend to $U_s$
pointwise, by the uniform convergence in (a), the continuity of $\Phi_{xx}$ and
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-ii}, and they are bounded by one; by the It\^o
isometry and bounded convergence the stochastic integrals converge in $L^2$. This gives the
representation of $M_t$, which is also \cite[Lemma~2]{AC15b}. By the It\^o isometry,
$\Gamma_{\alpha}(t)=\mathbb{E} M_t^2=\int_0^ta_s\mathbb{E} U_s^2\,ds$. The map $s\mapsto\mathbb{E} U_s^2$ is continuous, by
dominated convergence, since $\Phi_{xx}$ is continuous and bounded and $X$ has continuous paths. So
$\Gamma_{\alpha}\in C^1([0,1])$ with $\Gamma_{\alpha}'=a\,\mathbb{E} U^2$, and since $\xi''\in C^1([0,1])$, the formula
$\mathcal{O}_\alpha'=-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma_{\alpha}-t)$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iii}
shows that $\mathcal{O}_\alpha\in C^2([0,1])$ with the stated $\mathcal{O}_\alpha''$.

Let $Q\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\alpha$. Since $\Gamma_{\alpha}(1)=\mathbb{E}\tanh^2(X_1)<1$,
$\mathcal{O}_\alpha'(1)=\frac12\xi''(1)(1-\Gamma_{\alpha}(1))>0$, so $\mathcal{O}_\alpha<\mathcal{O}_\alpha(1)$ just below $1$,
and $Q<1$. Thus $Q$ is an interior minimum of the $C^2$ function $\mathcal{O}_\alpha$, and
$\mathcal{O}_\alpha'(Q)=0\le\mathcal{O}_\alpha''(Q)$. Since $\xi''(Q)>0$, this gives $\Gamma_{\alpha}(Q)=Q$ and
$\mathcal{O}_\alpha''(Q)=-\frac12\xi''(Q)(\Gamma_{\alpha}'(Q)-1)=\frac12\xi''(Q)(1-\xi''(Q)\mathbb{E} U_Q^2)$. For
$\alpha=\zeta_f$ the set $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}$ is $C_f$, and $1-\xi''(Q)\mathbb{E} U_Q^2=\Delta(Q)$.

\emph{(d).} The functions $\Phi_x$ and $\Phi_{xx}$ are continuous and bounded by one, and $X$ has
continuous paths. If $t_n\to t$, then $M_{t_n}\to M_t$ and $U_{t_n}\to U_t$ almost surely, and by
bounded convergence $W_1(\operatorname{Law}(M_{t_n}),\operatorname{Law}(M_t))\le\mathbb{E}|M_{t_n}-M_t|\to0$, and likewise for $U$.
Since $\Phi_x(t,\cdot)$ is injective by (b), $b_\alpha(t,M_t)=X_t$, so $u_\alpha(t,M_t)=U_t$, which
is the last claim.

label: lem:poisson-shift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poisson-shift}
Let $\mathsf{x}>0$, let $u_1>u_2>\cdots$ be the points of a Poisson point process on $\mathbb{R}$ with intensity
$\mathsf{x} e^{-\mathsf{x} u}\,du$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a Polish space. Let $(\gamma_n,S_n)_{n\ge1}$ be
i.i.d.\ random elements of $\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal E$, independent of $(u_n)_{n\ge1}$, such that
$\gamma_1$ is independent of $S_1$ and $c:=\mathsf{x}^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\mathsf{x}\gamma_1}<\infty$. Then almost
surely the numbers $u_n+\gamma_n$, $n\ge1$, are pairwise distinct and only finitely many of them
exceed any given level. If $k\mapsto n_k$ is the bijection of $\mathbb{N}$ that lists them in decreasing
order, then
\[
 \bigl(u_{n_k}+\gamma_{n_k}-c,\ S_{n_k}\bigr)_{k\ge1}\overset{d}{=}\bigl(u_k,\ S_k\bigr)_{k\ge1}
 \qquad\text{in }(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal E)^{\mathbb{N}}.
\]
head: environment
name: Shifted Poisson points with independent marks

label: eq:marking-laplace
title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Marking formula.} Let $\mu(du)=\mathsf{x} e^{-\mathsf{x} u}\,du$, and let $P_\gamma$, $P_S$ be the laws of
$\gamma_1$, $S_1$. For every measurable $h:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal E\to[0,\infty]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:marking-laplace}
 \mathbb{E}\exp\Bigl(-\sum_{n\ge1}h(u_n,\gamma_n,S_n)\Bigr)
 =\exp\Bigl(-\int\bigl(1-e^{-h}\bigr)\,d(\mu\otimes P_\gamma\otimes P_S)\Bigr).
\end{equation}
Indeed, given that the Poisson number $K_t$ of points in $(t,\infty)$, of mean $e^{-\mathsf{x} t}$, is
$k$, these points with their marks are, up to order, $k$ i.i.d.\ triples of law
$\mu_t\otimes P_\gamma\otimes P_S$ with $\mu_t=e^{\mathsf{x} t}\mu|_{(t,\infty)}$: the points are the
ordered values of $k$ i.i.d.\ draws from $\mu_t$, and the marks are i.i.d.\ and independent of
them. Averaging over $k$ gives \eqref{eq:marking-laplace} for the points in $(t,\infty)$; let
$t\to-\infty$ (dominated convergence on the left, monotone on the right).

\emph{Change of variables.} Let $\Xi=\sum_n\delta_{(u_n,S_n)}$ and
$\Xi'=\sum_n\delta_{(u_n+\gamma_n-c,\,S_n)}$. For measurable $\varphi\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal E$
vanishing on some $(-\infty,t]\times\mathcal E$, \eqref{eq:marking-laplace} with
$h(u,g,\varsigma)=\varphi(u+g-c,\varsigma)$, the substitution $w=u+g-c$ and
$\int e^{\mathsf{x}(g-c)}P_\gamma(dg)=1$, then \eqref{eq:marking-laplace} with
$h(u,g,\varsigma)=\varphi(u,\varsigma)$, give
\[
 \mathbb{E} e^{-\Xi'(\varphi)}
 =\exp\Bigl(-\iint\bigl(1-e^{-\varphi(w,\varsigma)}\bigr)\,\mathsf{x} e^{-\mathsf{x} w}\,dw\,P_S(d\varsigma)\Bigr)
 =\mathbb{E} e^{-\Xi(\varphi)}.
\]
For $\varphi=\epsilon\mathbf{1}_{(t,\infty)\times\mathcal E}$, $\epsilon\downarrow0$, this gives
$\Xi'((t,\infty)\times\mathcal E)<\infty$ almost surely for every $t$; for
$\varphi=\sum_{i\le m}\epsilon_i\mathbf{1}_{D_i}$ it gives equal laws for $(\Xi(D_i))_{i\le m}$ and
$(\Xi'(D_i))_{i\le m}$ whenever the $D_i$ are Borel subsets of some $(t,\infty)\times\mathcal E$.
Such sets generate the $\sigma$-field of the maps $\omega\mapsto\omega(D)$ on the space $\mathbf M$
of counting measures finite on every $(t,\infty)\times\mathcal E$, since
$\omega(D)=\lim_{t\to-\infty}\omega(D\cap((t,\infty)\times\mathcal E))$; hence
$\Xi'\overset{d}{=}\Xi$ in $\mathbf M$ by a $\pi$-system argument.

\emph{Measurable enumeration.} Almost surely $\Xi$ lies in the set $\mathbf M^*\subset\mathbf M$ of
measures with infinitely many atoms, all of mass one and with pairwise distinct first
coordinates; $\mathbf M^*$ is measurable, and so is the map
$\operatorname{List}:\mathbf M^*\to(\mathbb{R}\times\mathcal E)^{\mathbb{N}}$ listing the atoms by decreasing first
coordinate (both facts are standard). Hence $\Xi'\in\mathbf M^*$ almost surely, which is the first
claim, and $\operatorname{List}(\Xi')=(u_{n_k}+\gamma_{n_k}-c,S_{n_k})_{k\ge1}$ has the law of
$\operatorname{List}(\Xi)=(u_k,S_k)_{k\ge1}$.
