label: rem:max-overlap
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{rem:max-overlap}
\leavevmode
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-a} Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For every $f>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $c>0$ there is
 $\kappa\in(0,1]$ such that, for every $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge Nf\bigr)\le e^{-cN};
 \]
 any $\kappa$ with $\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2$ and $(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})^2\ge8c\,\xi(\kappa)$
 works.
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-b} Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, and let $\theta,t>0$ with $f_{\mathrm{eq}}+t<\ell_\theta$.
 There are $\kappa,c'>0$ such that, for all large $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{Q}_\theta\bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\bigr)\le e^{-c'N}.
 \]
 Together with Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}: with $\mathbb{Q}_\theta$-probability at least $1-2e^{-c'N}$, the
 set $\{x:F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\}$ contains every maximizer of $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ and lies in
 $\{q_x>\kappa\}$. If moreover $\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$ and $\mathrm{FM}^{\ge}(\xi,\theta)$ holds,
 then $\ell_\theta\ge p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-c} Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}, and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$,
 $\varepsilon\in(0,(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/4)$ and $c>0$. There is $\kappa>0$ such that, for all large $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\Bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\geM_N-\varepsilon N\ \Bigm|\
  |N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\Bigr)\le e^{-cN}.
 \]
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Positive overlap of near-maximizers

label: lem:var-small
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:var-small}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:var-small-a} For every $N$ and every $x\in[-1,1]^N$,
 \[
  F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\leH_N(x)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\,\vartheta(q_x).
 \]
\item\label{lem:var-small-b} For every $\kappa\in(0,1]$ and $u>0$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\Bigl(\sup\bigl\{H_N(x):\ x\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_x\le\kappa\bigr\}>N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+u\bigr)\Bigr)
  \le\exp\Bigl(-\frac{u^2N}{2\xi(\kappa)}\Bigr).
 \]
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: TAP values at small self-overlap

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:var-small-a} Let $q=q_x$ and $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. By~\eqref{eq:intro-ftap},
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le F_\zeta(x)$. Three bounds compare $F_\zeta(x)$ with $NP_\zeta$.
\begin{steplist}
\item $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,a)\le\Phi_\zeta(q,0)$ for every $a\in[-1,1]$: take $b=0$ in the infimum
 that defines $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,a)$ for $|a|<1$, and pass to the continuous extension at $a=\pm1$.
\item $\Phi_\zeta(q,0)\le\Phi_\zeta(0,0)$. When $\zeta$ has finitely many atoms,
 $\Phi_\zeta(t,\cdot)$ is convex and
 $\partial_t\Phi_\zeta=-\frac{\xi''}2(\partial_x^2\Phi_\zeta+\zeta([0,t])(\partial_x\Phi_\zeta)^2)\le0$
 on each step of the Cole--Hopf recursion, so $t\mapsto\Phi_\zeta(t,0)$ is nonincreasing; this
 passes to general $\zeta$ by the uniform continuity of $\zeta\mapsto\Phi_\zeta$
 \cite[Lemma~14]{JT16}.
\item Since $\zeta([0,t])\le1$ and $\int_0^qt\xi''(t)\,dt=\vartheta(q)$,
 $\int_q^1t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,dt\ge\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,dt-\vartheta(q)$.
\end{steplist}
Together, $F_\zeta(x)\leH_N(x)+NP_\zeta+\frac N2\vartheta(q)$. Take the infimum over $\zeta$.

\ref{lem:var-small-b} The set $S_\kappa=\{x\in[-1,1]^N:q_x\le\kappa\}$ is compact and $H_N$ is
almost surely continuous, so the supremum is a supremum over a countable dense subset, and its law
depends only on the covariance of $H_N$. For $x,y\in[-1,1]^N$,
$\mathbb{E}(H_N(x)-H_N(y))^2\le K_\xi|x-y|^2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-field}\ref{lem:gauss-field-b}. The
Sudakov--Fernique inequality, comparing with $\sqrt{K_\xi}\,g\cdot x$ for a standard Gaussian vector
$g$, gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{S_\kappa}H_N\le\sqrt{K_\xi}\,\mathbb{E}\sup_{|x|\le\sqrt{\kappa N}}g\cdot x
 =\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa N}\,\mathbb{E}|g|\le\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}\,N .
\]
On $S_\kappa$ the variance of $H_N(x)$ is $N\xi(q_x)\le N\xi(\kappa)$, since $\xi$ is
nondecreasing on $[0,1]$. The Borell--TIS inequality~\eqref{eq:gauss-conc} with deviation $uN$
gives the claim.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{rem:max-overlap-a} Let $u=(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2$ and let $\kappa\in(0,1]$ satisfy
$\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<u$ and $u^2\ge2c\,\xi(\kappa)$; such $\kappa$ exist because
$\vartheta(\kappa)\le\kappa\xi'(1)$ and $\xi(\kappa)\le\kappa^2\xi(1)$. Outside the event of
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-b}, which has probability at most
$e^{-u^2N/(2\xi(\kappa))}\le e^{-cN}$, every $x\in[-1,1]^N$ with $q_x\le\kappa$ satisfies, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-a} and the monotonicity of $\vartheta$ on $[0,1]$,
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+u\bigr)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\vartheta(\kappa)<N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+2u)=Nf .
\]
Both bounds hold for every $N$.

\ref{rem:max-overlap-b} Let $C=C(\xi,\theta)$ be the constant of~\eqref{eq:max-crude}, so that
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B)\le e^{2CN}\mathbb{P}(B)^{1/2}$ for every event $B$ (proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}). The
level $\ell_\theta$ is finite because $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le(\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta})^{1/2}\le e^{CN/2}$. Fix
$a\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+t,\ell_\theta)$, put $\gamma=(a-t-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2>0$, and choose $\kappa\in(0,1]$ with
$\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<\gamma$ and $\gamma^2\ge4(2C+1)\xi(\kappa)$. Consider
\[
 B_1=\{\logZ_N\ge Na\},\qquad
 B_2=\bigl\{\sup\{H_N(x):x\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_x\le\kappa\}\le N(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+\gamma)\bigr\}.
\]
For all large $N$, $(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge(\ell_\theta+a)/2$, so
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B_1^c)\le e^{\theta Na}/\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le e^{-\theta N(\ell_\theta-a)/2}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-b},
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B_2^c)\le e^{2CN}e^{-\gamma^2N/(4\xi(\kappa))}\le e^{-N}$. On $B_1\cap B_2$, every $x$ with
$q_x\le\kappa$ satisfies, by Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-a},
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+\gamma\bigr)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\vartheta(\kappa)<N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+2\gamma)
 =N(a-t)\le\logZ_N-tN .
\]
So the event of~\ref{rem:max-overlap-b} lies in $B_1^c\cup B_2^c$, whose $\mathbb{Q}_\theta$-probability is at
most $e^{-c'N}$ with $c'=\frac12\min\{\theta(\ell_\theta-a)/2,1\}$, for all large $N$. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}, $\mathbb{Q}_\theta(M_N<\logZ_N-tN)\le e^{-c'N}$ for all large $N$. Off both events,
the maximum $M_N$ is attained, every maximizer lies in $\{x:F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\}$, and this set
lies in $\{q_x>\kappa\}$. Finally, if $\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$ and $\mathrm{FM}^{\ge}(\xi,\theta)$
holds, then $\ell_\theta\ge\Lambda(\theta)/\theta=p(\theta)$; and $p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, since
otherwise $\zeta_\theta$ would minimize $P$ and equal $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-a}, while
$\zeta_\theta(\{0\})\ge\theta>\theta_*=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})$.

\ref{rem:max-overlap-c} The lower limit in Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} is
nondecreasing in $\varepsilon$ and tends to $\Sigma(f)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, so it is at
least $\Sigma(f)$ for each fixed $\varepsilon$. Hence, for all large $N$, the conditioning event
$\{|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\}$ has probability at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-1)}$. On it, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\geM_N-\varepsilon N$ implies
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-2\varepsilon)$, and $f-2\varepsilon>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ because $\varepsilon<(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/4$.
Apply~\ref{rem:max-overlap-a} at the level $f-2\varepsilon$ with the rate $c+1-\Sigma(f)$, which
is positive because $\Sigma\le0$; it gives $\kappa$ such that the unconditional probability of the
event is at most $e^{-(c+1-\Sigma(f))N}$ for every $N$. Dividing gives the bound $e^{-cN}$.

label: rem:rpde
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:rpde}
The class $\mathcal{C}$ enters our proofs only through facts on the Parisi equation and on the
functionals $\mathrm{TAP}(\mu,\zeta)$ that we cite from \cite{CPS} (Theorems~5 and~12, Lemma~37, and
Section~11 there), from \cite{AC15a,AC15b} and from \cite{Che17}. These papers state their models
under a summability condition such as $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$, which there serves to define the
Hamiltonian, while the cited statements involve $\xi$ only through $\xi'$ and $\xi''$ on $[0,1]$.
If they hold for every $\xi$ satisfying \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, then every statement of this paper made for
$\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ holds under \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}\ (together with \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ where it is assumed). We have not
checked their proofs in that generality, and we do not claim this extension. It would add the
covariances with $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2=\infty$, all of which have radius of convergence at most two;
covariances of radius two with $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$ already lie in $\mathcal{C}$. The rest of
this subsection gives details.

label: lem:matrix-comparison
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Gaussian comparison and the resolvent equation

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-a} For unit vectors $v,w$ with $v\cdot w=r$, put
$X_v=\sqrt a\,v^{\mathsf T}W_N v$ and $Y_v=2\sqrt{a/N}\,\gamma\cdot v$, with $\gamma$ a standard
Gaussian vector. From the covariance of $W_N$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}(X_v-X_w)^2=\frac{4a}N(1-r^2)\le\frac{8a}N(1-r)=\mathbb{E}(Y_v-Y_w)^2 .
\]
The Sudakov--Fernique inequality compares expected suprema of two Gaussian processes with this
ordering of increment variances. Its interpolation proof applies unchanged when the same
deterministic function, here $-v^{\mathsf T}D_Nv$, is added to both processes, because that
function does not contribute to the derivative along the interpolation. On finite subsets of the
sphere, and then by continuity on the whole sphere,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N\bigr)=\mathbb{E}\sup_{|v|=1}\{X_v-v^{\mathsf T}D_Nv\}
 \le\mathbb{E}\sup_{|v|=1}\{Y_v-v^{\mathsf T}D_Nv\}.
\]
For $t<\min_iD_{N,ii}$ and $|v|=1$, completing the square in each coordinate gives
$2\sqrt{a/N}\,\gamma\cdot v-v^{\mathsf T}D_Nv\le-t+\frac aN\sum_i\gamma_i^2/(D_{N,ii}-t)$, and
taking expectations proves~\eqref{eq:matrix-comparison}. For $D_N=0$ and $a=1$ the infimum is $2$,
attained at $t=-1$. As a function of the independent standard Gaussian variables that define
$W_N$, the largest eigenvalue is $\sqrt{2/N}$-Lipschitz, so Gaussian concentration
\cite{Ledoux} gives $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_{\max}(W_N)>2+\delta)\le e^{-\delta^2N/4}$, and the same holds
for $\lambda_{\max}(-W_N)$ since $-W_N$ has the law of $W_N$.

\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-b} Write $W_N=(W_{kl})$. The entries $W_{kl}$, $k\le l$, are independent, with variance
$1/N$ for $k<l$ and $2/N$ for $k=l$. Differentiating the inverse,
$\partial G/\partial W_{kl}=\sqrt a\,GE^{kl}G$ with $E^{kl}=e_ke_l^{\mathsf T}+e_le_k^{\mathsf T}$
for $k<l$ and $E^{kk}=e_ke_k^{\mathsf T}$. Since $G$ is symmetric,
$\partial(v^{\mathsf T}Gw)/\partial W_{kl}=\sqrt a\,[(Gv)_k(Gw)_l+(Gv)_l(Gw)_k]$ for $k<l$, and the
Gaussian Poincar\'e inequality, applied to real and imaginary parts, gives
$\operatorname{Var}(v^{\mathsf T}Gw)\le\frac{4a}N|Gv|^2|Gw|^2\le4a|v|^2|w|^2/(N\varepsilon^4)$, because
$\|G\|\le\varepsilon^{-1}$. For the trace, $\partial m_N/\partial W_{kl}=2\sqrt a\,(G^2)_{kl}/N$
for $k<l$ and $\sqrt a\,(G^2)_{kk}/N$ for $k=l$, so
$\operatorname{Var} m_N\le\frac{4a}{N^3}\|G^2\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le4a/(N^2\varepsilon^4)$. Conjugating by a diagonal
sign matrix preserves the law of $W_N$ and fixes $D_N$, so $(\mathbb{E} G)_{ij}=0$ for $i\ne j$. From
$(D_{N,ii}-z)G_{ii}=1+\sqrt a\sum_kW_{ik}G_{ki}$ and Gaussian integration by parts, in which the
diagonal variance $2/N$ supplies the second copy of $G_{ii}^2$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-ibp}
 (D_{N,ii}-z)\mathbb{E} G_{ii}=1+a\mathbb{E}[m_NG_{ii}]+\frac aN\mathbb{E}(G^2)_{ii}.
\end{equation}
By~\eqref{eq:matrix-resolvent-var} with $v=w=e_i$ and Cauchy--Schwarz,
$|\mathbb{E}[m_NG_{ii}]-\bar m_N\mathbb{E} G_{ii}|\le4a/(N^{3/2}\varepsilon^4)$, and
$|\frac aN(G^2)_{ii}|\le a/(N\varepsilon^2)$. Since $\operatorname{Im}\bar m_N\ge0$,
$|D_{N,ii}-z-a\bar m_N|\ge\varepsilon$, and~\eqref{eq:matrix-approx-dyson} follows by dividing and
averaging over $i$.

\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-c} Let $m_1,m_2$ be two solutions. Taking imaginary parts
in~\eqref{eq:matrix-dyson},
$a\int|D-z-am_j|^{-2}\rho(dD)=a\operatorname{Im}m_j/(\operatorname{Im}z+a\operatorname{Im}m_j)<1$.
Subtracting the two equations, if $m_1\ne m_2$ then
$1=a\int\rho(dD)/[(D-z-am_1)(D-z-am_2)]$, which contradicts Cauchy--Schwarz. Now let
$\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$. Since $|\bar m_N|\le\varepsilon^{-1}$, every subsequence has a further
subsequence along which $\bar m_N\to m^*$ with $\operatorname{Im}m^*\ge0$. In the average
in~\eqref{eq:matrix-approx-dyson} the integrand $D\mapsto(D-z-a\bar m_N)^{-1}$ is bounded by
$\varepsilon^{-1}$ and converges uniformly in $D$ to $(D-z-am^*)^{-1}$, which is bounded and
continuous; so $m^*=\int\rho(dD)/(D-z-am^*)$. The imaginary part of the integrand is positive, so
$\operatorname{Im}m^*>0$, and $m^*$ solves~\eqref{eq:matrix-dyson}. By uniqueness the whole
sequence $\bar m_N$ converges to this solution, and~\eqref{eq:matrix-resolvent-var} gives
convergence of $m_N$ in probability.
head: environment

label: lem:matrix-gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-gap}
Let $a>0$, let $0<U_i\le1$ for $i\le N$, put $\chi_N=N^{-1}\sum_iU_i$ and
$D_N=\operatorname{diag}(U_i^{-1}+a\chi_N)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:matrix-gap-a} If $1-aN^{-1}\sum_iU_i^2\ge d>0$, there are $g_0,c_M>0$ depending
 only on $a$ and $d$ such that
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-gap}
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\not\succeq g_0I\bigr)\le e^{-c_MN}.
 \end{equation}
 The same holds, with $(g_0,c_M)$ replaced by $(g_0/2,c_M/4)$, after $U_i^{-1}$ is replaced by
 $\min(U_i^{-1},K)$, for every fixed $K$ larger than a constant depending only on $a$ and $d$.
\item\label{lem:matrix-gap-b} Suppose that the empirical laws of the $U_i$ converge weakly to the
 law of a $(0,1]$-valued variable $U$ with $\chi=\mathbb{E} U$ and $1-a\mathbb{E} U^2>0$. Then, for deterministic
 vectors $v_N,w_N$ of bounded Euclidean norm,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-inverse}
  v_N^{\mathsf T}\bigl(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\bigr)^{-1}w_N-\sum_{i\le N}U_iv_{N,i}w_{N,i}\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \frac1N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\bigr)^{-1}\longrightarrow\chi
 \end{equation}
 in probability, where the left sides are set to zero outside the event of~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a}.
 The same holds for random vectors of bounded norm independent of $W_N$.
\item\label{lem:matrix-gap-c} \textup{(General profiles.)} Let $D_N$ be deterministic real diagonal
 matrices with $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho'$ weakly, and let $m_0\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy
 \[
  m_0=\int\frac{\rho'(dD)}{D-am_0},\qquad a\varsigma<1,\qquad
  \varsigma:=\int\frac{\rho'(dD)}{(D-am_0)^2},
 \]
 where $D_{N,ii}-am_0\ge c_\circ>0$ for all $i$ and all large $N$. If
 $\mathbb{P}(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\succeq g'I)\to1$ for some $g'>0$, then, for $v_N,w_N$ as
 in~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b},
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-variant}
 \begin{gathered}
  v_N^{\mathsf T}\bigl(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\bigr)^{-1}w_N-\sum_{i\le N}\frac{v_{N,i}w_{N,i}}{D_{N,ii}-am_0}
  \longrightarrow0,\\
  \frac1N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\bigr)^{-1}\longrightarrow m_0
 \end{gathered}
 \end{equation}
 in probability, with the left sides set to zero outside the event
 $\{D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N\succeq g'I\}$.
\item\label{lem:matrix-gap-d} \textup{(Capped profiles.)} Let $U$ be as in~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b},
 let $\rho_K$ be the law of $\min(U^{-1},K)+a\chi$ and $V=\max(U,K^{-1})$. For a small fixed
 $\delta>0$ and all large $K$, the map $m\mapsto\int\rho_K(dD)/(D-am)=\mathbb{E}[V/(1-a(m-\chi)V)]$ is a
 contraction of $[\chi-\delta,\chi+\delta]$; its fixed point $m_0=\chi+O(K^{-1})$ satisfies the
 hypotheses of~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-c} with $\rho'=\rho_K$ and $c_\circ=\frac12$, for every profile
 $D_{N,ii}=\min(u_i^{-1},K)+a\chi_N'$ with $0<u_i\le1$, $\chi_N'\to\chi$ and $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho_K$,
 except for the gap condition, which must be checked separately.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Spectral gap and inverse at a strictly stable profile

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a} Put $t=a\chi_N+s$ with $s=\min\{\frac12,d/(4a)\}$. Then
$D_{N,ii}-t=U_i^{-1}-s>0$, and the right side of~\eqref{eq:matrix-comparison} equals
\[
 -s+\frac{as}N\sum_i\frac{U_i^2}{1-sU_i}\le-ds+2as^2\le-\frac{ds}2 ,
\]
since $U_i^2/(1-sU_i)\le U_i^2+2s$ for $s\le\frac12$. The largest eigenvalue of
$\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N$ is $\sqrt{2a/N}$-Lipschitz in the standard Gaussian variables, so Gaussian
concentration at distance $ds/4$ gives~\eqref{eq:matrix-gap} with $g_0=ds/4$ and
$c_M=d^2s^2/(64a)$. For the cap put $V_i=\max(U_i,K^{-1})$; at the same $t$ the right side
of~\eqref{eq:matrix-comparison} becomes
$\frac aN\sum_i(V_i-U_i)-s+\frac{as}N\sum_iV_i^2/(1-sV_i)$, which differs from the uncapped value
by at most $(a+10as)/K$, uniformly in the profile, because $y\mapsto y^2/(1-sy)$ is
$10$-Lipschitz on $[0,1]$. For large $K$ the bound $-ds/4$ survives, and concentration at distance
$ds/8$ gives the capped statement.

\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b} Since $U$ has no atom at $0$, the empirical laws of $U_i^{-1}$ converge to
that of $U^{-1}$, and $\chi_N\to\chi$; so $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho:=\operatorname{Law}(U^{-1}+a\chi)$. Fix
$\varepsilon>0$ and put $z=\mathrm i\varepsilon$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-b}, $\mathbb{E} v^{\mathsf T}Gw$ equals
$\sum_iv_iw_i(D_{N,ii}-z-a\bar m_N)^{-1}+O(|v||w|/N)$, the denominators have modulus at least
$\varepsilon$, and $\bar m_N\to m(z)$ by part~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-c}. Together with the
variance bound,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-resolvent-limit}
 v_N^{\mathsf T}G_N(z)w_N-\sum_i\frac{v_{N,i}w_{N,i}}{D_{N,ii}-z-am(z)}\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
in probability; no delocalization is needed, since $\sum_i|v_iw_i|\le|v||w|$. We identify $m(z)$
for small $\varepsilon$. At $z=0$ the equation $m=\int\rho(dD)/(D-z-am)$, without the sign
condition, has the solution $m=\chi$, because $D-a\chi=U^{-1}$; the derivative of its right side in
$m$ there is $a\mathbb{E} U^2<1$, and all denominators are at least $1$ near $(0,\chi)$. The analytic
implicit function theorem gives a local solution $m_{\mathrm{loc}}(z)$ with
$m_{\mathrm{loc}}(0)=\chi$ and $m_{\mathrm{loc}}'(0)=\mathbb{E} U^2/(1-a\mathbb{E} U^2)>0$. Hence
$\operatorname{Im}m_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathrm i\varepsilon)>0$ for small $\varepsilon$, and uniqueness
in~\eqref{eq:matrix-dyson} gives $m(\mathrm i\varepsilon)=m_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathrm i\varepsilon)\to\chi$.
On the event of~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a}, which has probability tending to one because
$N^{-1}\sum_iU_i^2\to\mathbb{E} U^2$,
$\|G_N(\mathrm i\varepsilon)-(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N)^{-1}\|\le\varepsilon/g_0^2$. Finally
$D_{N,ii}-\mathrm i\varepsilon-am(\mathrm i\varepsilon)=U_i^{-1}+\delta_N(\varepsilon)$ with
$\delta_N(\varepsilon)=a(\chi_N-\chi)+a\chi-\mathrm i\varepsilon-am(\mathrm i\varepsilon)$
independent of $i$, and $|(U_i^{-1}+\delta)^{-1}-U_i|\le2|\delta|$ when $|\delta|\le\frac12$,
because $U_i^{-1}\ge1$. Letting first $N\to\infty$ and then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$
in~\eqref{eq:matrix-resolvent-limit} proves the first claim. For the trace,
$m_N(\mathrm i\varepsilon)\to m(\mathrm i\varepsilon)$ in probability, the gap event gives
$|m_N(\mathrm i\varepsilon)-N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N)^{-1}|\le\varepsilon/g_0^2$, and
$m(\mathrm i\varepsilon)\to\chi$. Random vectors independent of $W_N$ are handled by
conditioning on them.

\ref{lem:matrix-gap-c} The proof of~\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b} applies with $(\rho',m_0)$ in place of
$(\rho,\chi)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison} uses only that the diagonal is real and that its
empirical laws converge weakly, with errors uniform in the profile. The implicit function theorem
at $(0,m_0)$ uses the displayed conditions, since $\operatorname{supp}\rho'\subset[am_0+c_\circ,\infty)$, and gives
$m'(0)=\varsigma/(1-a\varsigma)>0$, which identifies the branch. The lower bound $c_\circ$ makes
the reciprocals $(D_{N,ii}-\mathrm i\varepsilon-am(\mathrm i\varepsilon))^{-1}$ converge to
$(D_{N,ii}-am_0)^{-1}$ uniformly in $i$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Only empirical laws and
weighted averages of reciprocals enter, not operator-norm convergence of the diagonals, so sparse
changes of coordinates are allowed.

\ref{lem:matrix-gap-d} Since $D-am=V^{-1}(1-a(m-\chi)V)$ for $D=V^{-1}+a\chi$, the formula for the
map holds. Its value at $m=\chi$ is $\mathbb{E} V=\chi+\mathbb{E}(K^{-1}-U)_+=\chi+O(K^{-1})$, and on
$|m-\chi|\le\delta$ its derivative is at most $a\mathbb{E} V^2/(1-a\delta)^2$, where
$a\mathbb{E} V^2\le a\mathbb{E} U^2+aK^{-2}<1$ for large $K$. For small $\delta$ and large $K$ the map is therefore
a contraction of $[\chi-\delta,\chi+\delta]$ into itself, and its fixed point $m_0$ satisfies
$|m_0-\chi|=O(K^{-1})$ and $a\varsigma<1$. The denominators satisfy
$D_{N,ii}-am_0\ge1-a|\chi_N'-\chi|-a|m_0-\chi|\ge\frac12$ for large $N$ and $K$.

label: lem:matrix-third
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The Hessian of the Gaussian field

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-third-a} Differentiating $N\xi(R(x,y))$ twice in $x$ and twice in $y$ and setting
$x=y$ gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\,\partial_{ij}H_N(y)\,\partial_{kl}H_N(y)
 =\frac{\xi''}N(\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}+\delta_{il}\delta_{jk})
 +\frac{\xi'''}{N^2}(y_iy_k\delta_{jl}+y_iy_l\delta_{jk}+y_jy_k\delta_{il}+y_jy_l\delta_{ik})
 +\frac{\xi''''}{N^3}y_iy_jy_ky_l,
\]
with the derivatives of $\xi$ at $r$. The three terms are the covariances of the three independent
summands in the displayed decomposition, which is therefore an identity in law between centred
Gaussian matrices. Contracting with $S$ gives~\eqref{eq:matrix-hess-cov}; the bound uses
$|Sy|^2\le\|S\|^2|y|^2\le N\operatorname{tr} S^2$, $(y^{\mathsf T}Sy)^2\le N^2\operatorname{tr} S^2$ and $r\le1$.

\ref{lem:matrix-third-b} For $k\in\{2,3\}$ let $T_k(y,\phi)=D^kH_N(y)[\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k]$ on the
index set $\mathcal I_k=[-1,1]^N\times(S^{N-1})^k$. By the series
$N\xi(R(x,y))=N\sum_p\beta_p^2(x\cdot y/N)^p$, the $j$-th derivative in $x$ along unit vectors
$\phi_1,\dots,\phi_j$ is $N^{1-j}\xi^{(j)}(R(x,y))\prod_i(y\cdot\phi_i)$, and each further
derivative in $y$ along a unit vector either differentiates $\xi^{(j)}(R(x,y))$, producing a factor
$x\cdot\psi/N$, or replaces a factor $y\cdot\phi_i$ by $\phi_i\cdot\psi$. Since
$|y\cdot\phi|\le\sqrt N$ and $|x\cdot\psi|/N\le N^{-1/2}$, every mixed derivative of order $j$ in
$x$ and $l$ in $y$, contracted with unit vectors, is bounded by $CN^{1-(j+l)/2}$, with $C$
depending on $\xi^{(i)}(1)$ for $i\le j+l$. Hence $\operatorname{Var} T_k(y,\phi)\le CN^{1-k}$. For the canonical
distance $d$ of $T_k$, the mean value theorem in $y$ (using the bound for $D^{k+1}H_N$) and
multilinearity in $\phi$ give
\[
 d\bigl((y,\phi),(y',\phi')\bigr)\le CN^{(1-k)/2}\Bigl(\frac{|y-y'|}{\sqrt N}+\sum_{i\le k}|\phi_i-\phi_i'|\Bigr).
\]
The set $N^{-1/2}[-1,1]^N$ lies in the unit ball, which, like the unit sphere, is covered by
$(3/s)^N$ balls of radius $s\le1$. For the distance in brackets, the product index set is
therefore covered by $(3(k+1)/s)^{(k+1)N}$ sets of radius $s\le k+1$, and Dudley's entropy bound
gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{\mathcal I_k}T_k\le CN^{(1-k)/2}\int_0^{2(k+1)}\sqrt{(k+1)N\log(3(k+1)/s)}\,ds\le C'N^{1-k/2},
\]
and the Borell--TIS inequality, with variance $\sigma^2\le CN^{1-k}$, gives
$\mathbb{P}(\sup T_k>\mathbb{E}\sup T_k+u)\le e^{-u^2/(2\sigma^2)}$. Taking $u$ a large constant for $k=2$ and a
large multiple of $N^{-1/2}$ for $k=3$ proves~\eqref{eq:matrix-sup}; the process is continuous, so
the suprema are measurable. Derivatives of $\xi$ up to order eight enter, through the canonical
distance of $T_3$.

label: rem:matrix-conditional
title: Remark
head: environment
name: Conditioned fields

label: lem:matrix-correction
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The TAP correction

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-correction-a} Let $\Phi_0$ be the solution on $[r,1]$ with coefficient zero and
terminal value $\log\cosh$. By the coefficient sandwich of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef}, which extends
to measurable coefficients by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}, and since the second moments
appearing there lie in $[0,1]$, $\Phi_\alpha(r,b)$ lies between $\Phi_0(r,b)$ and
$\Phi_0(r,b)+\frac12(\xi'(1)-\xi'(r))$. Here $\Phi_0(r,b)=\mathbb{E}\log\cosh(b+\sigma Z)$ with $Z$ standard Gaussian and
$\sigma^2=\xi'(1)-\xi'(r)$, so Jensen's inequality gives $\Phi_\alpha(r,b)\ge\log\cosh b\ge|b|-\log2$,
and $\log\cosh y\le y^2/2$ gives $\Phi_\alpha(r,0)\le\xi'(1)$. Hence
$-\log2\le\inf_b\{\Phi_\alpha(r,b)-mb\}\le\Phi_\alpha(r,0)\le\xi'(1)$.

\ref{lem:matrix-correction-b} By~\eqref{eq:matrix-onesided},
$\sup_b|\Phi_\alpha(r,b)-\Phi_\alpha(r',b)|\le\xi''(1)|r-r'|$, and an infimum preserves this bound;
the integral term of $V_\alpha$ is $\frac12\xi''(1)$-Lipschitz in $r$. For $|m|<1$ the infimum
defining $\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r,m)$ is attained at $b_\alpha(r,m)$, and $\partial_m\Phi^{*}_\alpha=-b_\alpha$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b},
$|b_\alpha(r,m)|\le\frac12\log(\overline C/2)+\frac12\log\frac1{1-|m|}$. The function
$s\mapsto\log\frac1{1-|s|}$ on $[-1,1]$ has decreasing rearrangement $y\mapsto\log(2/y)$ on $[0,2]$,
so its integral over any interval of length $h$ is at most $\int_0^h\log(2/y)\,dy=\varrho(h)$.
Therefore, using $h\le\varrho(h)$ and continuity at $m=\pm1$,
$|\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r,m)-\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r,m')|\le L_2\varrho(|m-m'|)$. Integrating over an optimal
coupling of $\mu$ and $\mu'$ and using the concavity of $\varrho$ gives the bound in $\mu$. An
infimum over $\alpha$ of functions with a common modulus has the same modulus.

\ref{lem:matrix-correction-c} By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef} on $[r,1]$, extended to measurable
coefficients by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable},
$\sup_b|\Phi_\alpha(r,b)-\Phi_\beta(r,b)|\le\frac12\xi''(1)\int_r^1|\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\beta}|$. The
conjugates inherit this bound, and the integral terms of $V_\alpha$ and $V_\beta$ differ by at most
the same amount.
head: environment

label: lem:matrix-orderstab
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-orderstab}
Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $t\in[0,1]$ put
$\epsilon=\int_t^1|\bar{\alpha}(s)-\bar{\beta}(s)|\,ds$. Then
\[
 \sup_{b\in\mathbb{R}}\bigl|\Phi_{\alpha,x}(t,b)-\Phi_{\beta,x}(t,b)\bigr|\le L_v\epsilon,\qquad
 \sup_{b\in\mathbb{R}}\bigl|\Phi_{\alpha,xx}(t,b)-\Phi_{\beta,xx}(t,b)\bigr|\le2\bigl(C_{34}L_v\epsilon\bigr)^{1/2},
\]
and there is a nondecreasing function $\omega_S$ on $[0,1]$ with $\omega_S(\epsilon)\to0$ as
$\epsilon\downarrow0$, depending only on $\xi'(1)$ and $\xi''(1)$, such that
\[
 \sup_{m\in[-1,1]}\bigl|u_\alpha(t,m)-u_\beta(t,m)\bigr|\le\omega_S(\epsilon).
\]
head: environment
name: Stability in the order parameter

title: Proof
body_md:
On $[t,1]$ the functions $\Phi_{\alpha,x}$ and $\Phi_{\beta,x}$ are the space derivatives of the
solutions with terminal value $\log\cosh$ and coefficients $\bar{\alpha}$ and $\bar{\beta}$ restricted
to $[t,1)$, with values in $[0,1]$. Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-stability} with $G=1$ and equal terminal
values, extended to measurable coefficients by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i},
gives the first bound. For the second, $w=\Phi_{\alpha,x}(t,\cdot)-\Phi_{\beta,x}(t,\cdot)$ satisfies
$\|w\|_\infty\le L_v\epsilon$ and $\|w''\|_\infty\le2C_{34}$, because
$|\Phi_{\alpha,xxx}|\le C_{34}\Phi_{\alpha,xx}\le C_{34}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}. Taylor's formula at $b\pm h$ gives
$|w'(b)|\le\|w\|_\infty/h+h\|w''\|_\infty/2$, and the choice $h=(2\|w\|_\infty/\|w''\|_\infty)^{1/2}$
gives $\|w'\|_\infty\le(2\|w\|_\infty\|w''\|_\infty)^{1/2}$.

For the susceptibilities fix $\tau\in(0,1)$. If $|m|\le1-\tau$, then by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b} both $b_\alpha=b_\alpha(t,m)$ and
$b_\beta=b_\beta(t,m)$ lie in $[-B_\tau,B_\tau]$, $B_\tau=\frac12\log(\overline C/2)+\frac12\log\frac1\tau$,
where $\Phi_{\alpha,xx}\ge c_\tau:=\underline c\,e^{-2B_\tau}$. Since
$\Phi_{\alpha,x}(t,b_\alpha)=m=\Phi_{\beta,x}(t,b_\beta)$, the mean value theorem gives
$c_\tau|b_\alpha-b_\beta|\le|\Phi_{\alpha,x}(t,b_\beta)-\Phi_{\beta,x}(t,b_\beta)|\le L_v\epsilon$.
Hence
\[
 |u_\alpha(t,m)-u_\beta(t,m)|\le C_{34}|b_\alpha-b_\beta|+\bigl|\Phi_{\alpha,xx}(t,b_\beta)-\Phi_{\beta,xx}(t,b_\beta)\bigr|
 \le\frac{C_{34}L_v\epsilon}{c_\tau}+2\bigl(C_{34}L_v\epsilon\bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
If $|m|>1-\tau$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b} gives
$0\le u_\alpha,u_\beta\le(2\overline C/\underline c)\tau$. The infimum over $\tau\in(0,1)$ of the
sum of the two bounds is the required $\omega_S(\epsilon)$.
head: environment

label: lem:matrix-hessian
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-hessian}
Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. Let $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $x\in(-1,1)^N\setminus\{0\}$, and put
$r=q_x\in(0,1)$, $a_r=\xi''(r)$, $u_i=u_\alpha(r,x_i)$, $b_i=b_\alpha(r,x_i)$, $v_i=v_\alpha(r,x_i)$,
$T_i=T_\alpha(r,x_i)$, $\chi_\alpha(x)=N^{-1}\sum_iu_i$ and
$\Delta_N^\alpha(x)=1-a_rN^{-1}\sum_iu_i^2$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:matrix-hessian-a} $F_\alpha$ is continuously differentiable on
 $(-1,1)^N\setminus\{0\}$, and
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-gradient}
  \nabla F_\alpha(x)=\nablaH_N(x)-(b_i)_{i\le N}-a_r\chi_\alpha(x)\,x .
 \end{equation}
\item\label{lem:matrix-hessian-b} For $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ let
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-ambient}
  \nabla^2_\sigma F_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2H_N(x)-\operatorname{diag}\bigl(u_1^{-1},\dots,u_N^{-1}\bigr)-a_r\chi_\alpha(x)\,I
  +R_\sigma(x),
 \end{equation}
 \[
  R_\sigma(x)=-\frac{a_r}N\bigl(xv^{\mathsf T}+vx^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
  -\frac2N\Bigl\{\xi'''(r)\chi_\alpha(x)-\frac{a_r^2}{2N}\sum_{i\le N}T_i
  +a_r\bar{\alpha}^{\sigma}(r)\,\Delta_N^\alpha(x)\Bigr\}xx^{\mathsf T}.
 \]
 Then, for every $e\in\mathbb{R}^N$,
 $\lim_{s\downarrow0}s^{-1}(\nabla F_\alpha(x+se)-\nabla F_\alpha(x))$ equals
 $\nabla^2_+F_\alpha(x)e$ if $x\cdot e\ge0$ and $\nabla^2_-F_\alpha(x)e$ if $x\cdot e\le0$. The
 matrix $R_\sigma(x)$ is symmetric, of rank at most two, with range in
 $\operatorname{span}\{x,v\}$, and
 $R_+(x)-R_-(x)=-\frac{2a_r}N\,\alpha(\{r\})\,\Delta_N^\alpha(x)\,xx^{\mathsf T}$. In particular
 $\nabla^2_+F_\alpha(x)=\nabla^2_-F_\alpha(x)$ when $\alpha(\{r\})=0$, and the compressions of the
 two one-sided Hessians to $x^\perp$ always coincide.
\item\label{lem:matrix-hessian-c} If $\nabla F_\alpha(x)=0$, this common compression is the
 Riemannian Hessian at $x$ of the restriction of $F_\alpha$ to the sphere $\{y:q_y=r\}$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Gradient and one-sided Hessians of the TAP function

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-hessian-a} Write $r_y=q_y$. In $F_\alpha(y)=H_N(y)+\sum_i\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r_y,y_i)
-\frac N2\int_{r_y}^1t\xi''(t)\bar{\alpha}(t)\,dt$, the derivative in $y_j$ of the middle term at fixed
$r_y$ is $-b_\alpha(r_y,y_j)$. The infimum defining $\Phi^{*}_\alpha$ is attained at a unique point
that depends continuously on $r$, so~\eqref{eq:matrix-onesided} gives the one-sided derivatives
$\partial_r^\pm\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r,m)=-\frac{a_r}2(u_\alpha+\bar{\alpha}^{\pm}(r)m^2)$. With
$\partial_{y_j}r_y=2y_j/N$, the terms produced by the dependence on $r_y$ are
\[
 \frac{2y_j}N\Bigl[-\frac{a_r}2\sum_i\bigl(u_i+\bar{\alpha}^{\pm}(r)y_i^2\bigr)
 +\frac N2\,r\,a_r\,\bar{\alpha}^{\pm}(r)\Bigr]=-a_r\chi_\alpha(y)\,y_j ,
\]
because $\sum_iy_i^2=Nr$: the terms containing $\bar{\alpha}^{\pm}$ cancel. So both one-sided
partial derivatives exist and are given by~\eqref{eq:matrix-gradient}, which is continuous in $y$;
hence $F_\alpha$ is continuously differentiable.

\ref{lem:matrix-hessian-b} Let $e\in\mathbb{R}^N$ and $y=x+se$. Then
$r_y-r=2s(x\cdot e)/N+s^2|e|^2/N$, so for small $s>0$ the self-overlap moves to the right of $r$ if
$x\cdot e>0$, to the left if $x\cdot e<0$, and by $O(s^2)$ if $x\cdot e=0$. By the
identities~\eqref{eq:matrix-inverse-field}, the joint continuity of $u_\alpha$, $v_\alpha$ and
$b_\alpha$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}), and the mean value theorem in
the variable $m$,
\[
 b_\alpha(r_y,y_j)-b_\alpha(r,x_j)=\frac{se_j}{u_j}+\frac{a_r}2\bigl(v_j+2\bar{\alpha}^{\sigma}(r)x_j\bigr)(r_y-r)+o(s),
\]
with $\sigma$ the sign of $x\cdot e$, and similarly for $u_\alpha(r_y,y_i)$. Differentiating the $j$-th component
$\partial_jH_N(y)-b_\alpha(r_y,y_j)-\xi''(r_y)\chi_\alpha(y)y_j$ of~\eqref{eq:matrix-gradient}
along $e$ with these expansions gives $\sum_k H_{jk}e_k$, where the contributions to $H_{jk}$ of the
last two terms are
\begin{align*}
 \partial_k\bigl[b_\alpha(r_y,y_j)\bigr]&=\frac{\delta_{jk}}{u_j}+\frac{a_r}N\bigl(v_jx_k+2\bar{\alpha}^{\sigma} x_jx_k\bigr),\\
 \partial_k\bigl[\xi''(r_y)\chi_\alpha(y)y_j\bigr]&=a_r\chi_\alpha\delta_{jk}+\frac{a_r}Nx_jv_k
 +\frac{2\xi'''(r)\chi_\alpha}Nx_jx_k\\
 &\qquad-\frac{a_r^2}{N^2}\Bigl(\sum_iT_i\Bigr)x_jx_k
 -\frac{2a_r^2\bar{\alpha}^{\sigma}}{N^2}\Bigl(\sum_iu_i^2\Bigr)x_jx_k ,
\end{align*}
where $\partial_k\chi_\alpha=N^{-1}[v_k+(2x_k/N)\sum_i\partial_r^\sigma u_\alpha(r,x_i)]$ was used.
Collecting the multiples of $x_jx_k$ gives~\eqref{eq:matrix-ambient}. When $x\cdot e=0$ the terms
containing $r_y-r$ are $o(s)$, and $R_+(x)e=R_-(x)e=-\frac{a_r}Nx(v\cdot e)$. The remaining claims
are read off from the formula for $R_\sigma$, since $\bar{\alpha}^{+}(r)-\bar{\alpha}^{-}(r)=\alpha(\{r\})$
and $Px=0$ for the orthogonal projection $P$ onto $x^\perp$.

\ref{lem:matrix-hessian-c} On the sphere $\{q_y=r\}$ the function $F_\alpha$ coincides with the
smooth function $\tilde F(y)=H_N(y)+\sum_i\Phi^{*}_\alpha(r,y_i)-c$, for a constant $c$. The
Riemannian Hessian of a function on a sphere centred at the origin is
$P(\nabla^2\tilde F(x)-(x\cdot\nabla\tilde F(x)/|x|^2)I)P$. Here
$\nabla^2\tilde F=\nabla^2H_N-\operatorname{diag}(u_i^{-1})$ and $\nabla\tilde F=\nablaH_N-(b_i)_i$, and
$\nabla F_\alpha(x)=0$ gives $x\cdot\nabla\tilde F(x)=a_r\chi_\alpha(x)|x|^2$ by~\eqref{eq:matrix-gradient}.
Since $PR_\sigma(x)P=0$ on $x^\perp$, the Riemannian Hessian equals the compression of
$\nabla^2_\sigma F_\alpha(x)$.

label: cor:matrix-truncated
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:matrix-truncated}
In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hessian}, for $K\ge1$ put
$D^\alpha_K(x)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\min(u_i^{-1},K)+a_r\chi_\alpha(x)\bigr)_{i\le N}$ and
$p^\alpha_K(x)=N^{-1}\#\{i:u_i<1/K\}$. Then $D^\alpha_K(x)\in\mathcal D_{K+\xi''(1)}$, and for
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$
\[
 d_{\mathrm{L}}\Bigl(\operatorname{ESD}\bigl(\nabla^2_\sigma F_\alpha(x)\bigr),\operatorname{ESD}\bigl(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D^\alpha_K(x)\bigr)\Bigr)
 \le p^\alpha_K(x)+\frac2N .
\]
head: environment
name: Capped diagonal

title: Proof
body_md:
The entries of $D^\alpha_K(x)$ lie in $[1,K+\xi''(1)]$ because $0<u_i\le1$ and $0\le\chi_\alpha\le1$.
The difference of the two matrices is $-\operatorname{diag}((u_i^{-1}-K)_+)+R_\sigma(x)$, of rank at most
$Np^\alpha_K(x)+2$; apply~\eqref{eq:matrix-rank}.

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a} \emph{Uniqueness.} Let $w\in\mathbb{C}^+$ and let $g_1,g_2$ solve
\eqref{eq:hess-pastur} with $\operatorname{Im}g_j<0$. Taking imaginary parts,
$-\operatorname{Im}g_j=(\operatorname{Im}w+a|\operatorname{Im}g_j|)I_j$ with
$I_j=\int\rho(dD)|w+D-ag_j|^{-2}$, so $aI_j<1$. If $g_1\ne g_2$, subtracting the two equations
gives $1=a\int\rho(dD)/[(w+D-ag_1)(w+D-ag_2)]$, which contradicts Cauchy--Schwarz.

\emph{Existence and convergence.} Let $D_N$ be real diagonal matrices with $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$, put
$X_N=D_N-\sqrt a\,W_N$, and let $m_N(z)=N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(X_N-z)^{-1}$ be the Stieltjes transform of
$\operatorname{ESD}(X_N)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-c}, $m_N(z)\to m(z)$ in
probability for every $z\in\mathbb{C}^+$, where $m(z)$ is the solution of~\eqref{eq:matrix-dyson}. Realize
the matrices $W_N$, $N\ge1$, on one probability space. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-a} and the Borel--Cantelli lemma,
$\|W_N\|\le3$ for all large $N$ almost surely, and then $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(X_N),\operatorname{ESD}(D_N))\le3\sqrt a$
by~\eqref{eq:matrix-weyl}; so $(\operatorname{ESD}(X_N))_N$ is almost surely tight. Given a subsequence, a
diagonal argument yields a further subsequence along which, almost surely, $m_N(z_k)\to m(z_k)$ for
every $z_k$ in a countable dense subset of $\mathbb{C}^+$. Along it, almost surely, every weak limit
point of $\operatorname{ESD}(X_N)$ is a probability measure whose Stieltjes transform agrees with $m$ on that set,
hence on $\mathbb{C}^+$; since a Stieltjes transform determines its measure, all limit points coincide
with one probability measure $\mu$, which depends only on $(a,\rho)$. So $\operatorname{ESD}(X_N)\to\mu$ weakly
in probability, and the expected empirical spectral distributions converge to $\mu$ as well. Let
$\nu$ be the image of $\mu$ under $\lambda\mapsto-\lambda$, so that
$\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)\to\nu$. For $w\in\mathbb{C}^+$, the Cauchy transform of $\nu$ is
$g(w)=\int\mu(d\lambda)/(w+\lambda)=\overline{m(-\bar w)}$. Conjugating~\eqref{eq:matrix-dyson} at
the point $-\bar w\in\mathbb{C}^+$ gives~\eqref{eq:hess-pastur}, and $\operatorname{Im}g(w)<0$. Applied
to the diagonal matrices of the quantiles of $\rho$, this shows that~\eqref{eq:hess-pastur} has a
solution for every $\rho\in\mathcal{P}([0,\infty))$; by uniqueness, and since a Cauchy transform
determines its measure, $\nu=\nu[a,\rho]$ is well defined.

\ref{lem:hess-pastur-b} Take $D_N$ with nonnegative entries and $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$, and let
$\delta>0$; by~\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a} the expected empirical spectral distributions of
$\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N$ converge weakly to $\nu$. On $\{\|W_N\|\le2+\delta\}$, $\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N\preceq\sqrt a(2+\delta)I$, so
$\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)$ gives no mass to $(\sqrt a(2+\delta),\infty)$. Write
$D_N=D_N\mathbf{1}_{\{D_N\le s\}}+D_N\mathbf{1}_{\{D_N>s\}}$. The matrix $\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N\mathbf{1}_{\{D_N\le s\}}$
has spectrum in $[-\sqrt a(2+\delta)-s,\infty)$, and subtracting the positive semidefinite matrix
$D_N\mathbf{1}_{\{D_N>s\}}$, of rank $\#\{i:D_{N,ii}>s\}$, moves at most that many eigenvalues below this
point. Hence
$\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)((-\infty,-\sqrt a(2+\delta)-s))\le\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)((s,\infty))$ on the same event.
Taking expectations, using $\mathbb{P}(\|W_N\|>2+\delta)\to0$, and applying the portmanteau theorem
(open sets on the left, the closed set $[s,\infty)$ on the right), we get
$\nu((\sqrt a(2+\delta),\infty))=0$ and $\nu((-\infty,-\sqrt a(2+\delta)-s))\le\rho([s,\infty))$;
let $\delta\downarrow0$.

\ref{lem:hess-pastur-c} Let $\nu_n=\nu[a_n,\rho_n]$ with Cauchy transforms $g_n$. By
\ref{lem:hess-pastur-b} and the tightness of $(\rho_n)$, the family $(\nu_n)$ is tight. Let $\nu^*$
be a subsequential weak limit; its Cauchy transform $g^*$ is the pointwise limit of $g_n$. For
$w\in\mathbb{C}^+$ we have $\operatorname{Im}(w-a_ng_n(w))\ge\operatorname{Im}w$, so the integrands
$D\mapsto(w+D-a_ng_n(w))^{-1}$ are bounded by $1/\operatorname{Im}w$ and converge uniformly on
$[0,\infty)$ to $(w+D-ag^*(w))^{-1}$. Since $\rho_n\to\rho$ weakly, $g^*$
solves~\eqref{eq:hess-pastur} for $(a,\rho)$, and $\operatorname{Im}g^*<0$; by uniqueness
$\nu^*=\nu[a,\rho]$. The uniform continuity follows, because
$[0,A]\times\mathcal{P}([0,B])$ is a compact metric space.

\ref{lem:hess-pastur-d} Take independent copies $(D_i,D_i')$, $i\ge1$, of the pair $(D,D')$,
independent of the matrices $W_N$, and put $D_N=\operatorname{diag}(D_i)_{i\le N}$ and
$D_N'=\operatorname{diag}(D_i')_{i\le N}$. Almost surely $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$ and $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N')\to\rho'$, so by
\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a}, applied conditionally on the diagonals, $\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)$ and
$\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N')$ converge in probability to $\nu[a,\rho]$ and $\nu[a,\rho']$. If
$|D-D'|\le\varepsilon$ almost surely, their L\'evy distance is at most
$\max_i|D_i-D_i'|\le\varepsilon$, by~\eqref{eq:matrix-weyl}. If $\mathbb{P}(D\ne D')\le p$, it is at most
$N^{-1}\#\{i\le N:D_i\ne D_i'\}\to\mathbb{P}(D\ne D')$, by~\eqref{eq:matrix-rank} and the law of large
numbers. Similarly
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N),\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt{a'}\,W_N-D_N))\le|\sqrt a-\sqrt{a'}|(2+\delta)$ on
$\{\|W_N\|\le2+\delta\}$. In each case the bound passes to the limits by the lower
semicontinuity of $d_{\mathrm{L}}$ under weak convergence, along a subsequence with almost sure convergence.

label: lem:matrix-hyp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-hyp}
Let $Q\in(0,1)$, and let $u_{\max}$ be the maximum of $b\mapsto\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}(Q,b)$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
Then $u_{\max}$ is the essential supremum of $U_Q$, and there are $c,\varepsilon_0>0$ such that
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(U_Q^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1}<\varepsilon\bigr)\ge c\,\varepsilon\qquad(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0).
\]
In particular $U=U_Q$ and $a=a_Q$ satisfy~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}.
head: environment
name: The edge hypothesis for the Parisi variables

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\Phi=\Phi_{\zeta_f}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a} the function
$b\mapsto\Phi_{xx}(Q,b)$ is positive and continuous and tends to $0$ at $\pm\infty$, so it attains
its maximum $u_{\max}$ at some $b_0$; it is twice differentiable with
$|\partial_b^2\Phi_{xx}|=|\Phi_{xxxx}|\le C_{34}$. Hence
$u_{\max}-\Phi_{xx}(Q,b)\le\frac12C_{34}(b-b_0)^2$, and if $|b-b_0|\le r_1$, where $r_1>0$ is such
that $\Phi_{xx}(Q,\cdot)\ge u_{\max}/2$ on $[b_0-r_1,b_0+r_1]$,
\[
 \Phi_{xx}(Q,b)^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1}=\frac{u_{\max}-\Phi_{xx}(Q,b)}{\Phi_{xx}(Q,b)\,u_{\max}}
 \le\frac{C_{34}}{u_{\max}^2}(b-b_0)^2 .
\]
Let $X$ be the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta_f$. Its drift is $\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,\theta_t$ with
$\theta_t=\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\bar{\zeta_f}(t)\Phi_x(t,X_t)$ and $|\theta_t|\le\sqrt{\xi''(1)}$. Let
$Z=\exp(-\int_0^Q\theta\,dB-\frac12\int_0^Q\theta^2\,dt)$. By Girsanov's theorem, under the measure
$Z\,d\mathbb{P}$ the variable $X_Q$ is centred Gaussian with variance $\xi'(Q)>0$, and
$\mathbb{E} Z^2\le e^{\xi''(1)}$, because $\exp(-2\int\theta\,dB-2\int\theta^2)$ is a martingale. By
Cauchy--Schwarz, for every Borel set $A$,
$\mathbb{P}(X_Q\in A)\ge e^{-\xi''(1)}\mathbb{P}(\sqrt{\xi'(Q)}\,Z'\in A)^2$ with $Z'$ standard Gaussian. So
$X_Q$ has full support, which gives the first claim, and
$\mathbb{P}(|X_Q-b_0|<s)\ge c_1s^2$ for $s\le1$. Since $U_Q=\Phi_{xx}(Q,X_Q)$, the event
$\{|X_Q-b_0|<\min(r_1,(\varepsilon/C_{34})^{1/2}u_{\max})\}$ is contained in
$\{U_Q^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1}<\varepsilon\}$, whose probability is therefore at least $c\varepsilon$ for
small $\varepsilon$. With $D=U_Q^{-1}+a_Q\chi_Q$ we have $D-\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D=U_Q^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1}$, and
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[(D-\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D)^{-2}\bigr]=\int_0^\infty\mathbb{P}\bigl(D-\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D<y^{-1/2}\bigr)\,dy
 \ge\int_{\varepsilon_0^{-2}}^\infty c\,y^{-1/2}\,dy=\infty .
 \qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the notation of Section~\ref{sec:hess-edge} and parts~\ref{lem:hess-edge-a}--\ref{lem:hess-edge-b},
proved there. Recall that $U\le u_{\max}\le1$, so $U^{-1}\ge1$.

\ref{lem:hess-edge-c} Put $z_2=z''(-a\chi)=2a\mathbb{E} U^3$ and $I=[-a\chi-\frac12,-a\chi+\frac12]$, which
lies in $(s_-,\infty)$ because $-a\chi-s_-=u_{\max}^{-1}\ge1$. For $s\in I$,
$s+D=U^{-1}+(s+a\chi)\ge\frac12U^{-1}$, so
$z''(s)=2a\mathbb{E}[U^3(1+(s+a\chi)U)^{-3}]\ge2a(2/3)^3\mathbb{E} U^3=:c_I$ and
$|z'''(s)|=6a\mathbb{E}(s+D)^{-4}\le96a$. Let $c_0=c_I/2$ and $|\Delta|\le c_0$. Since $z'(-a\chi)=\Delta$ and
$z''\ge c_I$ on $I$, the critical point lies in $I$, and $h:=s^*+a\chi$ satisfies
$|h|\le|\Delta|/c_I\le\frac12$. Taylor's formula at $-a\chi$ gives
$0=z'(s^*)=\Delta+z_2h+R_1$ with $|R_1|\le48ah^2$, and
$z(s^*)=\Delta h+\frac12z_2h^2+R_2$ with $|R_2|\le16a|h|^3$. Since
$\Delta h+\frac12z_2h^2=-\Delta^2/(2z_2)+\frac{z_2}2(h+\Delta/z_2)^2$ and $|h+\Delta/z_2|=|R_1|/z_2$,
\[
 \Bigl|\lambda_++\frac{\Delta^2}{4a\mathbb{E} U^3}\Bigr|=\Bigl|z(s^*)+\frac{\Delta^2}{2z_2}\Bigr|
 \le\frac{(48a)^2h^4}{2z_2}+16a|h|^3\le C|\Delta|^3 ,
\]
with $C$ depending only on $a$ and $\mathbb{E} U^3$.

\ref{lem:hess-edge-d} Let $g$ be the Cauchy transform of $\nu$, and $G(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}(\sigma+D)^{-1}$
for $\sigma>s_-$. The proof of part~\ref{lem:hess-edge-a} in Section~\ref{sec:hess-edge} shows that
every $w>\lambda_+$ satisfies $g(w)=G(s(w))$ and $z(s(w))=w$, where $s(w)=w-ag(w)>s^*$; thus $s(w)$ is
the inverse of the increasing branch of $z$, and $s(w)\downarrow s^*$ as $w\downarrow\lambda_+$. Since
$G'=(z'-1)/a$ and $s'(w)=1/z'(s(w))$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-gprime}
 -g'(w)=\int\frac{\nu(d\lambda)}{(w-\lambda)^2}=\frac{1-z'(s(w))}{a\,z'(s(w))}\qquad(w>\lambda_+).
\end{equation}
Because $z'''<0$, $z''$ is decreasing, so $c_2\le z''\le C_2$ on $[s^*,s^*+1]$. Let $t=w-\lambda_+$ and
$s=s(w)$, and assume $t\le t_0$, so that $s\le s^*+1$. Then $t=\int_{s^*}^sz'\le(s-s^*)z'(s)$ and
$z'(s)\ge c_2(s-s^*)$, so $t\le z'(s)^2/c_2$; and $t\ge c_2(s-s^*)^2/2$, $z'(s)\le C_2(s-s^*)$.
Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrix-zprime}
 \sqrt{c_2t}\le z'(s(w))\le C_2\sqrt{2t/c_2}\qquad(0<t=w-\lambda_+\le t_0).
\end{equation}
\emph{Upper bound.} For $0<\kappa\le t_0$ take $w=\lambda_++\kappa$; every
$\lambda\in[\lambda_+-\kappa,\lambda_+]$ has $w-\lambda\le2\kappa$, so
by~\eqref{eq:matrix-gprime}--\eqref{eq:matrix-zprime}
\[
 \nu([\lambda_+-\kappa,\lambda_+])\le4\kappa^2(-g'(w))\le\frac{4\kappa^2}{a\sqrt{c_2\kappa}}=C_4\kappa^{3/2},
 \qquad C_4:=\frac4{a\sqrt{c_2}} .
\]
\emph{Lower bound.} Put $F(y)=\nu([\lambda_+-y,\lambda_+])$. Then $F(0)=0$, since an atom at $\lambda_+$ would
make $g(w)$ unbounded as $w\downarrow\lambda_+$, while $g(w)=G(s(w))\to G(s^*)<\infty$. As $\nu$ is
carried by $(-\infty,\lambda_+]$, integration by parts gives, for $w=\lambda_++t$,
$-g'(w)=\int_0^\infty2F(y)(t+y)^{-3}\,dy$. If moreover $t\le c_2/(8C_2^2)$, then $z'(s)\le\frac12$
by~\eqref{eq:matrix-zprime}, and~\eqref{eq:matrix-gprime} gives $-g'(w)\ge1/(2az'(s))\ge c_3t^{-1/2}$
with $c_3=\sqrt{c_2/2}/(2aC_2)$. Split the integral at $\Theta t$ and at $y_0=t_0$, where
$\Theta=(16C_4/c_3)^2$; using $F\le1$, $F(y)\le C_4y^{3/2}$ for $y\le t_0$, and monotonicity of $F$,
\[
 c_3t^{-1/2}\le\frac{F(\Theta t)}{t^2}+\frac{4C_4}{\sqrt{\Theta t}}+\frac1{t_0^2}
 =\frac{F(\Theta t)}{t^2}+\frac{c_3}{4\sqrt t}+\frac1{t_0^2}
\]
(if $\Theta t>t_0$ the middle range is empty and the bound still holds). For
$t\le(c_3t_0^2/4)^2$ the last term is at most $c_3/(4\sqrt t)$, so $F(\Theta t)\ge\frac{c_3}2t^{3/2}$.
With
\[
 t_1=\min\Bigl\{t_0,\ \frac{c_2}{8C_2^2},\ \Bigl(\frac{c_3t_0^2}4\Bigr)^2\Bigr\},\qquad
 \kappa_0=\min\{t_0,\Theta t_1\},\qquad c=\frac{c_3}2\Theta^{-3/2},\qquad C=C_4,
\]
this gives $c\kappa^{3/2}\le\nu([\lambda_+-\kappa,\lambda_+])\le C\kappa^{3/2}$ for $0<\kappa\le\kappa_0$.
The constants $c$, $C$, $\kappa_0$ are continuous, strictly positive functions of
$(a,C_2,c_2,t_0)\in(0,\infty)^4$.

\ref{lem:hess-edge-e} Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hyp} gives~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp} for $U=U_Q$, and with
$a=a_Q$ the objects of Section~\ref{sec:hess-edge} are $\nu=\nu_Q$, $\lambda_+=\lambda_+(Q)$ and
$\Delta=\Delta(Q)$, by definition. For continuity, write $z_Q$, $s_-(Q)$, $s^*_Q$ for the objects
attached to $Q$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a},
$\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}(Q,b)\le\overline Ce^{-2|b|}$ and $\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}(Q,0)\ge\underline c$, so
$u_{\max}(Q)$ is a maximum over $|b|\le\frac12\log(\overline C/\underline c)$ of a jointly
continuous function, hence continuous in $Q$. The map $Q\mapsto\operatorname{Law}(U_Q)$ is weakly continuous
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-d}), so $\chi_Q$ and $s_-(Q)$ are continuous.
Fix $(Q_0,s_0)$ with $s_0>s_-(Q_0)$, and write $\sigma=s+a_Q\chi_Q$, so that
$\mathbb{E}(s+D_Q)^{-j}=\mathbb{E}[U_Q^j(1+\sigmaU_Q)^{-j}]$. For $(Q,s)$ near $(Q_0,s_0)$ we have
$\sigma\ge-1/(u_{\max}(Q_0)+2\delta_1)$ and $u_{\max}(Q)\le u_{\max}(Q_0)+\delta_1$ for some
$\delta_1>0$; so the laws of $U_Q$ are carried by $[0,u_{\max}(Q_0)+\delta_1]$, where
$1+\sigma U\ge\delta_1/(u_{\max}(Q_0)+2\delta_1)$. The integrand is therefore bounded and jointly
continuous there, and weak continuity of $\operatorname{Law}(U_Q)$ shows that $z_Q(s)$, $z_Q'(s)$ and $z_Q''(s)$
are jointly continuous near $(Q_0,s_0)$. Since $z_Q'$ is strictly increasing with the unique zero
$s^*_Q$, the strict signs of $z_{Q_0}'(s^*_{Q_0}\pm\delta)$ persist for $Q$ near $Q_0$, so
$Q\mapsto s^*_Q$ is continuous. Hence $\lambda_+(Q)=z_Q(s^*_Q)$ and the quantities $C_2=z_Q''(s^*_Q)$,
$c_2=z_Q''(s^*_Q+1)$ and $t_0=z_Q(s^*_Q+1)-\lambda_+(Q)$ are continuous and positive, and so are the
constants of~\ref{lem:hess-edge-d}. For $Q\inC_f$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c} gives $\Delta(Q)=2\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)/\xi''(Q)\ge0$.
Substituting into~\ref{lem:hess-edge-b} gives $\lambda_+(Q)=0$ if and only if $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)=0$, and
into~\ref{lem:hess-edge-c}, for $|\Delta(Q)|\le c_0$,
$\lambda_+(Q)=-\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^2/(\xi''(Q)^3\mathbb{E}U_Q^3)+O(\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^3)$, with a constant
depending only on $\xi''(Q)$ and $\mathbb{E}U_Q^3$.

label: lem:matrix-tilt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-tilt}
Let $a>0$, and let $U$ be a $(0,1]$-valued random variable on a probability space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,P_0)$ with $P_0$-essential supremum $u_{\max}$ and
$\mathbb{E}_0[(U^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1})^{-2}]=\infty$. Let $\mathcal R$ be a bounded random variable with
$\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R=0$, let $\eta_0=1/(2\|\mathcal R\|_\infty)$ (any $\eta_0>0$ if $\mathcal R=0$), and
for $\eta\in[0,\eta_0]$ let $dP_\eta=(1-\eta\mathcal R)\,dP_0$, $\chi_\eta=\mathbb{E}_\eta U$,
$\rho_\eta=\operatorname{Law}_{P_\eta}(U^{-1}+a\chi_\eta)$, $\nu^{(\eta)}=\nu[a,\rho_\eta]$ and
$\lambda_+^{(\eta)}=\sup\operatorname{supp}\nu^{(\eta)}$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:matrix-tilt-a} Each $P_\eta$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}, so
 Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge} applies to $\nu^{(\eta)}$.
\item\label{lem:matrix-tilt-b} The maps $\eta\mapsto\lambda_+^{(\eta)}$ and
 $\eta\mapsto(C_2,c_2,t_0)(\eta)$, the latter defined as in
 Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-d}, are continuous on $[0,\eta_0]$, the latter with
 values in $(0,\infty)^3$.
\item\label{lem:matrix-tilt-c} There are $0<c_\sharp\le C_\sharp$ and $\kappa_\sharp>0$ such that,
 for all $\eta\in[0,\eta_0]$ and $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_\sharp]$,
 \[
  c_\sharp\kappa^{3/2}\le\nu^{(\eta)}\bigl([\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-\kappa,\lambda_+^{(\eta)}]\bigr)\le C_\sharp\kappa^{3/2}.
 \]
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Uniformity under bounded tilts

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:matrix-tilt-a} The density $1-\eta\mathcal R$ lies in $[\frac12,\frac32]$, so $P_\eta$
and $P_0$ have the same null sets, $U$ has essential supremum $u_{\max}$ under $P_\eta$, and with
$D=U^{-1}+a\chi_\eta$,
$\mathbb{E}_\eta[(D-\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D)^{-2}]=\mathbb{E}_\eta[(U^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1})^{-2}]\ge\frac12\mathbb{E}_0[(U^{-1}-u_{\max}^{-1})^{-2}]=\infty$.

\ref{lem:matrix-tilt-b} Let $z_\eta$ be the edge function of $\nu^{(\eta)}$. The substitution
$\sigma=s+a\chi_\eta$ maps its domain $s>-(u_{\max}^{-1}+a\chi_\eta)$ onto $\sigma>-u_{\max}^{-1}$,
for every $\eta$, and
\[
 z_\eta(\sigma-a\chi_\eta)=\hat z_\eta(\sigma)-a\chi_\eta,\qquad
 \hat z_\eta(\sigma):=\sigma+a\,\mathbb{E}_0\Bigl[\frac{1-\eta\mathcal R}{\sigma+U^{-1}}\Bigr].
\]
For $k\le2$, $\partial_\sigma^k\hat z_\eta(\sigma)$ is affine in $\eta$, with coefficients that are
bounded continuous functions of $\sigma\ge\sigma_1$ for every $\sigma_1>-u_{\max}^{-1}$, by dominated
convergence with the bound $\|\mathcal R\|_\infty^j(\sigma_1+u_{\max}^{-1})^{-1-k}$. So
$\hat z_\eta$, $\hat z_\eta'$ and $\hat z_\eta''$ are jointly continuous on
$[0,\eta_0]\times(-u_{\max}^{-1},\infty)$, and $\chi_\eta=\chi_0-\eta\mathbb{E}_0[\mathcal RU]$ is
continuous. By Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-a}, $\hat z_\eta'$ is strictly
increasing with a unique zero $\sigma^*_\eta$, and the strict signs of
$\hat z_{\eta_1}'(\sigma^*_{\eta_1}\pm\delta)$ persist for $\eta$ near $\eta_1$; so
$\eta\mapsto\sigma^*_\eta$ is continuous. Derivatives in $s$ and in $\sigma$ coincide, so
$\lambda_+^{(\eta)}=\hat z_\eta(\sigma^*_\eta)-a\chi_\eta$, $C_2(\eta)=\hat z_\eta''(\sigma^*_\eta)$,
$c_2(\eta)=\hat z_\eta''(\sigma^*_\eta+1)$ and
$t_0(\eta)=\hat z_\eta(\sigma^*_\eta+1)-\hat z_\eta(\sigma^*_\eta)$ are continuous; the last three
are positive because $\hat z_\eta''>0$.

\ref{lem:matrix-tilt-c} The constants $c$, $C$, $\kappa_0$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-d} are continuous positive functions of
$(a,C_2,c_2,t_0)$. On the compact interval $[0,\eta_0]$ put $c_\sharp=\min_\eta c(\eta)$,
$C_\sharp=\max_\eta C(\eta)$ and $\kappa_\sharp=\min_\eta\kappa_0(\eta)$.
head: environment

label: lem:matrix-uniform
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-uniform}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For every $K,\eta,M>0$ there is $N_0$ such that, for $N\ge N_0$, outside an event of
outer probability at most $e^{-MN}$,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{L}}\Bigl(\operatorname{ESD}\bigl(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D\bigr),\nu[\xi''(q_x),\operatorname{ESD}(D)]\Bigr)\le\eta
 \qquad\text{for every } x\in[-1,1]^N \text{ and } D\in\mathcal D_K .
\]
head: environment
name: Uniform spectral estimate

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof has four steps: two uniform events, a concentration bound at a fixed pair $(x,D)$ for a
finite family of test functions, a union bound over a net, and interpolation between net points.

\emph{Step 1: two uniform events.} Let $C^H_2,C^H_3$ be given by
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-third}\ref{lem:matrix-third-b} with $M+1$ in place of $M$, and let
$\Omega_2=\{\sup_{[-1,1]^N}\|\nabla^2H_N\|\le C^H_2\}$ and $\Omega_3=\{\sup_{[-1,1]^N}\|D^3H_N\|\le C^H_3N^{-1/2}\}$.
Each fails with probability at most $e^{-(M+1)N}$.

\emph{Step 2: a fixed pair.} Let $h\in(0,1)$, $J=[-\ell,\ell]$ with $\ell=C^H_2+K+2\sqrt{\xi''(1)}+1$, and
$\varphi_y(\lambda)=\min\{1,\max\{0,(y+h-\lambda)/h\}\}$ for $y$ in a grid $\mathcal G\subset[-\ell,\ell+h]$ of
mesh $h$. If two probability measures carried by $J$ satisfy
$|\int\varphi_y\,d\mu-\int\varphi_y\,d\mu'|\le h$ for every $y\in\mathcal G$, then
$\mu((-\infty,t])\le\int\varphi_y\,d\mu\le\int\varphi_y\,d\mu'+h\le\mu'((-\infty,t+2h])+h$ for the grid
point $y\in[t,t+h]$, and symmetrically; so $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mu,\mu')\le2h$.

Fix $x\in[-1,1]^N$ and $D\in\mathcal D_K$, and put $a=\xi''(q_x)$. The Hessian $\nabla^2H_N(x)$ is a
centred Gaussian vector in the space of symmetric matrices with the Frobenius inner product, and
by~\eqref{eq:matrix-hess-cov} its covariance operator has norm at most $C_H/N$; so it is the image of a
standard Gaussian vector under a linear map of operator norm at most $(C_H/N)^{1/2}$. By the
Hoffman--Wielandt inequality \cite{HW} and Cauchy--Schwarz, $A\mapsto N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\varphi_y(A-D)$ is
$h^{-1}N^{-1/2}$-Lipschitz in the Frobenius norm. Gaussian concentration \cite{Ledoux} therefore
gives
\[
 \mathbb{P}\Bigl(\Bigl|\frac1N\operatorname{tr}\varphi_y\bigl(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D\bigr)-\mathbb{E}[\,\cdot\,]\Bigr|>\frac h2\Bigr)
 \le2\exp\Bigl(-\frac{h^4N^2}{8C_H}\Bigr).
\]
By the decomposition of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-third}\ref{lem:matrix-third-a},
\eqref{eq:matrix-rank} and~\eqref{eq:matrix-monotone}, the expectation differs by at most $2/N$
from $\mathbb{E} N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\varphi_y(\sqrt a\,W_N-D)$. We claim that for $N\ge N_1(h,K)$, uniformly in
$a\in[0,\xi''(1)]$, $D\in\mathcal D_K$ and $y\in\mathcal G$,
\[
 \Bigl|\mathbb{E}\frac1N\operatorname{tr}\varphi_y\bigl(\sqrt a\,W_N-D\bigr)-\int\varphi_y\,d\nu[a,\operatorname{ESD}(D)]\Bigr|\le\frac h4 .
\]
Otherwise there are $N_k\to\infty$, $a_k$, $D_k\in\mathcal D_K$ and $y_k$ violating it; passing to a
subsequence, $a_k\to a$, $\operatorname{ESD}(D_k)\to\rho\in\mathcal{P}([0,K])$ and $y_k=y$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a} the expected empirical spectral distribution of
$\sqrt a\,W_N-D_k$ converges to $\nu[a,\rho]$, and by~\eqref{eq:matrix-weyl} and
$\mathbb{P}(\|W_N\|>3)\le2e^{-N/4}$ the same holds for $\sqrt{a_k}\,W_N-D_k$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-c}, $\nu[a_k,\operatorname{ESD}(D_k)]\to\nu[a,\rho]$.
Since $\varphi_y$ is bounded and continuous, both integrals converge to the same limit, a
contradiction.

\emph{Step 3: a net.} Let $\mathcal N_x\subset[-1,1]^N$ be an $\epsilon_0\sqrt N$-net of the cube in the
Euclidean norm, with $|\mathcal N_x|\le(6/\epsilon_0)^N$, and let $\mathcal N_D\subset\mathcal D_K$ be
an $\epsilon_0$-net in the supremum norm, with $|\mathcal N_D|\le(K/\epsilon_0+1)^N$. By Step 2, for
$N\ge\max(N_1,8/h)$, the probability that some $(y,D')\in\mathcal N_x\times\mathcal N_D$ and some
$y_0\in\mathcal G$ have
$|N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\varphi_{y_0}(\nabla^2H_N(y)-D')-\int\varphi_{y_0}\,d\nu[\xi''(q_y),\operatorname{ESD}(D')]|>h$ is at most
$e^{CN}e^{-h^4N^2/(8C_H)}\le e^{-(M+1)N}$ for large $N$. Outside this event and on $\Omega_2$, both
$\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2H_N(y)-D')$ and $\nu[\xi''(q_y),\operatorname{ESD}(D')]$ are carried by $J$, the latter by
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-b} (its support lies in
$[-K-2\sqrt{\xi''(1)},2\sqrt{\xi''(1)}]$); so their L\'evy distance is at most $2h$ for every net
pair.

\emph{Step 4: interpolation.} Let $x\in[-1,1]^N$ and $D\in\mathcal D_K$, and pick a net pair $(y,D')$
with $|x-y|\le\epsilon_0\sqrt N$ and $\|D-D'\|\le\epsilon_0$. On $\Omega_3$,
$\|(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D)-(\nabla^2H_N(y)-D')\|\le(C^H_3+1)\epsilon_0$, which by~\eqref{eq:matrix-weyl} moves
the empirical spectral distribution by at most $(C^H_3+1)\epsilon_0$ in L\'evy distance. For the
targets, Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-d}, with the diagonal entries of $D$ and
$D'$ coupled through a uniform index, gives
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[\xi''(q_y),\operatorname{ESD}(D')],\nu[\xi''(q_x),\operatorname{ESD}(D)])\le\epsilon_0+2|\sqrt{\xi''(q_y)}-\sqrt{\xi''(q_x)}|$,
and $|q_x-q_y|\le2\epsilon_0$. Choose $h$ and $\epsilon_0$ such that
$(C^H_3+2)\epsilon_0+2h+2\omega(2\epsilon_0)\le\eta$, where $\omega$ is the modulus of continuity of
$\sqrt{\xi''}$ on $[0,1]$. The bad event is contained in the union of $\Omega_2^c$, $\Omega_3^c$ and
the event of Step 3, whose probability is at most $3e^{-(M+1)N}\le e^{-MN}$.
head: environment

label: step:matrix-bulk-K
title: Proof
body_md:
Write $u=u_{\zeta_f}$ and $a_t=\xi''(t)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b},
$u$ is uniformly continuous on $[0,1]\times[-1,1]$; let $\omega_u$ be its modulus for the distance
$|t-t'|+|m-m'|$. For $K\ge1$ the function $\psi_K=1/\max(u,K^{-1})=\min(u^{-1},K)$ has modulus at
most $K^2\omega_u$, because $y\mapsto1/\max(y,K^{-1})$ is $K^2$-Lipschitz on $[0,1]$. For
$(Q,\mu)\in\mathcal K$ let $\rho_K(Q,\mu)$ be the law of $\psi_K(Q,m)+a_Q\int u(Q,\cdot)\,d\mu$ under
$m\sim\mu$. Fix $\kappa>0$ and choose, in order:
\begin{steplist}
\item\label{step:matrix-bulk-K} $K\ge1$ with
 $\sup_{(Q,\mu)\in\mathcal K}\mu(\{m:u(Q,m)\le4/K\})\le\kappa/8$. This is possible because
 $(Q,\mu)\mapsto\mu(\{u(Q,\cdot)\le\epsilon\})$ is upper semicontinuous (the set
 $\{(t,m):u(t,m)\le\epsilon\}$ is closed) and decreases, as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, to
 $\mu(\{u(Q,\cdot)=0\})=\mu(\{-1,1\})=0$; on the compact set $\mathcal K$ the convergence is uniform
 (Dini).
\item\label{step:matrix-bulk-E} The event of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-uniform} with
 $(K+\xi''(1),\kappa/8,M+1)$ in place of $(K,\eta,M)$; let $\Omega_E$ be its complement.
\item\label{step:matrix-bulk-w} $w\in(0,r_0/2]$ so small that $(K^2+\xi''(1))\,\omega_S(w)\le\kappa/8$
 and $\omega_S(w)\le1/K$, with $\omega_S$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-orderstab}; that
 $\tau_2(w):=K(\omega_u(2w^{1/2})+w^{1/2})\le\kappa/8$; and that
 \[
  \tau_1(w):=\Bigl(K^2\omega_u(2w^{1/2})+Kw^{1/2}+\xi''(1)\bigl(\omega_u(2w^{1/2})+w^{1/2}\bigr)+\xi'''(1)w\Bigr)^{1/2}
 \]
 and $\xi'''(1)w$ have sum so small that the modulus of uniform continuity in
 Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-c} on $[0,\xi''(1)]\times\mathcal{P}([0,K+\xi''(1)])$
 is at most $\kappa/8$.
\end{steplist}
Now let $N\ge8/\kappa$ be large, and on $\Omega_E$ take $(Q,\mu)\in\mathcal K$, $x\in(-1,1)^N$ and
$\alpha$ satisfying the three window conditions; put $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. Note
$|q_x-Q|\le w\le r_0/2$, so $q_x\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*,widest=f,topsep=3pt,itemsep=2pt]
\item By Corollary~\ref{cor:matrix-truncated},
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2_\sigma F_\alpha(x)),\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D^\alpha_K(x)))\le p^\alpha_K(x)+2/N$.
\item By Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-uniform}, since $D^\alpha_K(x)\in\mathcal D_{K+\xi''(1)}$,
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2H_N(x)-D^\alpha_K(x)),\nu[a_{q_x},\operatorname{ESD}(D^\alpha_K(x))])\le\kappa/8$.
\item By Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-orderstab} at $t=q_x$,
 $\sup_m|u_\alpha(q_x,m)-u(q_x,m)|\le\omega_S(w)$. Since $y\mapsto\min(y^{-1},K)$ is
 $K^2$-Lipschitz on $(0,1]$ and $|\chi_\alpha(x)-\chi_{\zeta_f}(x)|\le\omega_S(w)$, the diagonal
 matrices $D^\alpha_K(x)$ and $D^{\zeta_f}_K(x)$ differ by at most $(K^2+\xi''(1))\omega_S(w)\le\kappa/8$
 entrywise, and Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-d} moves the target by at most
 $\kappa/8$.
\item Couple $m\sim\mu_x$ and $m'\sim\mu$ with $\mathbb{E}|m-m'|\le w$. On $\{|m-m'|\le w^{1/2}\}$ the
 points $(q_x,m)$ and $(Q,m')$ are within distance $2w^{1/2}$, and the complement has probability
 at most $w^{1/2}$. Hence $\mathbb{E}|\psi_K(q_x,m)-\psi_K(Q,m')|\le K^2\omega_u(2w^{1/2})+Kw^{1/2}$ and
 $\mathbb{E}|u(q_x,m)-u(Q,m')|\le\omega_u(2w^{1/2})+w^{1/2}$; also $|a_{q_x}-a_Q|\le\xi'''(1)w$. Since
 $\operatorname{ESD}(D^{\zeta_f}_K(x))$ is the law of $\psi_K(q_x,m)+a_{q_x}\int u(q_x,\cdot)\,d\mu_x$,
 \eqref{eq:matrix-coupling} gives $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(D^{\zeta_f}_K(x)),\rho_K(Q,\mu))\le\tau_1(w)$, and the
 choice of $w$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-c} give
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[a_{q_x},\operatorname{ESD}(D^{\zeta_f}_K(x))],\nu[a_Q,\rho_K(Q,\mu)])\le\kappa/8$.
\item The variables $\psi_K(Q,m')+c$ and $u(Q,m')^{-1}+c$, with $c=a_Q\int u(Q,\cdot)\,d\mu$, differ
 only when $u(Q,m')<1/K$. Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-d} and the choice of $K$
 give $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[a_Q,\rho_K(Q,\mu)],\nu[a_Q,\rho_{Q,\mu}])\le\kappa/8$.
\item Since $\sup_m|u_\alpha(q_x,m)-u(q_x,m)|\le1/K$, every $i$ with $u_\alpha(q_x,x_i)<1/K$ has
 $u(q_x,x_i)<2/K$. Let $\phi(t,m)=\min\{1,\max\{0,3-Ku(t,m)\}\}$, which equals one where
 $u\le2/K$, vanishes where $u\ge3/K$, and is $K$-Lipschitz in $u$. With the coupling of (d),
 \[
  p^\alpha_K(x)\le\int\phi(q_x,\cdot)\,d\mu_x\le\mathbb{E}\phi(Q,m')+K\mathbb{E}\bigl|u(q_x,m)-u(Q,m')\bigr|
 \]
 and the last sum is at most $\mu(\{u(Q,\cdot)\le3/K\})+\tau_2(w)\le\kappa/4$.
\end{enumerate}
By the triangle inequality,
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2_\sigma F_\alpha(x)),\nu[\xi''(Q),\rho_{Q,\mu}])\le\frac\kappa4+\frac2N+\frac{4\kappa}8<\kappa$.
The exceptional event is $\Omega_E^c$, of outer probability at most $e^{-(M+1)N}\le e^{-MN}$.
