label: lem:matrix-band
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-band}
Let $Q\inC_f$ and $\hat\zeta=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f$. Then $\hat\zeta$ is the unique minimizer of
$\beta\mapsto V_\beta(Q,L_{Q})$ over $\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$. In particular
$V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(Q,L_{Q})=V_{\zeta_f}(Q,L_{Q})$.
head: environment
name: The band problem at a contact

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Uniqueness.} At a contact $\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(Q)=Q$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}), that is, $\int m^2\,L_{Q}(dm)=Q$. For such
$\mu$, Chen, Panchenko and Subag define the TAP correction $\mathrm{TAP}(\mu,\beta)$ \cite[(2.24)]{CPS}
with the terminal value $\log(2\cosh)$; hence $\mathrm{TAP}(\mu,\beta)=V_\beta(Q,\mu)+\log2$. They prove
that its infimum over $\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ is attained at a unique point
\cite[(2.26) and Theorem~12(i), (iii)]{CPS}. Since the conjugate is even in $m$, only the law of
$|m|$ under $\mu$ enters there; under $L_{Q}$ this law is not carried by $\{0,1\}$, because $X_Q$
has full support (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hyp}) and $\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(Q,\cdot)$ maps $\mathbb{R}$ onto
$(-1,1)$. Their model class \cite[(1.2)]{CPS} contains every mixture with
$\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$, that is, every $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. So $\beta\mapsto V_\beta(Q,L_{Q})$ has
at most one minimizer over $\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$.

\emph{Convexity.} For a step coefficient $c$ on $[Q,1)$ with values in $[0,1]$, the verification
identity of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-b} writes $W[c,\log\cosh](Q,y)$ as the maximum
over bounded progressively measurable controls $u$ of
$\mathbb{E}\log\cosh\bigl(y+\int_Q^1\xi''cu\,dr+\int_Q^1\sqrt{\xi''}\,dB\bigr)-\frac12\mathbb{E}\int_Q^1\xi''cu^2\,dr$.
For fixed $u$ this is jointly convex in $(c,y)$, so the maximum is jointly convex, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i} this persists for measurable coefficients.
A partial infimum of a jointly convex function is convex, so $c\mapsto\inf_y\{W[c](Q,y)-my\}$ is
convex. Since $\beta\mapsto\bar{\beta}$ is affine and
$\Phi_\beta(Q,\cdot)=W[\bar{\beta}|_{[Q,1)},\log\cosh](Q,\cdot)$, the map $\beta\mapsto V_\beta(Q,\mu)$ is
convex on $\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ for every $\mu$.

\emph{First variation.} Let $\mu=L_{Q}$, $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$, and
$\beta_\epsilon=\hat\zeta+\epsilon(\alpha-\hat\zeta)$ for $\epsilon\in(0,1]$. By convexity,
$V_\alpha(Q,\mu)-V_{\hat\zeta}(Q,\mu)\ge\epsilon^{-1}(V_{\beta_\epsilon}(Q,\mu)-V_{\hat\zeta}(Q,\mu))$. For
$y\in\mathbb{R}$ let $Y^y$ be the Auffinger--Chen process of the coefficient $\bar{\hat\zeta}=\bar{\zeta_f}$ on
$[Q,1]$ started at $(Q,y)$, and $\Gamma^y(r)=\mathbb{E}\,\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(r,Y^y_r)^2$. The left inequality of the
coefficient sandwich (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef}, extended to measurable coefficients by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}) gives
$\Phi_{\beta_\epsilon}(Q,y)-\Phi_{\hat\zeta}(Q,y)\ge\frac\epsilon2\int_Q^1\xi''(r)(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\hat\zeta})(r)\Gamma^y(r)\,dr$.
Evaluating at $y=b_\epsilon(m):=b_{\beta_\epsilon}(Q,m)$, where the infimum defining
$\Phi^{*}_{\beta_\epsilon}(Q,m)$ is attained, and bounding $\Phi^{*}_{\hat\zeta}(Q,m)$ from above by
the value at the same point,
\[
 \frac{V_{\beta_\epsilon}(Q,\mu)-V_{\hat\zeta}(Q,\mu)}\epsilon
 \ge\frac12\int\mu(dm)\int_Q^1\xi''(r)(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\hat\zeta})(r)\,\Gamma^{b_\epsilon(m)}(r)\,dr
 -\frac12\int_Q^1r\xi''(r)(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\hat\zeta})(r)\,dr .
\]
As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $b_\epsilon(m)\to b_{\hat\zeta}(Q,m)$ for $|m|<1$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-orderstab} and the strict monotonicity of $\Phi_{\hat\zeta,x}(Q,\cdot)$; and
$y\mapsto\Gamma^y(r)$ is continuous, since the drift of $Y^y$ is Lipschitz in space. By bounded
convergence the right side tends to
$\frac12\int_Q^1\xi''(r)(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\hat\zeta})(r)\bigl(\int\Gamma^{b_{\hat\zeta}(Q,m)}(r)\,\mu(dm)-r\bigr)dr$.
Now $\Phi_{\hat\zeta}(Q,\cdot)=\Phi_{\zeta_f}(Q,\cdot)$, so $b_{\hat\zeta}(Q,M_Q)=X_Q$, where $X$ is the
Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta_f$ and $M_Q=\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(Q,X_Q)\sim\mu$. By strong uniqueness,
$(X_r)_{r\ge Q}$ is the process $Y^{X_Q}$, so $\int\Gamma^{b_{\hat\zeta}(Q,m)}(r)\,\mu(dm)=\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(r)$.
With $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}$, $\mathcal{O}'=-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma_{\zeta_f}-t)$, $\mathcal{O}(1)=0$, and
$(\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\hat\zeta})(r)=(\alpha-\hat\zeta)([Q,r])$ for $r\ge Q$, Fubini's theorem turns the
limit into
\[
 -\int_Q^1\mathcal{O}'(r)\,(\alpha-\hat\zeta)([Q,r])\,dr=\int_{[Q,1]}\mathcal{O}\,d(\alpha-\hat\zeta)
 =\int_{[Q,1]}\bigl(\mathcal{O}-\mathcal{O}(Q)\bigr)\,d\alpha\ \ge0 .
\]
Here we used Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}: $\mathcal{O}\ge\mathcal{O}_{\min}=\mathcal{O}(Q)$ on
$[Q,1]\subset(0,1]$, and $\hat\zeta$ is carried by $\{Q\}\cup(\operatorname{supp}\zeta_f\cap(Q,1])\subsetC_f$, where
$\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\min}$. Hence $V_\alpha(Q,\mu)\ge V_{\hat\zeta}(Q,\mu)$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$, and
$\hat\zeta$ is the minimizer. Finally $V_{\zeta_f}=V_{\hat\zeta}$ at $(Q,\mu)$, by the remark
after~\eqref{eq:matrix-split}.
head: environment

label: cor:matrix-tilted
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:matrix-tilted}
Let $Q\inC_f$, $M=\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(Q,\cdot)$ and $\pi_0=\operatorname{Law}(X_Q)$. For every $x\in[-1,1]^N$ and every
probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathbb{R}$,
\[
 0\le\frac{F_{\zeta_f}(x)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)}N\le4C_*\,d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\pi,\pi_0)+2L_1|q_x-Q|+2L_2\,\varrho\bigl(W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi)\bigr).
\]
If moreover $x_i=M(b_i)$ for all $i$, $\int M^2\,d\pi=Q$, and the empirical law of the $b_i$ is
within quadratic Wasserstein distance $w\le2$ of $\pi$, then $W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi)\le w$ and
$|q_x-Q|\le2w$, so the right side is at most $4C_*d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\pi,\pi_0)+(4L_1+2L_2)\varrho(w)$.
head: environment
name: The fixed order parameter is nearly optimal near a contact

title: Proof
body_md:
By~\eqref{eq:matrix-split}, $F_{\zeta_f}(x)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)=N[V_{\zeta_f}(q_x,\mu_x)-V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(q_x,\mu_x)]\ge0$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-correction}\ref{lem:matrix-correction-b}, applied to $V_{\zeta_f}$ and to
$V_{\mathrm{TAP}}$, moves $(q_x,\mu_x)$ to $(Q,M_\#\pi)$ at cost
$2L_1|q_x-Q|+2L_2\varrho(W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi))$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-correction}\ref{lem:matrix-correction-a},
$|V_\beta(Q,M_\#\pi)-V_\beta(Q,L_{Q})|\le2C_*d_{\mathrm{TV}}(M_\#\pi,M_\#\pi_0)\le2C_*d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\pi,\pi_0)$
for every $\beta$, and the same holds for $V_{\mathrm{TAP}}$. Since
$V_{\zeta_f}(Q,L_{Q})=V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(Q,L_{Q})$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-band}, the first claim
follows. For the second, $M$ is $1$-Lipschitz because $0<\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}\le1$, so
$W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi)\leW_1(N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{b_i},\pi)\le w$; and $|m^2-m'^2|\le2|m-m'|$ on
$[-1,1]$ gives $|q_x-Q|\le2w$. Finally $w\le\varrho(w)$ on $[0,2]$.
head: environment

label: lem:matrix-own
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:matrix-own}
For every $\tau>0$ there is $\gamma>0$ such that, for all $Q\inC_f$, $r\in[0,1]$,
$\mu\in\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with
\[
 |r-Q|\le\gamma,\qquadW_1(\mu,L_{Q})\le\gamma,\qquad V_\alpha(r,\mu)\le V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(r,\mu)+\gamma ,
\]
one has $\int_r^1|\bar{\alpha}(t)-\bar{\zeta_f}(t)|\,dt\le\tau$.
head: environment
name: Near-minimizers of the band problem

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose not. Then there are $\tau>0$ and, for every $n$, $Q_n\inC_f$ and $(r_n,\mu_n,\alpha_n)$
satisfying the three conditions with $\gamma=1/n$ but
$\int_{r_n}^1|\bar{\alpha_n}-\bar{\zeta_f}|>\tau$. Passing to a subsequence, $Q_n\to Q\inC_f$, because
$C_f$ is compact (Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}), and $\alpha_n\to\alpha$
weakly, so that $\bar{\alpha_n}\to\bar{\alpha}$ in $L^1$. Then $r_n\to Q$ and, since
$t\mapstoL_{t}$ is $W_1$-continuous (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-d}),
$W_1(\mu_n,L_{Q})\to0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-correction}\ref{lem:matrix-correction-b}--\ref{lem:matrix-correction-c},
$V_{\alpha_n}(r_n,\mu_n)\to V_\alpha(Q,L_{Q})$ and
$V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(r_n,\mu_n)\to V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(Q,L_{Q})$. Hence $V_\alpha(Q,L_{Q})\le V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(Q,L_{Q})$.
Since $V_\alpha(Q,\cdot)=V_{\operatorname{Shift}_Q\alpha}(Q,\cdot)$, the measure $\operatorname{Shift}_Q\alpha$ minimizes the band
problem, and Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-band} gives $\operatorname{Shift}_Q\alpha=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f$, that is,
$\bar{\alpha}=\bar{\zeta_f}$ on $[Q,1]$. Therefore
$\int_{r_n}^1|\bar{\alpha_n}-\bar{\zeta_f}|\le\int_0^1|\bar{\alpha_n}-\bar{\alpha}|+|r_n-Q|\to0$, a
contradiction.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\kappa>0$, let $\gamma>0$ be given by Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-own} with $\tau=\kappa/2$, and
choose $\kappa_1\in(0,\min\{\kappa,\gamma/2,r_0\}]$ such that $W_1(L_{Q},L_{Q'})\le\gamma/2$
whenever $|Q-Q'|\le\kappa_1$; this is possible because $t\mapstoL_{t}$ is uniformly continuous on
$[0,1]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-d}). Let $\delta_1,c>0$ be such that
both parts \ref{thm:struct-i} and~\ref{thm:struct-ii} of Theorem~\ref{thm:struct} hold at accuracy
$\kappa_1$ with these constants, and put $\varepsilon=\min\{\delta_1,\gamma/2\}$. For large $N$,
outside the union of the two exceptional events, of outer probability at most
$2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c/2)}$, let $x\in[-1,1]^N$ and $\alpha$ satisfy
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ and $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$. Then
$\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa_1\le\kappa$ and $W_1(\mu_x,L_{q_x})<\kappa_1\le\kappa$. Pick $Q\inC_f$
with $|q_x-Q|<\kappa_1\le\gamma$; since $\kappa_1\le r_0$, also $q_x\in(r_0,1-r_0)$. Then
$W_1(\mu_x,L_{Q})<\kappa_1+\gamma/2\le\gamma$, and by~\eqref{eq:matrix-split}
$V_\alpha(q_x,\mu_x)-V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(q_x,\mu_x)=(F_\alpha(x)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x))/N\le2\varepsilon\le\gamma$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-own} gives $\int_{q_x}^1|\bar{\alpha}-\bar{\zeta_f}|\le\kappa/2<\kappa$. The
proposition holds with $\varepsilon$ and $c/2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{prop:hess-index-a} The map $Q\mapsto\nu_Q$ is weakly continuous on $(0,1)$: $a_Q$ and
$\chi_Q=\mathbb{E}U_Q$ are continuous, $\operatorname{Law}(U_Q)$ is weakly continuous
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-d}) and
$U_Q>0$, so $\rho_Q$ is weakly continuous, and Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-c}
applies. The edge $\lambda_+$ is continuous by Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-e}. Let
$Q_n\to Q$ in $C_f^\kappa$. For large $n$,
$(\lambda_+(Q_n)-\kappa/2,\infty)\supset(\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa/4,\infty)$, and the portmanteau theorem gives
$\liminf_n\nu_{Q_n}((\lambda_+(Q_n)-\kappa/2,\infty))\ge\nu_Q((\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa/4,\infty))>0$, the last
because $\lambda_+(Q)$ lies in the support. By compactness of $C_f^\kappa$ the infimum
in~\eqref{eq:hess-kappaprime} is positive. For the order of magnitude, the constants $c,C,\kappa_0$
of Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-d} for $\nu_Q$ depend continuously on $Q$ and are
positive, so there are $c_\flat,C_\flat,\kappa_\flat>0$ with $c\ge c_\flat$, $C\le C_\flat$ and
$\kappa_0\ge\kappa_\flat$ for every $Q$ in the compact set $C_f^{\kappa_*}$. Let
$\kappa_{\mathrm{ix}}=\min(\kappa_*,2\kappa_\flat)$. Since $\nu_Q$ is
carried by $(-\infty,\lambda_+(Q)]$, for $\kappa\le\kappa_{\mathrm{ix}}$ and $Q\inC_f^\kappa$,
\[
 c_\flat(\kappa/4)^{3/2}\le\nu_Q\bigl([\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa/4,\lambda_+(Q)]\bigr)
 \le\nu_Q\bigl((\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa/2,\infty)\bigr)\le C_\flat(\kappa/2)^{3/2},
\]
which gives~\ref{prop:hess-index-a} with $c_{\mathrm{ix}}=c_\flat4^{-3/2}/2$ and
$C_{\mathrm{ix}}=C_\flat2^{-3/2}/2$.

\ref{prop:hess-index-b} Let $\kappa'=\kappa'(\kappa)$ and $\eta=\min(\kappa/2,\kappa'/2)$, and
let $\varepsilon,c$ be given by Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iii} at accuracy $\eta$.
Outside its exceptional event, let $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$. Then
$\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\eta\le\kappa$, so $q_x\inC_f^\kappa$. Write $\lambda_+=\lambda_+(q_x)$ and
$\nu=\nu_{q_x}$, and let $H\in\mathcal H_\varepsilon(x)$ be one of the one-sided Hessians, so that
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(H),\nu)\le\eta$. Since $\nu$ is carried by $(-\infty,\lambda_+]$ and $\eta<\kappa$, the
right inequality of~\eqref{eq:hess-levy} gives
\[
 \operatorname{ESD}(H)\bigl((\lambda_++\kappa,\infty)\bigr)\le\nu\bigl([\lambda_++\kappa-\eta,\infty)\bigr)+\eta
 =\eta<\kappa' .
\]
Since $\eta\le\kappa/2$ and $q_x\inC_f^\kappa$, the left inequality gives
\[
 \operatorname{ESD}(H)\bigl((\lambda_+-\kappa,\infty)\bigr)\ge\nu\bigl((\lambda_+-\kappa/2,\infty)\bigr)-\eta
 \ge2\kappa'-\kappa'/2=\tfrac32\kappa' .
\]
The eigenvalue counts are integers. So $\#\{i:\lambda_i(H)>\lambda_+-\kappa\}>\kappa'N$ gives
$\lambda_{\lceil\kappa'N\rceil}(H)>\lambda_+-\kappa$, and
$\#\{i:\lambda_i(H)>\lambda_++\kappa\}<\kappa'N\le\lceil\kappa'N\rceil$ gives
$\lambda_{\lceil\kappa'N\rceil}(H)\le\lambda_++\kappa$. For a compression $H'$ of such an $H$, the
interlacing inequalities before~\eqref{eq:hess-interlace} change each count by at most one, and
cannot increase the count above $\lambda_++\kappa$. The count above $\lambda_+-\kappa$ remains at least
$\frac32\kappa'N-1\ge\lceil\kappa'N\rceil$ once $\kappa'N\ge4$, and the same conclusions follow.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-e}, $\lambda_+$ is uniformly continuous on the compact
set $C_f^{\kappa_*}$. Take $\kappa_{\rm loc}\in(0,\kappa/4]$ with
$|\lambda_+(Q)-\lambda_+(Q')|\le\kappa/2$ whenever $Q,Q'\inC_f^{\kappa_*}$ and
$|Q-Q'|\le\kappa_{\rm loc}$. Let $\kappa'=\kappa'(\kappa/2)$, and apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iii} at accuracy
$\eta=\min(\kappa/4,\kappa'/2,\kappa_{\rm loc})$; this gives $\varepsilon$ and $c$. Outside its
exceptional event, let $x$ be as in the statement, and pick $Q\inC_f$ with $|q_x-Q|<\eta$. The
proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-index}\ref{prop:hess-index-b}, run with $\kappa/2$ in place of
$\kappa$, uses exactly $\eta\le\kappa/4$, $\eta\le\kappa'(\kappa/2)/2$ and
$q_x\inC_f^{\kappa/2}$. It shows that every $H\in\mathcal H_\varepsilon(x)$ has
$\lambda_{\lceil\kappa'N\rceil}(H)\in[\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa/2,\lambda_+(q_x)+\kappa/2]$ and fewer than
$\kappa'N$ eigenvalues above $\lambda_+(q_x)+\kappa/2$, for large $N$. Since
$|\lambda_+(q_x)-\lambda_+(Q)|\le\kappa/2$, the interval lies in $[\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa,\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa]$, and
$\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa\ge\lambda_+(q_x)+\kappa/2$. The description of $\lambda_+(Q)$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-e}.
head: environment

label: prop:matrix-window
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:matrix-window}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-a} and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. There is
$\kappa_{\mathrm w}\in(0,\frac12]$ with the following property. For $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm w}]$ and $\delta>0$ let
$\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$ be the event that some $x\in(-1,1)^N$ satisfies
\[
 \nabla F_{\zeta_f}(x)=0,\qquadF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\delta),\qquad
 \lambda_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}(H)<\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa\ \text{ for every } H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{fix}}(x).
\]
Then for every $c'>0$ and all large $N$, $\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$ contains an event of
probability at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c')}$. Consequently, for no $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm w}]$ are there
$\delta,c>0$ such that, for all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, every $m\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ has
$\lambda_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}(H)\ge\lambda_+(q_m)-\kappa$ for some $H\in\mathcal H^{\mathrm{fix}}(m)$.
head: environment
name: The index window cannot be widened

title: Proof
body_md:
The parameters are chosen in the order: $\kappa_{\mathrm w}$; then $\kappa$, $\delta$ and $c'$; then the tilt
$\eta$; then the cutoff $\delta_c$; then the window $w$; then $N$. The point is that $\kappa_{\mathrm w}$ must
not depend on $\eta$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-tilt} provides this.

\emph{Step 0: uniform edge constants.} If $\Delta(q)>0$ only $\eta=0$ is admissible; set
$\mathcal R=0$. If $\Delta(q)=0$, let $\mathcal R$ and $\eta_0=(2\|\mathcal R\|_\infty)^{-1}$ be as
in Section~\ref{sec:stab-kr}, so that every admissible $\eta$ lies in $(0,\eta_0]$. Under $\pi_0$
the variable $U$ has the law of $U_q$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hyp} gives the hypothesis of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-tilt} with $P_0=\pi_0$. In the notation of Section~\ref{sec:stab-kr},
$\nu^{(\eta)}=\nu[a,\operatorname{Law}_{\pi_\eta}(U^{-1}+a\chi_\eta)]$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-tilt}\ref{lem:matrix-tilt-c} gives $C_\sharp,\kappa_\sharp>0$ with
\[
 \nu^{(\eta)}\bigl([\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-y,\lambda_+^{(\eta)}]\bigr)\le C_\sharp y^{3/2}
 \qquad(\eta\in[0,\eta_0],\ 0<y\le\kappa_\sharp).
\]
Choose $\kappa_{\mathrm w}\in(0,\frac12]$ with $\frac32\kappa_{\mathrm w}\le\kappa_\sharp$ and
$C_\sharp(\frac32)^{3/2}\kappa_{\mathrm w}^{1/2}\le\frac14$.

\emph{Step 1: the bulk at the retained points.} The law $M_\#\pi_\eta$ puts no mass at $\pm1$, and
$u_{\zeta_f}(q,M(b))=U(b)$; so, in the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk},
$\nu[a,\rho_{q,M_\#\pi_\eta}]=\nu^{(\eta)}$. Moreover $\lambda_+^{(\eta)}\le\lambda_+(q)$: for
$\eta=0$ they are equal, and if $\Delta(q)=0$ then $\lambda_+(q)=0$ while $\lambda_+^{(\eta)}\le0$, both by
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-b}, applied under $\pi_\eta$ with
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-tilt}\ref{lem:matrix-tilt-a}.

\emph{Step 2: parameters.} Fix $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm w}]$, $\delta>0$ and $c'\in(0,1)$.
\begin{itemize}
\item Choose an admissible $\eta$ with $\varepsilon_3(\eta)\le c'/4$ and
 $\varepsilon_1(\eta)\le\delta/4$, in the notation of
 \ref{step:stab-k2}--\ref{step:stab-k3}.
\item Choose $\delta_c\in(0,q/2)$ with $\frac12\log(1-\delta_c/q)\ge-c'/4$. By \ref{step:stab-k3}
 there is $w_2>0$ such that
 $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta_c,w)\ge1)\ge\Sigma(f)-3c'/4$ for every
 $w\in(0,w_2]$.
\item Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk} to the one-point set
 $\mathcal K=\{(q,M_\#\pi_\eta)\}$, which lies in $[r_0,1-r_0]\times\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$ because
 $q\inC_f$, with accuracy $\kappa/4$ and exponent $2-\Sigma(f)>0$. This gives $w_H>0$ and, for
 large $N$, a measurable set $E_N$ of probability at most $2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-2)}$, containing the
 exceptional set of the proposition (the union of $\Omega_2^c$, $\Omega_3^c$ and the event of
 Step~3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-uniform}), outside of which the conclusion of the proposition
 holds.
\item By Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-e} choose $w_\lambda>0$ with
 $|\lambda_+(q')-\lambda_+(q)|\le\kappa/4$ whenever $|q'-q|\le2w_\lambda$.
\item Fix $w\in(0,\min\{w_2,w_H/2,w_\lambda\}]$ with $\varepsilon_2(w)\le\delta/4$.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Step 3: the retained points.} By \ref{step:stab-k1}--\ref{step:stab-k2}, every point $x$
retained by $\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta_c,w)$ lies in $(-1,1)^N$, satisfies $\nabla F_{\zeta_f}(x)=0$,
$W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi_\eta)\le w$ and $|q_x-q|\le2w$, and
$|N^{-1}F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-f|\le\delta/2+2N^{-2}\le\delta$ for large $N$.

\emph{Step 4: the spectrum at the retained points.} On $\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}\setminus E_N$ let $x$
be a retained point. Since $|q_x-q|\le w_H$ and $W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi_\eta)\le w_H$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk} with $\alpha=\zeta_f$ and Step 1 give
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)),\nu^{(\eta)})\le\kappa/4$. By the choice of $w_\lambda$ and Step 1,
$\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa\ge\lambda_+(q)-\frac54\kappa\ge\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-\frac54\kappa$. If
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mu_1,\mu_2)\le\epsilon$, then $\mu_1([t,\infty))\le\mu_2([t-\epsilon,\infty))+\epsilon$; and
$\nu^{(\eta)}$ is carried by $(-\infty,\lambda_+^{(\eta)}]$. Hence, by Step 0 and
$\frac32\kappa\le\kappa_\sharp$,
\[
 \operatorname{ESD}\bigl(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)\bigr)\bigl([\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa,\infty)\bigr)
 \le\nu^{(\eta)}\bigl([\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-\tfrac32\kappa,\lambda_+^{(\eta)}]\bigr)+\frac\kappa4
 \le C_\sharp\bigl(\tfrac32\kappa\bigr)^{3/2}+\frac\kappa4\le\frac\kappa2 .
\]
So at most $\kappa N/2$ eigenvalues of either one-sided Hessian are at least $\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa$.
For $\kappa N>2$ we have $\kappa N/2<\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor$, hence
$\lambda_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x))<\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa$. Cauchy interlacing gives
$\lambda_i(H')\le\lambda_i(H)$ for the compression $H'$ and $i\le N-1$, and
$\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor\le N-1$, so the same holds for the compression. With Step 3, $x$ witnesses
$\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$.

\emph{Step 5: probability.} The event $\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}\setminus E_N$ is contained in
$\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$, and by Step~2 its probability is at least
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-7c'/8)}-2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-2)}\ge e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c')}$ for large $N$, since $c'<1$.
This proves the first claim for $c'\in(0,1)$, and hence for every $c'>0$.

For the consequence, suppose that for some $\kappa\le\kappa_{\mathrm w}$ there were such $\delta$ and $c$.
Every witness of $\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$ violates the property in question, so the event of
the first claim with $c'=c/2$, of probability at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c/2)}$, would be contained in
an event of outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, which is impossible for large $N$.

label: prop:kr-main
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:kr-main}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and that $\xi$ has two active degrees, and let
$f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f),
\]
and the witnesses of $\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$ can be taken of the form $(\zeta_f,x)$. More precisely,
the retained points of Appendix~\ref{app:kr-count} have the properties
\ref{step:stab-k1}--\ref{step:stab-k3} listed in Section~\ref{sec:stab-kr}.
head: environment
name: Critical points of the fixed TAP function

label: lem:kr-contact
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The first contact

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:kr-contact-a}--\ref{lem:kr-contact-b} By
Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-a}--\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-b}, $\theta\in(0,1)$,
$\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$ and $\Sigma(f)=\theta(P_\zeta-f)$, and $\zeta$ is unique
(Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-a}). By Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}, $C_f$ is a
compact subset of $(0,1)$ containing $\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$, and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ on
$(0,1]\setminusC_f$. Since $q=\minC_f$, this gives $\zeta((0,q))=0$ and
$\mathcal{O}_\zeta(r)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}=\mathcal{O}_\zeta(q)$ for $0<r<q$. The identities $\Gamma_{\zeta}(q)=q$ and
$\Delta_0=2\mathcal{O}_\zeta''(q)/a\ge0$ are Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}.

\ref{lem:kr-contact-c} This is Remark~\ref{rem:var-level}: by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-c}, $\Lambda'=p+\theta p'$ with $p(\theta)=P_\zeta$ and
$p'(\theta)=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_\zeta(0)-\int\mathcal{O}_\zeta\,d\zeta\bigr)/(1-\theta)=\mathcal{O}_\zeta(0)-\mathcal{O}_\zeta(q)$, since
$\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$ and $\mathcal{O}_\zeta=\mathcal{O}_\zeta(q)$ on $\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$; and $\Lambda'(\theta)=f$
by Proposition~\ref{prop:var-regular}\ref{prop:var-regular-b}.

\ref{lem:kr-contact-d} This is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}--\ref{lem:pde-standing-b},
together with $\Phi_{xx}\le1$, which holds for finitely supported order parameters by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a} with $G=1$ and passes to the limit by the uniform
convergence in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}.

\ref{lem:kr-contact-e} On $[0,q)$ the coefficient $\bar{\zeta}$ equals $\theta$, so
$w(t,b)=e^{\theta\Phi(t,b)}$ solves the backward heat equation $\partial_tw+\frac{\xi''}2w_{xx}=0$
there (the Cole--Hopf form \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} of the Parisi equation on a step). On $[0,q]$
the Auffinger--Chen process, whose drift is $\theta\xi''\Phi_x=\xi''\partial_x\log w$, is the
Doob transform of the Gaussian martingale $\int_0^t\sqrt{\xi''}\,dB$ by $w$. Its law at time $q$
therefore has density $w(q,b)/w(0,0)$ with respect to the law of that martingale at time $q$,
which is $\mathcal N(0,\xi'(q))$ because $\xi'(0)=0$. This is \eqref{eq:kr-law}, the plateau
Cole--Hopf identity of \cite[Lemma~A.3, (A.11)]{Bou26b} with lower endpoint zero. Since
$|\Phi_x|<1$, $|\Phi(q,b)-\Phi(q,0)|\le|b|$, so the density is positive and $\pi_0$ has Gaussian
tails. Differentiating the logarithm of the density gives $-b/c+\theta M(b)$, and
\eqref{eq:kr-ward} follows by integration by parts.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-tilt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-tilt}
Assume $\Delta_0=0$. Let $\mathcal R$ be the residual of $U^2$ after orthogonal projection in
$L^2(\pi_0)$ onto $\operatorname{span}\{1,M^2\}$. Then $\mathcal R$ is bounded and not identically
zero, and $\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R=\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal RM^2=0$ and $\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal RU^2=\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R^2$. For
$0<\eta\le\eta_0:=(2\|\mathcal R\|_\infty)^{-1}$, the measure $\pi_\eta=(1-\eta\mathcal R)\pi_0$ is a
probability measure whose density with respect to $\pi_0$ lies in $[\frac12,\frac32]$, and
\[
 \mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}M^2=q,\qquad
 \Delta_\eta:=1-a\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}U^2=a\eta\,\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R^2>0 .
\]
head: environment
name: Field-law tilt

title: Proof
body_md:
The functions $1$ and $M^2$ are linearly independent in $L^2(\pi_0)$, because $M$ is strictly
increasing and $\pi_0$ has a positive density. All three functions $1,M^2,U^2$ are bounded, so the
projection has bounded coefficients and $\mathcal R$ is bounded. Orthogonality gives
$\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R=\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal RM^2=0$ and $\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal RU^2=\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R^2$, and these give the
normalization, $\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}M^2=\mathbb{E}_0M^2=q$ and $\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}U^2=\mathbb{E}_0U^2-\eta\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal R^2$.
Suppose $\mathcal R=0$ in $L^2(\pi_0)$. By continuity and the full support of $\pi_0$,
$U^2=\bar A+\bar BM^2$ at every field. As $b\to\pm\infty$, $M(b)\to\pm1$ and $U(b)\to0$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-contact}\ref{lem:kr-contact-d}), so $\bar B=-\bar A$, and $\bar A>0$ since
$U>0$. Then $M'=U=\sqrt{\bar A(1-M^2)}$, whose solution reaches $1$ at a finite field, which
contradicts $|M|<1$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-energy
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Energy shift

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $w_p=\beta_p^2q^p/s_0$, a probability vector on the degrees. Then
$\det S_0=s_0^2\operatorname{Var}_w(p)>0$, since two degrees are active. Grouping the numerator of $A$ into
unordered pairs of degrees gives, for $z\in[0,1]$,
\[
 A(qz)=\sum_{p<s}\lambda_{ps}\,\frac{sz^p-pz^s}{s-p},\qquad
 \lambda_{ps}=\frac{w_pw_s(s-p)^2}{\operatorname{Var}_w(p)},\qquad\sum_{p<s}\lambda_{ps}=1 .
\]
For $2\le p<s$, polynomial multiplication verifies
\[
 1-\frac{sz^p-pz^s}{s-p}=(1-z)^2Q_{ps}(z),\qquad
 Q_{ps}(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}(j+1)z^j+\sum_{j=p}^{s-2}\frac{p(s-1-j)}{s-p}\,z^j .
\]
All coefficients of $Q_{ps}$ are nonnegative and its constant coefficient is one, so
$Q_{ps}\ge1$ on $[0,1]$; summing with the weights $\lambda_{ps}$ proves the first inequality in
\eqref{eq:kr-collar}. Each pair has second derivative $-ps$ at $z=1$, so
$qA''(q)=-q^{-1}\sum_{p<s}\lambda_{ps}ps<0$. The series may be differentiated termwise because
$\xi$ has radius of convergence greater than one. Finally, $H_N(x)$ is independent of the part of
$\nablaH_N(x)$ orthogonal to $x$, and its regression on $x\cdot\nablaH_N(x)$ leaves the variance
$N(s_0-s_1^2/s_2)=N\det S_0/s_2$, which is \eqref{eq:kr-sigmaH}.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-endpoints
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-endpoints}
The functions $u,v,T$ are jointly continuous on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$, with $|v|\le C_{34}$ and
$|T|\le(C_{34}+C_{34}^2)\,u$. As $m\to\pm1$, uniformly in $t\in[0,1]$,
\[
 u(t,m)\to0,\qquad v(t,m)\to\mp2,\qquad T(t,m)\to0,
\]
so $u,v,T$ extend to jointly continuous functions on $[0,1]\times[-1,1]$. Moreover $b_t(m)$,
$u(t,m)$ and $\log u(t,m)$ are Lipschitz in $t\in[0,1]$, uniformly in $m\in(-1,1)$.
head: environment
name: Inverse fields up to the boundary

title: Proof
body_md:
The bounds on $v$ and $T$ follow from Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-contact}\ref{lem:kr-contact-d}, since
$|T|\le|\Phi_{xxxx}|+\Phi_{xxx}^2/\Phi_{xx}$. Joint continuity on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$ follows from
the continuity of the spatial derivatives of $\Phi$ and of $b_t(m)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}--\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}). The limit of $u$
is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}, and then $T\to0$ by the bound on $T$.

For $v$, by oddness of $\Phi_x(t,\cdot)$ it suffices to show $v(t,m)\to-2$ as $m\uparrow1$.
Since $b_t(m)\ge\frac12\log\frac{c_1}{2(1-m)}$ for $m\in[0,1)$ (proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}), it suffices to show
$\Phi_{xxx}(t,b)/\Phi_{xx}(t,b)\to-2$ as $b\to\infty$, uniformly in $t$. First let $\zeta'$ be
finitely supported, let $\tilde X$ be its Auffinger--Chen process started at $(t,b)$ and put
$I=\int_t^1\xi''(r)\bar{\zeta'}(r)\Phi_{\zeta',xx}(r,\tilde X_r)\,dr\in[0,V_*]$, $V_*=\xi'(1)$. The
Feynman--Kac formulas in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing} give
\[
 \frac{\Phi_{\zeta',xxx}(t,b)}{\Phi_{\zeta',xx}(t,b)}+2
 =\frac{2\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\,e^{I}\,\bigl(1-\tanh(\tilde X_1)e^{2I}\bigr)\bigr]}
  {\mathbb{E}\bigl[\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\,e^{I}\bigr]} .
\]
Write $\tilde X_r=b+D_r+J_r$ with $|D_r|\le V_*$ and $J_r=\int_t^r\sqrt{\xi''(s)}\,dB_s$, and let
$R>0$ and $b>V_*+R$. On $\{\sup_r|J_r|\le R\}$ the path stays above $b-V_*-R$, so
$I\le V_*C_1e^{-2(b-V_*-R)}$ and $1-\tanh\tilde X_1\le2e^{-2(b-V_*-R)}$; there the last factor in
the numerator is at most $\epsilon(b,R)$, with $\epsilon(b,R)\to0$ as $b\to\infty$ for fixed $R$.
Elsewhere it is at most $1+e^{2V_*}$. The denominator is at least $\mathbb{E}\operatorname{sech}^2(\tilde X_1)\ge
e^{-2b-2V_*}\mathbb{E} e^{-2|J_1|}$, and the numerator restricted to $\{\sup_r|J_r|>R\}$ is at most
$Ce^{-2b}\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{2|J_1|}\mathbf{1}\{\sup_r|J_r|>R\}\bigr]$, with $C$ depending only on $V_*$. By
Cauchy--Schwarz and the Gaussian maximal inequality for $J$, whose variance is at most $V_*$, the
ratio of these two bounds tends to zero as $R\to\infty$, uniformly in $b$, $t$ and $\zeta'$. Taking
$b\to\infty$ and then $R\to\infty$ gives the claim for finitely supported $\zeta'$, uniformly in
$\zeta'$. For $\zeta$ it follows by the uniform convergence of the spatial derivatives along
finitely supported approximations (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}).

Finally, the one-sided derivatives in \eqref{eq:kr-inverse-field} are bounded, and
$|\partial_t^\pm\log u|\le\xi''(1)\bigl(\frac12(C_{34}+C_{34}^2)+1\bigr)$; a continuous function
with bounded one-sided derivatives is Lipschitz.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-block
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-block}
Under \eqref{eq:kr-conditioning}, relative to the decomposition $\mathbb{R} e\oplus e^\perp$, the left
Hessian has the law
\[
 \nabla^2_-F_\zeta(x)\overset{d}{=}
 \begin{pmatrix} r_N+\varsigma Z/\sqrt N & z_N^{\mathsf T}\\ z_N & C_N\end{pmatrix},
\]
where
\begin{align}
 C_N&=P\bigl[\sqrt a\,W_N-\operatorname{diag}(U(b_i)^{-1}+a\chi_N)\bigr]P\big|_{e^\perp},\label{eq:kr-transverse}\\
 z_N&=P\psi_N+\sqrt{\tau/N}\,g,\label{eq:kr-cross}\\
 r_N&=A_2h+B_2d_N-\frac{\langle M^2/U\rangle_N}q-a\chi_N-2a\langle Mv\rangle_N
 -2q\bigl[a\theta+a_1\chi_N+a\langle\dot u\rangle_N\bigr].\label{eq:kr-radial}
\end{align}
Here $W_N$ is a GOE matrix, $g$ a standard Gaussian vector in $e^\perp$ and $Z$ a standard
Gaussian variable, all independent. The right Hessian has the same representation with $\theta$
replaced by $\zeta([0,q])$ in $r_N$ and in $\dot u$.
head: environment
name: Conditional block representation

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\mathcal G=\nablaH_N(x)$ and $\mathcal H=\nabla^2H_N(x)$. Differentiating the covariance
$N\xi(R(y,z))$ gives $\operatorname{Cov}(H_N(x),x\cdot\mathcal G)=NS_0$ and $\operatorname{Cov}(P\mathcal G)=cP$, the two
being independent, and, for unit vectors $u',v'\perp e$,
\begin{gather*}
 \operatorname{Cov}(u'^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He,v'\cdot\mathcal G)=\frac{a\sqrt q}{\sqrt N}\,u'\cdot v',\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(u'^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He,v'^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He)=\frac{a+qa_1}N\,u'\cdot v',\\
 \operatorname{Cov}\bigl(e^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He,(H_N(x),x\cdot\mathcal G)\bigr)=\mathbf t^{\mathsf T},
\end{gather*}
and $\operatorname{Var}(e^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He)=(2a+4qa_1+q^2a_2)/N$. The transverse block
$P\mathcal HP|_{e^\perp}$ has GOE covariance with off-diagonal variance $a/N$ and is uncorrelated
with all conditioned variables, with the cross entries and with the radial entry; the cross
entries are uncorrelated with $H_N(x)$, $x\cdot\mathcal G$ and the radial entry, and the radial
entry with $P\mathcal G$. Gaussian regression, with $P\mathcal G=Pb$ under
\eqref{eq:kr-conditioning}, gives
\[
 P\mathcal He=\frac{a\sqrt q}{c\sqrt N}\,Pb+\sqrt{\tau/N}\,g,\qquad
 e^{\mathsf T}\mathcal He=A_2h+B_2d_N+\varsigma Z/\sqrt N .
\]
Now take $y=x$ and $\sigma=-$ in \eqref{eq:kr-hessian}, where $\bar{\zeta}^-(q)=\theta$ and
$\xi'''(q)\chi_N-\frac{a^2}{2N}\sum_iT(b_i)+a\theta\Delta_N(x)=a\theta+a_1\chi_N+a\langle\dot u\rangle_N$.
Its transverse, cross and radial blocks are \eqref{eq:kr-transverse}--\eqref{eq:kr-radial}; for
the cross block note $P\operatorname{diag}(U^{-1})e=P(M/U)(b_i)_i/\sqrt{Nq}$ and
$\frac aNP\mathbf v_x(x\cdot e)=a\sqrt{q/N}\,P\mathbf v_x$. Complete the transverse GOE block to a
full GOE matrix by independent entries; they do not appear in $PW_N P$. The right Hessian
differs only through $\bar{\zeta}^+(q)=\zeta([0,q])$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-schur
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-schur}
Let $\pi$ have finite exponential moments of every order, with $\mathbb{E}_\pi M^2=q$ and
$\Delta_\pi=1-a\mathbb{E}_\pi U^2>0$, and let $h\to h_\infty$ as $N\to\infty$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:kr-schur-a} Consider anchors whose fields satisfy the cap \eqref{eq:kr-cap}, with
 $W_2(\pi_x,\pi)\to0$ as $N\to\infty$. Under \eqref{eq:kr-conditioning}, with probability tending
 to one, $C_N\preceq-g_0I$ for a constant $g_0>0$ depending only on $a$ and $\Delta_\pi$, and
 \[
  r_N+\varsigma Z/\sqrt N-z_N^{\mathsf T}C_N^{-1}z_N\longrightarrow\mathcal S(\pi,h_\infty)
  \qquad\text{in probability.}
 \]
\item\label{lem:kr-schur-b} If $\mathcal S(\pi,h_\infty)<0$, there is $g>0$ such that, for the
 anchors of~\ref{lem:kr-schur-a}, both one-sided Hessians satisfy $\nabla^2_\pm F_\zeta(x)\preceq-gI$
 with probability tending to one.
\item\label{lem:kr-schur-c} \textup{(Anchors off the sphere.)} Consider anchors $x$ with
 $q_x\to q$ whose fields satisfy \eqref{eq:kr-cap}, with $W_2(\pi_x,\pi)\to0$ as $N\to\infty$, and
 condition on $H_N(x)=Nh$ and $\nabla F_\zeta(x)=0$. Then the conclusions of~\ref{lem:kr-schur-a}
 hold for the blocks of the frozen left Hessian, and, if $\mathcal S(\pi,h_\infty)<0$, the conclusion
 of~\ref{lem:kr-schur-b} holds for the frozen left Hessian.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Radial Schur complement

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:kr-schur-a} Let $\widetilde C_N=\sqrt a\,W_N-\operatorname{diag}(U(b_i)^{-1}+a\chi_N)$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. The empirical laws of the
$U(b_i)$ converge to $\operatorname{Law}_\pi(U)$, a law on $(0,1]$ with mean $\chi_\pi$ and
$1-a\mathbb{E}_\pi U^2=\Delta_\pi>0$. Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gap}\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a}--\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b} gives a gap
$\widetilde C_N\preceq-g_0I$ with probability at least $1-e^{-c_MN}$, the inverse equivalent
$v_N^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_N^{-1}w_N+\sum_iU(b_i)v_{N,i}w_{N,i}\to0$ in probability for vectors
of bounded norm that are deterministic or independent of $W_N$, and
$N^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\widetilde C_N^{-1}\to-\chi_\pi$ (all set to zero off the gap event). The inverse of the
compression $C_N$, extended by zero on $\mathbb{R} e$, is
\[
 K_N=\widetilde C_N^{-1}-\frac{\widetilde C_N^{-1}ee^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_N^{-1}}
 {e^{\mathsf T}\widetilde C_N^{-1}e},
\]
since $K_Ne=0$ and $P\widetilde C_NPK_N=P$. The denominator converges to $-\upsilon_\pi/q<0$. By
the inverse equivalent applied to $\psi_N$ and $e$,
$\psi_N^{\mathsf T}K_N\psi_N\to-\mathbb{E}_\pi(U\psi^2)+[\mathbb{E}_\pi(UM\psi)]^2/\upsilon_\pi$. The rank-one
term of $K_N$ has trace at most $g_0^{-1}$ in absolute value on the gap event, so
$N^{-1}\operatorname{tr} K_N\to-\chi_\pi$. Conditionally on $W_N$, the Gaussian cross term and the centred
quadratic form in $g$ have variance $O(N^{-1})$. Hence
\[
 z_N^{\mathsf T}C_N^{-1}z_N\longrightarrow-\mathbb{E}_\pi(U\psi^2)+\frac{[\mathbb{E}_\pi(UM\psi)]^2}{\upsilon_\pi}
 -\tau\chi_\pi ,
\]
while $\varsigma Z/\sqrt N\to0$ and $r_N$ converges to the corresponding $\pi$-average, by uniform
integrability under the cap. The apparently singular moments of $1/U$ cancel: since
$U\psi^2=M^2/(qU)-2aM\ell+qa^2U\ell^2$, $UM\psi=\sqrt q(-M^2/q+aUM\ell)$ and
$\mathbb{E}_\pi(M\ell)=k_\pi/c-\mathbb{E}_\pi(Mv)$, the limit of the Schur complement is \eqref{eq:kr-schur-generic}.

\ref{lem:kr-schur-b} Take an event of probability tending to one on which
$C_N\preceq-g_0I$, the Schur complement is at most $-s<0$ and $|g|^2\le2N$. There
$\|C_N^{-1}z_N\|\le K_*:=g_0^{-1}(B_\psi+\sqrt{2\tau})$. For $(t,v)\in\mathbb{R}\oplus e^\perp$, with
$\hat r_N=r_N+\varsigma Z/\sqrt N$ and $w=v+tC_N^{-1}z_N$,
\[
 \hat r_Nt^2+2tz_N^{\mathsf T}v+v^{\mathsf T}C_Nv
 =(\hat r_N-z_N^{\mathsf T}C_N^{-1}z_N)t^2+w^{\mathsf T}C_Nw
 \le-\min(s,g_0)(t^2+|w|^2),
\]
and $t^2+|v|^2\le\max(2,1+2K_*^2)(t^2+|w|^2)$. This is a gap for $\nabla^2_-F_\zeta(x)$. The right
Hessian differs by $-\frac2N a\,\zeta(\{q\})\Delta_N(x)\,xx^{\mathsf T}$, which is negative
semidefinite once $\Delta_N(x)\ge0$, and $\Delta_N(x)\to\Delta_\pi>0$.

\ref{lem:kr-schur-c} By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints}, $|b_Q(m)-b_q(m)|\le C|Q-q|$ uniformly in
$m$, so the empirical laws of the fields $b_Q(x_i)$ and $b_q(x_i)=M^{-1}(x_i)$ are within
$W_2$-distance $C|Q-q|$, and \eqref{eq:kr-cap} persists with $L_0$ replaced by
$e^{t_0C|Q-q|}L_0$. The coefficients are smooth in $Q$, and $u,v,T$ are uniformly continuous on
$[q/2,(1+q)/2]\times[-1,1]$. Hence empirical windows formulated with the fixed-radius fields
$\pi_x$ give limiting moments, and values of \eqref{eq:kr-schur-generic}, within $o(1)$ as
$Q\to q$, and the proofs of~\ref{lem:kr-schur-a} and of the left-Hessian part
of~\ref{lem:kr-schur-b} apply to the frozen left Hessian.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-c3
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-c3}
For every $H_0<\infty$ there are $\varepsilon_0,c_3>0$ and $C=C(H_0)$ such that the following holds
for every $N$, every $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with
$|q_x-q|\le\varepsilon_0$ and every value $(Nh',\mathbf y)$ of $(H_N(x),\nablaH_N(x))$ with
$|h'|+N^{-1/2}|\mathbf y|\le H_0$: conditionally on $(H_N(x),\nablaH_N(x))=(Nh',\mathbf y)$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}_{\rm cond}\Bigl(\sup_{z\in[-1,1]^N}\|D^3H_N(z)\|_{\rm op}>\frac C{\sqrt N}\Bigr)\le e^{-c_3N}.
\]
In particular, on the complement, $\|\nabla^2H_N(y)-\nabla^2H_N(x)\|\le
C|y-x|/\sqrt N$ for all $y\in[-1,1]^N$.
head: environment
name: Conditional third derivatives

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $H_N=m_{\rm cond}+G$, with $m_{\rm cond}$ the conditional mean and $G$ the centred conditional
field. Gaussian conditioning decreases pointwise variances and variances of increments, so the
bounds on the pointwise variance and the canonical metric of the trilinear process
$(z,\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)\mapsto D^3H_N(z)[\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3]$ used in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-third}\ref{lem:matrix-third-b} hold for $G$, and that proof gives the bound for
$G$ (Remark~\ref{rem:matrix-conditional}). For the mean,
let $\mathbf Z=(H_N(x)/\sqrt N,\nablaH_N(x))$. Its covariance is uniformly nondegenerate for
$|q_x-q|\le\varepsilon_0$: the part of $\nablaH_N(x)$ orthogonal to $x$ has covariance
$\xi'(q_x)$ times the identity, and the pair $(H_N(x)/\sqrt N,\,x\cdot\nablaH_N(x)/|x|)$ has a
covariance matrix whose determinant is $\det S_0(q_x)/q_x>0$, where $S_0(r)$ is $S_0$ with $q$
replaced by $r$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy}). On the conditioning event
$|\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf Z)^{-1/2}\mathbf Z|\le C\sqrt N$. By Gaussian regression and Cauchy--Schwarz, each
$m_{\rm cond}$-derivative $D^3m_{\rm cond}(z)[\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3]$, $|\varphi_j|=1$, is at most the
unconditional standard deviation of $D^3H_N(z)[\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3]$, which is at most $C/N$
by the variance bound in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-third}\ref{lem:matrix-third-b}, times
$C\sqrt N$. This is the
only place where the nondegeneracy of $\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf Z)$, and hence the second active degree, is
used in this lemma.
head: environment

label: prop:kr-local
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:kr-local}
Let $\pi$ be a law on $\mathbb{R}$ with finite exponential moments of every order and $h\in\mathbb{R}$, such that
\[
 \mathbb{E}_\pi M^2=q,\qquad \Delta_\pi=1-a\mathbb{E}_\pi U^2>0,\qquad \mathcal S(\pi,h)<0,
\]
and fix $L_0>\mathbb{E}_\pi e^{t_0|b|}$. There are $g_*,\rho_*>0$ such that the following hold, where the
suprema are over admissible data of width at most $w$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:kr-local-a} \textup{(Strong concavity on a ball.)}
 \[
  \lim_{w\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{(x,h')}\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}\Bigl(\exists\,y\in(-1,1)^N,\
  |y-x|\le\rho_*\sqrt N,\ \sigma\in\{\pm\}:\ \nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(y)\not\preceq-g_*I\Bigr)=0 .
 \]
\item\label{prop:kr-local-b} \textup{(Typical determinant.)} For every $t>0$,
 \[
  \lim_{w\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{(x,h')}\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}\Bigl(\exists\,\sigma\in\{\pm\}:\
  \Bigl|\frac1N\log\bigl|\det\nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(x)\bigr|-\mathfrak d_\pi\Bigr|>t\Bigr)=0 .
 \]
\end{thmlist}
The constants $g_*,\rho_*$ depend on $\pi$, $h$ and $L_0$ only.
head: environment
name: Strict Hessian bound around a conditioned critical point

title: Proof
body_md:
By the contradiction argument at the end of the proof it suffices to treat sequences of data
whose widths tend to zero; along such a sequence $q_x\to q$, the empirical field laws converge to
$\pi$ in $W_2$, \eqref{eq:kr-cap} holds and $h'\to h$. We work under $\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}$, and all
statements hold with conditional probability tending to one.

\emph{Step 1: a continuous upper envelope.} For $K\ge1$ and $y\in(-1,1)^N$ with $r=q_y>0$, let
$\mathcal M_{N,K}(y)$ be the matrix obtained from \eqref{eq:kr-hessian} by replacing $u_i^{-1}$ with
$\min(u_i^{-1},K)$ and $\bar{\zeta}^\sigma(r)$ with $\theta$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints}, all
coefficient functions of $\mathcal M_{N,K}$ are uniformly continuous functions of $(r,y_i)$ on
$[q/2,(1+q)/2]\times[-1,1]$, across every atom of $\zeta$. If $|y-x|\le\rho\sqrt N$, at most a
fraction $\rho$ of the coordinates have $|y_i-x_i|>\sqrt\rho$, so averages $N^{-1}\sum_i\phi(r,y_i)$
of such functions change by at most $\omega_\phi(\sqrt\rho+|q_y-q_x|)+2\|\phi\|_\infty\rho$. In
particular $\Delta_N(y)\ge\Delta_\pi/2$ for $|y-x|\le\rho_1\sqrt N$ and narrow windows. Since
$\bar{\zeta}^\sigma\ge\theta$, this gives the exact matrix inequality
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-envelope}
 \nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(y)\preceq\mathcal M_{N,K}(y)\qquad(\sigma=\pm,\ |y-x|\le\rho_1\sqrt N).
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 2: the cap keeps the anchor gap.} The matrix $\mathcal M_{N,\infty}(x)$ is the frozen left
Hessian at $x$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-schur}\ref{lem:kr-schur-c} gives $-\mathcal M_{N,\infty}(x)\succeq g_1I$. Write $-\mathcal M_{N,\infty}(x)=A_N-F_N$ with
$A_N=\operatorname{diag}(u_i^{-1}+a\chi_N)-\sqrt a\,W_N$ (the transverse GOE completed as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-block}) and $F_N$ of bounded rank. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-block}, the vectors
spanning the range of $F_N$ are, after normalization by $\sqrt N$, combinations of $x$, $b$,
$(M/U)(b_i)$ and bounded functions of the fields, so \eqref{eq:kr-cap} gives $\|F_N\|\le C$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gap}\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a}, $A_N\succeq g_0I$. A convex combination of
$A_N-F_N\succeq g_1I$ and $A_N-F_N\succeq A_N-CI$ gives
\[
 A_N-F_N\succeq t_*A_N,\qquad t_*=\frac{g_1}{C+g_1}.
\]
Let $A_{N,K}$ be $A_N$ with $u_i^{-1}$ capped at $K$. The capped statement of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gap}\ref{lem:matrix-gap-a} gives $A_{N,K}\succeq g_0'I$ for all large fixed $K$. On $\{\|\sqrt a\,W_N\|\le B\}$ we have
\[
 \|A_N^{-1}-A_{N,K}^{-1}\|\le C'/K :
\]
split the indices into those with $u_i^{-1}\le K$ and the rest; on the second block both inverses
have norm at most $(K-B)^{-1}$, the Schur complements of the first block differ by at most
$2B^2/(K-B)$ and have inverses of norm at most $1/g_0'$, and the block inverse formula bounds every
block of the difference by $O(K^{-1})$. Hence $\|A_N^{-1/2}-A_{N,K}^{-1/2}\|=O(K^{-1/2})$.
Conjugating the last display by $A_N^{-1/2}$ and using $\|F_N\|\le C$ gives
$I-A_{N,K}^{-1/2}F_NA_{N,K}^{-1/2}\succeq\frac{t_*}2I$ for large fixed $K$. Since capping changes
only the diagonal, $\mathcal M_{N,K}(x)=F_N-A_{N,K}\preceq-\frac{t_*}2g_0'I$. No independence of
$F_N$ and $W_N$ is used.

\emph{Step 3: a uniform negative median near the anchor.} This step cannot follow from
operator-norm continuity of the diagonal, since a single coordinate of $y$ may move by a fixed
amount. Under $\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}$ with $w\le1$ we have $|h'|\le|h|+1$, and
$\nablaH_N(x)=b^{(q_x)}+\xi''(q_x)\chi_xx$ by~\eqref{eq:kr-gradient}, so $N^{-1/2}|\nablaH_N(x)|$ is
bounded by~\eqref{eq:kr-cap} and Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints}; this fixes $H_0$, depending only on
$h$, $L_0$ and $\xi$, and with it the constants $C=C(H_0)$ and $c_3$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-c3},
used here and in Step~4. By that lemma, outside an event of conditional probability $e^{-c_3N}$ the
conditional Hessian of $H_N$ moves by at most $C|y-x|/\sqrt N\le C\rho$ in operator norm over the
ball. Freeze it at $x$. Apart from the capped diagonal, every deterministic term of
$\mathcal M_{N,K}(y)$ then changes by $o_\rho(1)$ in operator norm, uniformly for
$|y-x|\le\rho\sqrt N$, by Step~1; normalized rank-one terms are controlled by the normalized
Euclidean norms of their vectors. The remaining matrix, expressed through the conditional
transverse GOE and the independent cross vector of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-block}, has transverse block
$P[\sqrt a\,W_N-\operatorname{diag}(\min(u(r,y_i)^{-1},K)+a\chi_N)]P$, cross vector
\[
 P\Bigl\{-\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\min(u(r,y_i)^{-1},K)\bigr)e+\frac{a\sqrt q}{\sqrt N}\bigl(b/c-\mathbf v_x\bigr)\Bigr\}
 +\sqrt{\tau/N}\,g,
\]
and radial entry obtained from \eqref{eq:kr-radial} by replacing $q^{-1}\langle M^2/U\rangle_N$
with $e^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(\min(u(r,y_i)^{-1},K))e$, plus the independent residual
$\varsigma Z/\sqrt N$. Its Schur vectors are deterministic vectors plus the same Gaussian $g$,
independent of the auxiliary full GOE. The finite-$N$ comparison
\eqref{eq:matrix-comparison} still gives a transverse gap: at its fixed trial point the
reciprocal denominators stay bounded below and their average changes by $o_\rho(1)$. The
compressed-inverse formula uses finitely many bilinear forms of the transverse inverse with
deterministic profile vectors and the independent cross vector, and the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gap}\ref{lem:matrix-gap-b}--\ref{lem:matrix-gap-c}, which works at a fixed
spectral parameter through Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-b}--\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-c},
applies to the changed bounded diagonal; the changed cross weight satisfies $|\min(u(r,y_i)^{-1},K)x_i|\le K|x_i|$, so no
integrability of the fields of $y$ is needed. For weights involving the fields of $x$ first restrict
to $|b_i|\le L'$ and use uniform continuity; \eqref{eq:kr-cap} makes the remaining squared norms
uniformly small as $L'\to\infty$. Gaussian quadratic forms of the cross vector have conditional
variance $O(N^{-1})$. Hence every compressed Schur entry converges to a deterministic weighted
average, which is continuous under the profile changes above and tends to its value at the anchor
as the radius and the windows shrink. If no uniform negative median existed in any small ball and
window, we could select radii and widths tending to zero, $N\to\infty$, and failing points $y$; along
this sequence the transverse gap and every Schur entry converge to their capped anchor values, the
capped anchor gap of Step~2 makes the limiting Schur complement strictly negative, and the block
inverse identity gives a full gap, a contradiction. So for some $g_2,\rho_0>0$, depending on $K$,
\[
 \operatorname{median}_{\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}}\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\mathcal M_{N,K}(y)\bigr)\le-4g_2
 \qquad(|y-x|\le\rho_0\sqrt N)
\]
for all sufficiently narrow windows and large $N$.

\emph{Step 4: concentration and a net.} For a deterministic symmetric $S$, covariance
differentiation gives the bound \eqref{eq:matrix-hess-cov} of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-third}\ref{lem:matrix-third-a},
$\operatorname{Var}\operatorname{tr}(S\nabla^2H_N(y))\le\frac CN\operatorname{tr} S^2$, and conditioning decreases this variance. So
$\lambda_{\max}(\mathcal M_{N,K}(y))$ is a $C/\sqrt N$-Lipschitz function of the remaining standard
Gaussian variables, and, uniformly over deterministic $y$ in the ball,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-pointwise}
 \mathbb{P}_{x,h'}\bigl(\lambda_{\max}(\mathcal M_{N,K}(y))>-3g_2\bigr)\le2e^{-c_KN}.
\end{equation}
Fix a mesh $s>0$ and round each coordinate of $y-x$ toward zero to a multiple of $s$. The rounded
point stays in the cube and in the ball, is within $s$ of $y$ in every coordinate, and has at most
$\rho^2N/s^2$ nonzero rounded coordinates. For $\rho^2/s^2<\frac12$ the set of rounded points has
cardinality at most
\[
 \sum_{j\le\rho^2N/s^2}\binom Nj\lceil4/s\rceil^j
 \le\exp\Bigl\{N\Bigl[H_2(\rho^2/s^2)+\frac{\rho^2}{s^2}\log\lceil4/s\rceil+o(1)\Bigr]\Bigr\},
\]
with $H_2(p)=-p\log p-(1-p)\log(1-p)$. Between a point and its rounding the Hessian of $H_N$
moves by at most $Cs$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-c3}) and the other terms by at most $\omega_K(s)$, a
modulus from Step~1. Choose, in this order, the cap $K$ of Step~2 (which fixes $g_2$, $\rho_0$,
$c_K$), a mesh $s$ with $Cs+\omega_K(s)<g_2$, a radius $\rho\le\min(\rho_0,\rho_1)$ with
$\rho^2/s^2<\frac12$ and entropy below $c_K/2$, and then narrow windows and large $N$. The union
bound over the rounded points and \eqref{eq:kr-pointwise} give $\mathcal M_{N,K}(y)\preceq-2g_2I$ for
all $|y-x|\le\rho\sqrt N$, with exponentially small failure probability, and
\eqref{eq:kr-envelope} proves~\ref{prop:kr-local-a} with $\rho_*=\rho$ and $g_*=2g_2$.

\emph{Step 5: the typical determinant.} Let $\rho_K$ be the limit law of the capped diagonal
entries $\min(U^{-1},K)+a\chi_\pi$, and let $\mu_K$ be the reflection of
$\nu[a,\rho_K]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}), the limit of the empirical spectral
distribution of $A_{N,K}$. Its Stieltjes transform $m_K(z)=\int\mu_K(d\lambda)/(\lambda-z)$ solves
$m_K(z)=\int\rho_K(dD)/(D-z-am_K(z))$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-c}), and $\operatorname{supp}\mu_K\subset[g_0',\infty)$ by the gap. On the real
half-line below $\operatorname{supp}\mu_K$ put
\[
 L_K(z)=\int\log\bigl(D-z-am_K(z)\bigr)\,\rho_K(dD)+\frac a2m_K(z)^2 .
\]
The logarithms are defined: with $\varpi(z)=z+am_K(z)$, which is real and strictly increasing
there and tends to $-\infty$ as $z\to-\infty$, the imaginary part of the equation at
$z+\mathrm i\epsilon$ and Fatou's lemma give $a\int(D-\varpi(z))^{-2}\rho_K(dD)\le1$; integrating
over $z$ in a compact interval $J$ and substituting $\varpi(z)$, whose derivative is bounded on
$J$, shows that $\rho_K$ charges no point of the interior of $\varpi(J)$, since
$\int_I(D-x)^{-2}dx=\infty$ for $D$ in the interior of an interval $I$. So $\rho_K$-almost every
$D$ exceeds $\varpi(z)$, and the equation extends to the real half-line by dominated convergence.
Differentiating and using the equation gives $L_K'=-m_K$, and $L_K(z)=\log(-z)+o(1)$ as
$z\to-\infty$; these are also the derivative and the normalization of
$\int\log(\lambda-z)\,\mu_K(d\lambda)$, so the two functions coincide. Spectral convergence and the
gap give $N^{-1}\log\det A_{N,K}\to L_K(0)$. To remove the cap, increase the capped entries one at a
time: by the matrix determinant lemma and the gap,
\[
 0\le\log\det A_N-\log\det A_{N,K}\le\sum_{i:\,u_i^{-1}>K}\log\Bigl(1+\frac{u_i^{-1}-K}{g_0'}\Bigr).
\]
Each summand is at most $C(1+|b_i|)$ and vanishes unless $|b_i|\ge c'\log K-C$, so \eqref{eq:kr-cap}
makes the normalized sum uniformly small for large $K$. Real roots of the capped equation need not
be unique, so we identify $m_K(0)$ through traces: $N^{-1}\operatorname{tr} A_{N,K}^{-1}\to m_K(0)$, and by the
capped form of the inverse equivalent
(Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gap}\ref{lem:matrix-gap-c}--\ref{lem:matrix-gap-d}) the same traces converge
to a fixed point $\chi_\pi+O(K^{-1})$. Hence $m_K(0)\to\chi_\pi$, the logarithm arguments
$\min(U^{-1},K)+a(\chi_\pi-m_K(0))$ are at least $\frac12$ for large $K$, and dominated convergence,
with $|\log U|\le C(1+|b|)$, gives $L_K(0)\to\mathfrak d_\pi$ as $K\to\infty$. Finally, the negative of
the conditional Hessian differs from $A_N$ by a matrix of bounded rank $r$, and both have a gap
$g_*'>0$. By \eqref{eq:kr-cap}, $\max_i|b_i|\le t_0^{-1}\log(NL_0)$, so both have operator norm at
most $CN^C$, and eigenvalue interlacing bounds the difference of their log-determinants by
$2r\log(CN^C/g_*')=O(\log N)$. The other one-sided Hessian differs by a rank-one term and keeps the
gap. This proves~\ref{prop:kr-local-b} along the sequence.

\emph{Step 6: uniformity.} If either double limit in the proposition were positive, there would
be $\delta_*>0$, widths $w_k\downarrow0$, dimensions $N_k\uparrow\infty$ and admissible data of
width at most $w_k$ at dimension $N_k$ whose conditional failure probabilities exceed $\delta_*$.
These data obey \eqref{eq:kr-cap} with the same $L_0$, and their radii, empirical field laws and
energies converge to $q$, $\pi$ and $h$. Steps~1--5 apply along this sequence, so the failure
probabilities tend to zero, a contradiction.

title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Conditional comparison and a quadratic gap

label: eq:kr-condmean
title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Regression.} The covariance of $(H_N(x),x\cdot\nablaH_N(x))$ is $NS_0$, the projection of
$\nablaH_N(x)$ onto $x^\perp$ is independent of this pair with covariance $c$ times the identity
on $x^\perp$, and for $R(x,y)=r$
\[
 N^{-1}\operatorname{Cov}\bigl(H_N(y),(H_N(x),x\cdot\nablaH_N(x))\bigr)=\bigl(\xi(r),r\xi'(r)\bigr).
\]
Inverting $S_0$ and then regressing on the transverse gradient gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-condmean}
 \frac1N\mathbb{E}_{\rm cond}H_N(y)=A(r)h+B(r)d_N+\lambda_r\Bigl(\frac{b\cdot y}N-\frac rqk_N\Bigr),
\end{equation}
with the actual empirical moments $k_N=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_x}bM$ and $d_N=k_N+aq\chi_N$. Let $G_x$ be the centred
conditional field. On the slice $\{q_y=q,\ R(x,y)=r\}$ its covariance is
$N[\xi(R(y,z))-\xi'(r)^2R(y,z)/c]$ up to a constant independent of $y,z$. With
\[
 K_r(t)=\xi(t)-\frac{\xi'(r)^2}ct+r\xi'(r)-\xi(r),
\]
this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-increments}
 \frac1{2N}\mathbb{E}\bigl(G_x(y)-G_x(z)\bigr)^2=K_r(q)-K_r(R(y,z)).
\end{equation}
Since $0<\xi'(r)<c$, the numbers $\mathsf v_r=K_r'(r)$, $\bar{\mathsf v}_r=K_r'(q)-K_r'(r)$ and
$\mathsf w_r=qK_r'(q)-K_r(q)$ are positive, and $K_r(r)=rK_r'(r)$.

\emph{A Poisson comparison field.} Let $(\Pi_\alpha)$ be the points of a Poisson process on $\mathbb{R}$ with
intensity $\theta e^{-\theta u}\,du$. Independently, let $Z_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\mathsf v_r)$,
$g_{i\alpha}\sim\mathcal N(0,\bar{\mathsf v}_r)$ and $Y_\alpha\sim\mathcal N(0,N\mathsf w_r)$ be
independent; the $Z_i$ are common to all leaves $\alpha$. With
$\Psi(y)=\sum_i\{\lambda_rb_iy_i+\Phi^{*}(q,y_i)\}$, compare
\[
 X(y,\alpha)=G_x(y)+Y_\alpha+\Pi_\alpha+\Psi(y),\qquad
 \widetilde X(y,\alpha)=\sum_iy_i(Z_i+g_{i\alpha})+\Pi_\alpha+\Psi(y).
\]
For two indices put $q_{\alpha\beta}=q$ if $\alpha=\beta$ and $q_{\alpha\beta}=r$ otherwise. By
\eqref{eq:kr-increments}, the squared increment of $\widetilde X$ minus that of $X$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-bregman}
 2N\bigl\{K_r(R)-K_r(q_{\alpha\beta})-K_r'(q_{\alpha\beta})(R-q_{\alpha\beta})\bigr\}\ge0,
 \qquad R=R(y,z) .
\end{equation}
For equal leaves this is $2NK_r'(q)(q-R)-2N[K_r(q)-K_r(R)]$; for distinct leaves it uses
$\mathsf w_r=qK_r'(q)-K_r(q)$ and $K_r(r)=rK_r'(r)$. The inequality holds because
$K_r''=\xi''\ge0$ on $[-1,1]$, including negative values of $R$; this is the only place where the
proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} uses the convexity of $\xi$ on $[-1,0]$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-retained}\ref{prop:kr-retained-b} also uses it, through
Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}\ref{prop:max-fm-a}; see Remark~\ref{rem:kr-window}). Conditionally on the scores $\Pi_\alpha$, apply the
Sudakov--Fernique inequality to finite subsets of the slice and finitely many leaves; the means of
$X$ and $\widetilde X$ agree. Passing to all leaves is legitimate because, after subtracting one
fixed variable, the increasing maxima are nonnegative and their limits have finite expectation by
\eqref{eq:kr-marking} below; passing to the whole slice uses continuity and the integrability of
Gaussian suprema. So $\mathbb{E}\sup_{y,\alpha}X\le\mathbb{E}\sup_{y,\alpha}\widetilde X$.

\emph{Marking.} If $V_\alpha$ are i.i.d., independent of $(\Pi_\alpha)$, with
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta V}<\infty$, then Lemma~\ref{lem:poisson-shift} (with a trivial mark space) shows that
$\sup_\alpha(\Pi_\alpha+V_\alpha)-\theta^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta V}$ has the law of $\sup_\alpha \Pi_\alpha$,
a Gumbel variable with finite mean. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-marking}
 \mathbb{E}\sup_\alpha(\Pi_\alpha+V_\alpha)=\mathbb{E}\sup_\alpha \Pi_\alpha+\theta^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta V} .
\end{equation}
On the left, the supremum separates into $\sup_y\{G_x(y)+\Psi(y)\}$ plus $\sup_\alpha(Y_\alpha+\Pi_\alpha)$,
whose marking cost is $\theta N\mathsf w_r/2$. On the right, enlarge the slice to the cube and use
$\sup_{m\in[-1,1]}\{tm+\Phi^{*}(q,m)\}=\Phi(q,t)$ coordinatewise. Conditionally on the root vector
$(Z_i)$, the leaf marks $\sum_i\Phi(q,Z_i+\lambda_rb_i+g_{i\alpha})$ are i.i.d., and since
$\bar{\zeta}=\theta$ on $(r,q)$, the Cole--Hopf form of the Parisi equation gives
\[
 \frac1\theta\log\mathbb{E}_g\exp\Bigl\{\theta\sum_i\Phi(q,Z_i+\lambda_rb_i+g_i)\Bigr\}
 =\sum_i\Phi(r,Z_i+\lambda_rb_i);
\]
the exponential moments are finite since $|\Phi(q,t)|\le C+|t|$. Applying \eqref{eq:kr-marking}
on both sides and cancelling $\mathbb{E}\sup_\alpha \Pi_\alpha$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_y\bigl\{G_x(y)+\Psi(y)\bigr\}\le\sum_i\mathcal B(r,b_i)-\frac{N\theta}2\mathsf w_r .
\]
Finally, \eqref{eq:kr-condmean}, the identity $\Phi^{*}(q,x_i)=\Phi(q,b_i)-b_ix_i$ and the
cancellation of the equal Onsager integrals at $q_y=q_x$ give \eqref{eq:kr-exact-comparison}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q=q_x$ and $t_y=R(x,y)$. The same regression gives, for all $y,z$,
\[
 \frac1N\mathbb{E}\,G_x(y)G_x(z)=\xi(R(y,z))-\mathbf s(t_y)^{\mathsf T}S_0(Q)^{-1}\mathbf s(t_z)
 -\frac{\xi'(t_y)\xi'(t_z)}{\xi'(Q)}\Bigl(R(y,z)-\frac{t_yt_z}Q\Bigr),
\]
with $\mathbf s(t)=(\xi(t),t\xi'(t))^{\mathsf T}$ and $S_0(Q)$ the covariance matrix of
$N^{-1/2}(H_N(x),x\cdot\nablaH_N(x))$ (as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-c3}). Both $S_0(Q)$ and $\xi'(Q)$ are uniformly
invertible near $q$, so on the competitor window
\[
 \Bigl|\frac1{2N}\mathbb{E}\bigl(G_x(y)-G_x(z)\bigr)^2-K_r(q)+K_r(R(y,z))\Bigr|\le C\omega ;
\]
here and below $C$ depends on $I$, $\xi$, $\zeta$, $\pi$ and $h$ only. The conditional mean is controlled
without any identity specific to the law: the selected gradient is
$\nablaH_N(x)=b^{(Q)}+\xi''(Q)\chi_xx$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints}
$\|b^{(Q)}-b\|/\sqrt N\le C\omega$ and $|\chi_x-\chi_N|\le C\omega$, while the Wasserstein window
bounds $N^{-1}|b|^2$. Replacing $Q,t_y$ by $q,r$ and the actual-radius quantities by their
fixed-radius values in the conditional mean costs at most $CN\omega$, and the conjugate
$\Phi^{*}(\cdot,m)$ and the Onsager integral change by at most $CN\omega$ when the radius is frozen,
because $|\partial_t\Phi|$ is bounded and the infimum defining $\Phi^{*}$ preserves this bound.

Fix $\rho\in(0,1)$ and a Euclidean $\rho\sqrt N$-net $y_1,\dots,y_n$ of the competitor window, with
$n\le(1+2/\rho)^N$. On the net the increment difference \eqref{eq:kr-bregman} now has an error of
at most $CN\omega$, which includes the discrepancies in the self-overlaps of the competitors. Add
independent Gaussians $\epsilon_j+\epsilon'_\alpha$, each of variance $C_0N\omega$, to
$\widetilde X(y_j,\alpha)$. Distinct indices differ in the physical or the leaf index, so every
squared increment gains at least $2C_0N\omega$, and the comparison holds without error for $C_0$
large. The physical noise costs at most $\mathbb{E}\max_j\epsilon_j\le\sqrt{2C_0N\omega\log n}$. The leaf
noise has an exact cost: replacing $\Pi_\alpha$ by $\Pi_\alpha+\epsilon'_\alpha$ translates the Poisson
process by $\theta C_0N\omega/2$, by \eqref{eq:kr-marking}, and the other leaf marks keep their
law, also conditionally on the root field. After division by $N$ the two noises cost at most
$C\sqrt{\omega\log(1+2/\rho)}+C\omega$, whatever the number of leaves.

It remains to remove the net. Conditioning reduces increment variances, and the canonical metric
of $H_N$ is at most $C|y-z|$ on the cube, so the Gaussian entropy integral gives
$\mathbb{E}\sup_y|G_x(y)-G_x(y_{j(y)})|\le CN\rho\sqrt{\log(C/\rho)}$. The linear part of the endpoint
changes by at most $CN\rho$. For the conjugate part, let $\Omega$ be a modulus of continuity of
$\Phi^{*}(q,\cdot)$ on $[-1,1]$ and $C_\Phi$ a bound on its absolute value; splitting coordinates
at $|y_i-z_i|=\sqrt\rho$ gives
$N^{-1}\sum_i|\Phi^{*}(q,y_i)-\Phi^{*}(q,z_i)|\le\Omega(\sqrt\rho)+2C_\Phi\rho$ when
$|y-z|\le\rho\sqrt N$. On the comparison side we again enlarge the net to the cube. Finally the
endpoint averages are close to their $\pi$-averages: $b\mapsto\mathcal B(r,b)-\Phi(q,b)$ is
uniformly Lipschitz, $U$ is bounded and Lipschitz, $b\mapsto bM(b)$ has derivative at most
$C(1+|b|)$, and Cauchy--Schwarz under a $W_2$-coupling bounds the differences by $C\omega$.
Altogether the normalized error is at most
\[
 C\omega+C\sqrt{\omega\log(1+2/\rho)}+C\rho\sqrt{\log(C/\rho)}+C\rho+\Omega(\sqrt\rho)+2C_\Phi\rho ,
\]
which is small if $\rho$ is small and then $\omega$ is small. All estimates precede the limit in
$N$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{The baseline.} The regression coefficients satisfy
$cA(r)+(c+aq)B(r)=r\xi'(r)/q$ and $\xi(q)A(r)+qcB(r)=\xi(r)$. With \eqref{eq:kr-k0} and
\eqref{eq:kr-h0}, every $\chi_0$-term of \eqref{eq:kr-endpoint} cancels and
\[
 \mathcal C_{\pi_0,h_0}(r)=\theta\bigl\{qc-\xi(q)-r\xi'(r)+\xi(r)\bigr\}=\theta\,\mathsf w_r .
\]
On the plateau, $e^{\theta\Phi}$ is space-time harmonic for the heat flow with clock $\xi'$, and
the Auffinger--Chen process on $[0,q]$ is its Doob transform. The density change depends only on
the endpoint, so given $X_q=b$ the law of $X_r$ is the Gaussian bridge with mean $\lambda_rb$ and
variance $\mathsf v_r$. Hence $\mathbb{E}_0\mathcal B(r,b)=\mathbb{E}\Phi(r,X_r)$, and It\^o's formula gives
$\frac d{dt}\mathbb{E}\Phi(t,X_t)=\frac\theta2\xi''(t)\Gamma_{\zeta}(t)$ on $(0,q)$. Therefore
\[
 J_{\pi_0,h_0}(r)=-\frac\theta2\int_r^q\xi''(t)\bigl(\Gamma_{\zeta}(t)-t\bigr)\,dt
 =-\theta\bigl(\mathcal{O}_\zeta(r)-\mathcal{O}_\zeta(q)\bigr),
\]
which is \eqref{eq:kr-baseline-J}.

\emph{The double contact at $q$.} Recall from before Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy} that $A(q)=1$,
$A'(q)=0$, $B(q)=0$ and $B'(q)=q^{-1}$. Although $\mathsf v_q=0$, the heat-semigroup rule, which differentiates in the
variance and not in its square root, gives
$\partial_r\mathcal B(r,b)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Phi_t+\lambda_r'b\,\Phi_x+\frac12\mathsf v_r'\Phi_{xx}\bigr](r,\lambda_rb+Z)$.
As $r\uparrow q$, $\mathsf v_r'\to-a$ and $\lambda_r'\to a/c$, and the Parisi equation on the plateau
gives $\Phi_t(q-,b)=-\frac a2(U+\theta M^2)$. So
\[
 \partial_r\mathcal B(q-,b)=-aU(b)-\frac{a\theta}2M(b)^2+\frac acbM(b),\qquad
 \mathcal C_{\pi,h}'(q)=a\chi_\pi-\frac ack_\pi ,
\]
and for every $\pi$ with $\mathbb{E}_\pi M^2=q$ and every $h$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-double-contact}
 J_{\pi,h}(q)=0,\qquad J_{\pi,h}'(q-)=0 .
\end{equation}
A second heat differentiation expresses $\partial_r^2\mathcal B(r,b)$ as an average at
$(r,\lambda_rb+Z)$ of $\Phi_{tt},\Phi_{tx},\Phi_{txx}$ and of $\Phi_x,\dots,\Phi_{xxxx}$, with
coefficients built from $\lambda_r',\lambda_r'',\mathsf v_r',\mathsf v_r''$ and $b$, at most quadratic in
$b$; on the plateau the Parisi equation expresses the time derivatives through spatial derivatives
of order at most four. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-contact}\ref{lem:kr-contact-d} these are bounded on
$[0,q]\times\mathbb{R}$, so $|\partial_r^2\mathcal B(r,b)|\le C(1+b^2)$ for $0<r<q$, which also justifies the
left derivatives at $q$ by dominated convergence.

\emph{The tilt and the shift.} The map $\pi\mapsto J_{\pi,h_0}$ is affine, and
$\pi_\eta-\pi_0=-\eta\mathcal R\pi_0$ with $\mathcal R$ bounded, while $\pi_0$ has moments of all
orders. So $\sup_{0<r<q}|(J_{\pi_\eta,h_0}-J_{\pi_0,h_0})''(r)|\le C_J\eta$ for $0<\eta\le\eta_0$.
Integrating twice from $q$ and using \eqref{eq:kr-double-contact},
$|J_{\pi_\eta,h_0}(r)-J_{\pi_0,h_0}(r)|\le C_J\eta(q-r)^2$. The energy shift contributes exactly
$L\eta(A(r)-1)\le-L\eta(1-r/q)^2$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy}. With $L_J=q^2(C_J+1)$,
\eqref{eq:kr-baseline-J} gives \eqref{eq:kr-tilted-gap}.

title: Lemma

name: Values at the selected data

title: Proof
body_md:
The first two assertions are in Corollary~\ref{cor:matrix-tilted} (with $Q=q$ and $\pi=\pi_\eta$),
and~\ref{lem:kr-correction-a} follows from them and
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-correction}\ref{lem:matrix-correction-b}, since $2L_1w+L_2\varrho(w)\le
C_V\varrho(w)$. Corollary~\ref{cor:matrix-tilted} also gives~\ref{lem:kr-correction-b}, because the
total variation distance between $\pi_\eta=(1-\eta\mathcal R)\pi_0$ and $\pi_0$ is at most
$\eta\|\mathcal R\|_\infty$; the corollary rests on the identity
$V_{\mathrm{TAP}}(q,M_\#\pi_0)=V_\zeta(q,M_\#\pi_0)$ at the contact $q$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-band}). Finally, by the Fenchel identity
$\Phi^{*}(q,M(b))=\Phi(q,b)-bM(b)$, \eqref{eq:kr-level} says $h_0+V_\zeta(q,M_\#\pi_0)=f$; and
$|V_\zeta(q,M_\#\pi_\eta)-V_\zeta(q,M_\#\pi_0)|\le2C_*\eta\|\mathcal R\|_\infty$ because the conjugates
are bounded by $C_*$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-correction}\ref{lem:matrix-correction-a}), while
$h_\eta-h_0=L\eta$.

label: lem:kr-marked
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-marked}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Borel subset of $\{x\in(-1,1)^N:q_x>0\}$ and let $\mathsf Q(x,H_N)\ge0$ be a
measurable mark. Then
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sum_{x\in\mathcal A:\,\nabla F_\zeta(x)=0}\mathsf Q(x,H_N)
 =\int_{\mathcal A}p_{\nabla F_\zeta(x)}(0)\,
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\,\mathsf Q(x,H_N)\bigm|\nabla F_\zeta(x)=0\bigr]\,dx,
\]
also when both sides are infinite. Almost surely no critical point in $\{q_x>0\}$ lies on a sphere
$\{q_x=t\}$ with $t$ an atom of $\zeta$, so the Hessian on the right is the ordinary one for almost
every $x$. The conditional expectation is the canonical one: given $\nabla F_\zeta(x)=0$, the field
$H_N$ has the law of the Gaussian regression of $H_N$ on $\nablaH_N(x)$ evaluated at the gradient
value \eqref{eq:kr-gradient}.
head: environment
name: Marked Kac--Rice formula

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $x_*\neq0$. The covariance $\Sigma_*$ of $\nablaH_N(x_*)$ is positive definite. Put
$\mathbf Z=\Sigma_*^{-1/2}\nablaH_N(x_*)$, $\psi_j(x)=\mathbb{E}[H_N(x)\mathbf Z_j]$, so that
$H_N(x)=\psi(x)\cdot\mathbf Z+\widetilde H_N(x)$ with $\widetilde H_N$ independent of $\mathbf Z$.
The matrix $\mathcal J(x)_{ij}=\partial_i\psi_j(x)$ equals $\Sigma_*^{1/2}$ at $x_*$, hence is invertible
on a deterministic neighbourhood $U_*$. Conditionally on $\widetilde H_N$, let
$b_*(x)=\nabla\widetilde H_N(x)+\nabla(F_\zeta-H_N)(x)$ and $T_*(x)=-\mathcal J(x)^{-1}b_*(x)$, a
locally Lipschitz map; the critical equation is $\mathbf Z=T_*(x)$, and at almost every $x$,
$DT_*(x)=-\mathcal J(x)^{-1}\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)$ evaluated at $\mathbf Z=T_*(x)$. The area formula
for Lipschitz maps \cite[Section~3]{Federer}, extended to the nonnegative weight equal to the
Gaussian density at $T_*(x)$ times the mark by monotone convergence, equates the Gaussian average
of the marked number of solutions with the integral of that weight times $|\det DT_*|$. Averaging
over $\widetilde H_N$ and changing variables from $\mathbf Z$ to the gradient gives the formula on
$U_*$; countably many such charts and Tonelli's theorem give it on $\mathcal A$. The union of the
atom spheres is Lebesgue-null, a locally Lipschitz map between spaces of equal dimension maps null
sets to null sets, and $\mathbf Z$ is independent of $\widetilde H_N$; this gives the second
assertion. Finally, the conditional law produced by the argument is Gaussian with mean affine in
the gradient value and covariance independent of it, as is the regression of $H_N$ on
$\nablaH_N(x)$; two such versions agree for almost every gradient value, since the law of
$\nabla F_\zeta(x)$ is nondegenerate, hence for every value. Conditioning in addition on $H_N(x)$,
as below, is the same canonical regression on $(H_N(x),\nablaH_N(x))$.

label: lem:kr-marks
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: The marks

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:kr-marks-a} The set $B(x)$ is convex, and for $z\in B(x)$,
$\sqrt{q_z}\ge\sqrt{q_x}-\rho_\eta\ge\sqrt{3q/4}-\sqrt q/2>0$. Let $y\neq y'$ in $B(x)$,
$z_t=y'+t(y-y')$ and $\phi(t)=\langle\nabla F_\zeta(z_t),y-y'\rangle$ for $t\in[0,1]$. The segment is a
compact subset of $(-1,1)^N\setminus\{0\}$, where $\nabla F_\zeta$ is locally Lipschitz, so $\phi$ is
Lipschitz and $\phi(1)-\phi(0)=\int_0^1\phi'(t)\,dt$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hessian}\ref{lem:matrix-hessian-b}, at every $t$ the right derivative of
$\phi$ is $\langle\nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(z_t)(y-y'),y-y'\rangle$, with $\sigma$ the sign of
$z_t\cdot(y-y')$, and by~\ref{step:kr-ret4} it is at most $-g_\eta|y-y'|^2$. At almost every $t$ the
derivative $\phi'(t)$ exists and equals the right derivative, and integration gives the claim.

\ref{lem:kr-marks-b} Put $r_j=\min\{\delta'+2j\omega_c,\,q-\delta'\}$ for
$0\le j\le J=\lceil(q-2\delta')/(2\omega_c)\rceil$, so that $\mathcal K(x)\subset\bigcup_jS_j$ with
$S_j=\{y\in[-1,1]^N:|q_y-q|\le\omega_c,\,|R(x,y)-r_j|\le\omega_c\}$, and $J+1\le q/\omega_c$. The anchor
data have width at most $\omega_c$, because $|q_x-q|\le2w\le\omega_c$, $W_2(\pi_x,\pi)\le w$ and
$|h'-h|\le N^{-2}\le\omega_c$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-comparison}\ref{lem:kr-comparison-b}
and~\ref{lem:kr-comparison-c}, and the definition of $\gamma$,
$Y_j=\sup_{y\in S_j}\{F_\zeta(y)-F_\zeta(x)\}$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}_{x,h'}Y_j\le-\frac34\gamma N$ whenever
$S_j\neq\varnothing$. Under $\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}$, $F_\zeta(x)$ is a constant, and $Y_j$ is the supremum over
the compact set $S_j$ of a continuous function plus a centred Gaussian field $G_x$ with continuous
paths and $\operatorname{Var} G_x(y)\le\operatorname{Var}H_N(y)\le N\xi(1)$. Gaussian concentration for Lipschitz functions
\cite[(1.22)--(1.23)]{Ledoux}, applied to maxima over finite subsets increasing to a dense set and
passed to the limit by monotone convergence and Fatou's lemma, gives
$\mathbb{P}_{x,h'}(Y_j>-\frac12\gamma N)\le\exp\{-(\gamma N/4)^2/(2N\xi(1))\}$. If~\ref{step:kr-ret5}
fails, some $Y_j$ exceeds $-\frac12\gamma N$; the union bound over $J+1\le q/\omega_c$ indices
proves the claim.

\ref{lem:kr-marks-c} The data $(x,h')$ are admissible of width at most $w+N^{-2}$ in the sense of
Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-local}, and $\rho_\eta\le\rho_*$; part~\ref{prop:kr-local-a} of that
proposition gives the claim.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-normalization
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Rate of the selected data

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:kr-law} and \eqref{eq:kr-ito},
$D(\pi_0\Vert\mathcal N(0,c))=\theta\,\mathbb{E}_0[\Phi(q,b)-\Phi(0,0)]=\theta(f-P_\zeta)+\frac{\theta^2}2\vartheta(q)$.
By \eqref{eq:kr-k0}, $k_0-c\chi_0=c\theta q$, and by \eqref{eq:kr-h0},
$h_0-cd_0/(c+aq)=\theta(\xi(q)-qc^2/(c+aq))=\theta\sigma_H^2$. So the two quadratic terms of
\eqref{eq:kr-SigmaKR} add up to
$\frac{\theta^2}2\bigl(\frac{acq^2}{c+aq}-\xi(q)+\frac{qc^2}{c+aq}\bigr)=\frac{\theta^2}2\vartheta(q)$, and
$\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_0,h_0)=\theta(P_\zeta-f)=\Sigma(f)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-contact}\ref{lem:kr-contact-a}. For $\eta>0$, the log-density ratio
$\log(1-\eta\mathcal R)$ is $O(\eta)$ uniformly, the original log-density grows at most linearly
in $|b|$, every other moment in \eqref{eq:kr-SigmaKR} is affine in $\eta$ with bounded slope, and
$h_\eta-h_0=L\eta$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-count
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-count}
Let $\mathcal W_N(w)$ be the set of $x\in(-1,1)^N$ whose fields satisfy
$|N^{-1}\sum_i\varphi(b_i)-\mathbb{E}_\pi\varphi|\le w$ for the five functions
$\varphi(b)=b^2,\ \log U(b),\ \log\frac{d\pi}{db}(b),\ U(b),\ bM(b)$. Then
\[
 \liminf_{w\downarrow0}\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)
 \ge\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta).
\]
head: environment
name: Expected marked count

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal S_N$ be the set of $x$ satisfying~\ref{step:kr-ret2}; it is a Borel subset of
$\{q_x\ge q-2w\}$. For $x\in\mathcal S_N$ let $r=q_x$, $c_r=\xi'(r)$, $a_r=\xi''(r)$,
$k_x=N^{-1}b^{(r)}\cdot x$, $d_x=k_x+a_rr\chi_x$ and $\mathbf g(x)=b^{(r)}+a_r\chi_xx$, so that
$\nabla F_\zeta(x)=\nablaH_N(x)-\mathbf g(x)$. Covariance differentiation gives
$\operatorname{Cov}(\nablaH_N(x))=c_rI+\frac{a_r}Nxx^{\mathsf T}$, with determinant $c_r^N(1+a_rr/c_r)$, and
\[
 \log p_{\nablaH_N(x)}(\mathbf g(x))=-\frac N2\log(2\pi c_r)-\frac12\log\Bigl(1+\frac{a_rr}{c_r}\Bigr)
 -\frac{|b^{(r)}|^2}{2c_r}-N\Bigl[\frac{a_r\chi_xk_x}{c_r}+\frac{a_r^2r\chi_x^2}{2c_r}
 -\frac{a_rd_x^2}{2c_r(c_r+a_rr)}\Bigr],
\]
using $|\mathbf g(x)|^2=|b^{(r)}|^2+2Na_r\chi_xk_x+Na_r^2r\chi_x^2$ and $x\cdot\mathbf g(x)=Nd_x$.
Given $\nablaH_N(x)=\mathbf g(x)$, $H_N(x)$ is Gaussian with mean $Nc_rd_x/(c_r+a_rr)$ and variance
$N\sigma_H^2(r)$, where $\sigma_H^2(r)=\xi(r)-rc_r^2/(c_r+a_rr)>0$ is continuous near $q$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy} at radius $r$). By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-marked}, disintegrating over
$H_N(x)=Nh'$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\widehat C_N=\int_{\mathcal S_N}p_{\nablaH_N(x)}(\mathbf g(x))\int_{|h'-h|\le N^{-2}}
 Np_x(Nh')\,\mathbb{E}_{x,h'}\bigl[|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\,\mathbf{1}\{\text{\ref{step:kr-ret4},\ \ref{step:kr-ret5}}\}\bigr]\,dh'\,dx ,
\]
with $p_x$ the conditional density of $H_N(x)$. Fix $t>0$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-local}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-marks}\ref{lem:kr-marks-b}--\ref{lem:kr-marks-c}, there is $w(t)>0$ such
that for $w\le w(t)$ and $N\ge N(t,w)$, uniformly over $x\in\mathcal S_N$ and $|h'-h|\le N^{-2}$,
the event that~\ref{step:kr-ret4} and~\ref{step:kr-ret5} hold and
$N^{-1}\log|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\ge\mathfrak d_\pi-t$ has conditional probability at least
$\frac12$, so that
\[
 \mathbb{E}_{x,h'}\bigl[|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\,\mathbf{1}\{\text{\ref{step:kr-ret4},\ \ref{step:kr-ret5}}\}\bigr]
 \ge\tfrac12e^{N(\mathfrak d_\pi-t)} .
\]
Up to a constant factor, the energy window contributes at least
\[
 N^{-3/2}\exp\Bigl\{-\frac N{2\sigma_H^2(r)}\Bigl[\Bigl(h-\frac{c_rd_x}{c_r+a_rr}\Bigr)^2+O(N^{-2})\Bigr]\Bigr\}.
\]
Change
variables $x_i=M(b_i)$, a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^N$ onto $(-1,1)^N$ with Jacobian $\prod_iU(b_i)$, and
write $dx=\prod_i[U(b_i)/\pi'(b_i)]\,\pi^{\otimes N}(db)$ with $\pi'=d\pi/db$. On $\mathcal S_N$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints} gives $|b^{(r)}_i-b_i|\le C|r-q|\le2Cw$ and $|\chi_x-\chi_N|+|k_x-k_N|\le Cw$,
hence $N^{-1}\bigl||b^{(r)}|^2-|b|^2\bigr|\le Cw$; the windows of $\mathcal W_N(w)$ control the
averages of $b^2,\log U,\log\pi',U$ and $bM$. Collecting the exponents,
$N^{-1}\sum_i\log U(b_i)$ cancels $-\mathbb{E}_\pi\log U$ in $\mathfrak d_\pi$ up to $w$; the terms
$-\mathbb{E}_\pi\log\pi'-\frac12\log(2\pi c)-\mathbb{E}_\pi b^2/(2c)$ make $-D(\pi\Vert\mathcal N(0,c))$; and the
quadratic identity
\[
 -\frac{a\chi k}c-\frac{a^2q\chi^2}{2c}+\frac{a(k+aq\chi)^2}{2c(c+aq)}+\frac a2\chi^2
 =\frac{a(k-c\chi)^2}{2c(c+aq)}
\]
turns the remaining terms of the gradient density and of $\mathfrak d_\pi$ into the second term of
\eqref{eq:kr-SigmaKR}. Hence, for $w\le w(t)$ and $N\ge N(t,w)$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\widehat C_N\ge\tfrac12\,N^{-C}\,\pi^{\otimes N}(\mathcal S_N)\,
 \exp\bigl\{N\bigl(\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi,h)-t-\epsilon(w)\bigr)\bigr\},
\]
with $\epsilon(w)\to0$ as $w\downarrow0$. Under $\pi^{\otimes N}$ the empirical law of the fields
converges to $\pi$ in $W_2$ almost surely, $N^{-1}\sum_ie^{t_0|b_i|}\to\mathbb{E}_\pi e^{t_0|b|}<L_0$, and the
five averages converge, all by the law of large numbers; so $\pi^{\otimes N}(\mathcal S_N)\to1$. Let
$N\to\infty$, then $w\downarrow0$ and $t\downarrow0$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-code
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-code}
For $N\ge3$ and $\sqrt s<t<t'<1$,
\[
 n_N(s)\le\frac{2N}{t'-t}\bigl(1-t'^2\bigr)^{-(N-3)/2};\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log n_N(s)\le-\frac12\log(1-s).
\]
head: environment
name: Spherical code

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal A\subset S^{N-1}$ have pairwise inner products at most $s$, and let $K(u)=\{v\in S^{N-1}:\langle v,u\rangle\ge t\}$. We claim that
$|\mathcal A\cap K(u)|\le N$ for every unit $u$. If $u\in\mathcal A$, every other $v\in\mathcal A$ has
$\langle v,u\rangle\le s<t$, so the intersection is $\{u\}$. Otherwise each $v$ in it differs from
$\pm u$, so $v-\langle v,u\rangle u$ is a nonzero vector of $u^\perp$, and for distinct $v,v'$ in it
$\langle v-\langle v,u\rangle u,\,v'-\langle v',u\rangle u\rangle\le s-t^2<0$. In $\mathbb{R}^d$ at most $d+1$
vectors have pairwise negative inner products: if $v_1,\dots,v_{d+2}$ did, an affine dependence
$\sum_j\lambda_jv_j=0$, $\sum_j\lambda_j=0$, $\lambda\neq0$, would give
$z=\sum_{\lambda_j>0}\lambda_jv_j=\sum_{\lambda_k<0}|\lambda_k|v_k$ with
$|z|^2=\sum_{\lambda_j>0>\lambda_k}\lambda_j|\lambda_k|\langle v_j,v_k\rangle<0$. With $d=N-1$ this
proves the claim. For $u$ uniform on $S^{N-1}$, rotation invariance gives
$\mathbb{E}|\mathcal A\cap K(u)|=|\mathcal A|\mathbb{P}(u_1\ge t)$, so $|\mathcal A|\le N/\mathbb{P}(u_1\ge t)$. The
density of $u_1$ is proportional to $(1-z^2)^{(N-3)/2}\le1$ on $(-1,1)$, with normalizing integral
at most $2$, so $\mathbb{P}(u_1\ge t)\ge\frac12(t'-t)(1-t'^2)^{(N-3)/2}$. Let $N\to\infty$, $t'\downarrow t$
and $t\downarrow\sqrt s$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-separation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-separation}
Let $w\le w_1$ and $N\ge3\gamma^{-1/2}$. Then distinct retained points $x,y$ satisfy
$R(x,y)<\delta'$, and $\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)\le n_N(s_w)$ with $s_w=\delta'/(q-2w)\le\frac13$.
This holds for every realization of $H_N$ and every choice of the sets $\mathcal W_N(w)$.
head: environment
name: Separation of retained points

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x\neq y$ be retained. By~\ref{step:kr-ret2} and~\ref{step:kr-ret3} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-correction}\ref{lem:kr-correction-a},
$|F_\zeta(z)/N-f_\eta|\le N^{-2}+C_V\varrho(w)$ for $z\in\{x,y\}$. If $R(x,y)\ge q-\delta'$, then
$|x-y|^2/N=q_x+q_y-2R(x,y)\le4w+2\delta'\le3\delta'<\rho_\eta^2$, so $y\in B(x)$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-marks}\ref{lem:kr-marks-a} with~\ref{step:kr-ret1} at both points gives
$0=\langle\nabla F_\zeta(y)-\nabla F_\zeta(x),y-x\rangle\le-g_\eta|y-x|^2<0$, a contradiction. If
$\delta'\leR(x,y)<q-\delta'$, then $y\in\mathcal K(x)$, so~\ref{step:kr-ret5} gives
$F_\zeta(y)-F_\zeta(x)\le-\gamma N/2$; but
