$F_\zeta(y)-F_\zeta(x)\ge-2N(N^{-2}+C_V\varrho(w))>-\gamma N/2$, since $C_V\varrho(w)\le\gamma/8$ and
$N^{-2}<\gamma/8$, again a contradiction. So $R(x,y)<\delta'$. The unit vectors $x/|x|$, for
retained $x$, are then pairwise distinct with inner products $R(x,y)/\sqrt{q_xq_y}<\delta'/(q-2w)$,
since $q_x,q_y\ge q-2w$; and $s_w\le(q/4)/(3q/4)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\eta$ be admissible and choose the parameters~\ref{step:kr-par1}--\ref{step:kr-par6}, with
$\mathcal W_N(w)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count}, and call the points counted by $\widehat C_N$
retained. We verify~\ref{step:stab-k1}--\ref{step:stab-k3} of Section~\ref{sec:stab-kr}, in which
$\pi_x$, $M$ and $\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)$ are as here.

\emph{\ref{step:stab-k1}.} By~\ref{step:kr-ret1} and~\ref{step:kr-ret4}, every retained point is a
critical point of $F_\zeta$ in $(-1,1)^N$, and $\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\zeta(y)\preceq-g_\eta I$ whenever
$|y-x|\le\rho_\eta\sqrt N$; $g_\eta$ and $\rho_\eta$ depend only on $\eta$ (through $L_0$, which we fix
as a function of $\eta$).

\emph{\ref{step:stab-k2}.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-correction},
$W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi_\eta)\le W_2(\pi_x,\pi_\eta)\le w$ and $|q_x-q|\le2w$. As in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-separation}, $|F_\zeta(x)/N-f_\eta|\le N^{-2}+C_V\varrho(w)$, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-correction}\ref{lem:kr-correction-b} the value $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)/N$ lies within
$C_V(\eta+\varrho(w))$ below $F_\zeta(x)/N$. With \eqref{eq:kr-feta},
\[
 \Bigl|\frac{F_\zeta(x)}N-f\Bigr|+\Bigl|\frac{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)}N-f\Bigr|
 \le\varepsilon_1(\eta)+\varepsilon_2(w)+2N^{-2},\qquad
 \varepsilon_1(\eta)=(2L+3C_V)\eta,\quad \varepsilon_2(w)=3C_V\varrho(w),
\]
and $\varepsilon_1(0)=0$, as required.

\emph{\ref{step:stab-k3}.} Since $\widehat C_N$ is a nonnegative integer,
$\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N\le\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)\max\widehat C_N\le\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)\,n_N(s_w)$ for
$N\ge3\gamma^{-1/2}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-separation}. Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-count}
and~\ref{lem:kr-code}, the continuity of $w\mapsto s_w$ and $s_w\to\delta'/q$ give
\[
 \liminf_{w\downarrow0}\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)\ge1\bigr)
 \ge\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta)+\frac12\log\Bigl(1-\frac{\delta'}q\Bigr)
 \ge\Sigma(f)-\varepsilon_3(\eta)+\frac12\log\Bigl(1-\frac\delta q\Bigr),
\]
with $\varepsilon_3(\eta)=|\Sigma(f)-\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta)|\le C_\Sigma\eta$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-normalization}, and $\delta'\le\delta$.

\emph{Existence.} Fix $\varepsilon>0$. Choose an admissible $\eta$ with
$\varepsilon_1(\eta)\le\varepsilon/3$ (this is $\eta=0$ if $\Delta_0>0$), then $\delta\in(0,q/2)$, then
$w$ so small that $\varepsilon_2(w)\le\varepsilon/3$, and let $N^{-2}\le\varepsilon/6$. By~\ref{step:stab-k2}
every retained point $x$ satisfies \eqref{eq:event-exist} with $\zeta=\zeta_f$, so
$\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f))\ge\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)$ for all large $N$, for every such $w$. By
\ref{step:stab-k3},
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\bigr)
 \ge\Sigma(f)-C_\Sigma\eta+\frac12\log\Bigl(1-\frac\delta q\Bigr).
\]
The left side depends neither on $\eta$ nor on $\delta$. Let $\delta\downarrow0$ and then
$\eta\downarrow0$ through admissible values.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{The bound $g_\eta\le-\lambda_+^{(\eta)}$.} Fix $\kappa>0$ and put
$\tau':=\frac12\min\{\kappa,\nu^{(\eta)}([\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-\kappa,\infty))\}$, which is positive because
$\lambda_+^{(\eta)}\in\operatorname{supp}\nu^{(\eta)}$. Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk} to the single pair
$(q,M_\#\pi_\eta)$, which puts no mass at $\pm1$, with the order parameter $\zeta_f$ and accuracy $\tau'$.
Since $u(q,M(b))=\Phi_{\zeta_f,xx}(q,b)=U(b)$, the bulk law attached to this pair is $\nu^{(\eta)}$. This gives
$w_H>0$ such that, for every $L'>0$ and all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most
$e^{-L'N}$, every $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $|q_x-q|\le w_H$ and $W_1(\mu_x,M_\#\pi_\eta)\le w_H$ satisfies
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)),\nu^{(\eta)})\le\tau'$. Fix $\delta\in(0,q/2)$. By \ref{step:stab-k3} we
may choose $w\le w_H/2$ and $L'>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)\ge1)\ge e^{-L'N/2}$ for
all large $N$. Then, for large $N$, with positive probability there is a retained point $x$ outside
the exceptional event; by \ref{step:stab-k2} it satisfies the two window conditions. For
$H=\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)$, since $\tau'<\kappa$,
\[
 \operatorname{ESD}(H)\bigl((\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-2\kappa,\infty)\bigr)
 \ge\nu^{(\eta)}\bigl((\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-2\kappa+\tau',\infty)\bigr)-\tau'
 \ge\nu^{(\eta)}\bigl([\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-\kappa,\infty)\bigr)-\tau'>0 .
\]
So $\lambda_{\max}(H)>\lambda_+^{(\eta)}-2\kappa$, while \ref{step:stab-k1} gives
$\lambda_{\max}(H)\le-g_\eta$. Hence $g_\eta<-\lambda_+^{(\eta)}+2\kappa$ for every $\kappa>0$.

\emph{The expansion.} Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge} applies to the law of $U$ under $\pi_\eta$. Its
hypothesis holds under $\pi_0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-hyp}), and it is preserved by a change of
measure whose density $1-\eta\mathcal R$ lies in $[\frac12,\frac32]$, since such a change preserves
null sets and essential suprema and changes expectations of nonnegative functions by a factor at
least $\frac12$. The quadratic expansion of the edge in that lemma states that
$|\lambda_++\Delta^2/(4a\mathbb{E} U^3)|\le C|\Delta|^3$ when $|\Delta|\le c_0$, with $c_0,C$ depending only on $a$
and $\mathbb{E} U^3$. Under $\pi_\eta$ one has $\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}U^3\in[\frac12\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}U^3,\frac32\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}U^3]$,
so $c_0$ and $C$ can be taken uniform in $\eta\in(0,\eta_0]$ (they are explicit and monotone in
$\mathbb{E} U^3$; see the proof in Appendix~\ref{app:matrix-pastur}). Insert $\Delta_\eta$ from
\eqref{eq:stab-tilt} and $\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}U^3=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}U^3-\eta\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}[\mathcal RU^3]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{Lower bounds.} Take the construction of Theorem~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-a} at an
admissible tilt $\eta$.
The coupling that moves the mass of $\eta\mathcal R_+\pi_0$ onto that of $\eta\mathcal R_-\pi_0$
gives $W_2(\pi_\eta,\pi_0)^2\le2\eta\|\mathcal R\|_\infty\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}b^2$. By \ref{step:stab-k1} and
\ref{step:stab-k2}, once $\eta$, $w$ and $N^{-1}$ are small enough in terms of $\varepsilon$, every
retained point is an $\varepsilon$-SUSY state. Hence
$\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge\mathbb{P}(\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge1)\ge\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)$, and
\ref{step:stab-k3} gives both lower bounds after $\delta\downarrow0$ and $\eta\downarrow0$.

\emph{Upper bound.} The upper bound of part~\ref{prop:stab-susy-i} is
Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-susy} below, whose hypotheses are those of
Proposition~\ref{prop:stab-susy}. The $\liminf_N$ and the $\limsup_N$ of
$N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}$ are nondecreasing in $\varepsilon$, since
$\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}$ is; with the lower bound this gives the last assertion of
part~\ref{prop:stab-susy-i}.

The first assertion of part~\ref{prop:stab-susy-ii} was obtained with the lower bounds. The second
follows from part~\ref{prop:stab-susy-i}, the first assertion, and
$1\le\mathbb{E}[\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\mid\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge1]
=\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}/\mathbb{P}(\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge1)$.
head: environment

label: prop:kr-susy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:kr-susy}
Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main}, and let $\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}$ be the
number of $\varepsilon$-SUSY states at level $f$. Then
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\le\Sigma(f).
\]
head: environment
name: Annealed upper bound for SUSY states

label: lem:kr-ld
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-ld}
Let $A,B$ be real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices and $\iota\in(0,1]$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:kr-ld-a} $|\operatorname{ld}_\iota(A)-\operatorname{ld}_\iota(B)|\le\iota^{-1}\sqrt n\,\|A-B\|_{\rm HS}$.
\item\label{lem:kr-ld-b} If $n\ge2$ and $\check A$ is the compression of $A$ to a hyperplane, then
 $\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\check A)\le\operatorname{ld}_\iota(A)+\log\frac1\iota$ and
 $\operatorname{ld}_\iota(A)\le\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\check A)+\log\frac1\iota+2\log\max(\|A\|,1)$.
\item\label{lem:kr-ld-c} If $B=\mathsf D-E$ with $\mathsf D\succeq0$ diagonal and $E$ symmetric, then
 $\sum_i\varphi(|\lambda_i(B)|)\le\sum_i\varphi(\mathsf D_{ii}+\|E\|)$ for every nondecreasing
 $\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Spectral facts

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:kr-ld-a} By the Hoffman--Wielandt inequality \cite{HW},
$\sum_i(\lambda_i(A)-\lambda_i(B))^2\le\|A-B\|_{\rm HS}^2$, with eigenvalues in decreasing order;
combine it with the Lipschitz bound for $l_\iota$ and Cauchy--Schwarz.

\ref{lem:kr-ld-b} Let $\mu_1\ge\dots\ge\mu_{n-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $\check A$. By
Courant--Fischer, $\lambda_{j+1}\le\mu_j\le\lambda_j$. If $\mu_j\ge0$ then
$l_\iota(\mu_j)\le l_\iota(\lambda_j)$; if $\mu_j<0$ then $l_\iota(\mu_j)\le l_\iota(\lambda_{j+1})$.
With $t=\#\{j:\mu_j\ge0\}$ the indices used are $\{1,\dots,t\}\cup\{t+2,\dots,n\}$; only
$\lambda_{t+1}$ is unused, and $l_\iota(\lambda_{t+1})\ge\log\iota$. This is the first inequality. For
the second, let $s=\#\{i:\lambda_i\ge0\}$. If $2\le i\le s$ then $0\le\lambda_i\le\mu_{i-1}$, and if
$s+1\le i\le n-1$ then $\mu_i\le\lambda_i<0$; so $l_\iota(\lambda_i)$ is at most $l_\iota$ of the
indicated $\mu$, and these indices are distinct. At most two eigenvalues of $A$ are unassigned, each
with $l_\iota\le\log\max(\|A\|,1)$, and at most one eigenvalue of $\check A$ is unused, with
$l_\iota\ge\log\iota$.

\ref{lem:kr-ld-c} By Courant--Fischer, $|\lambda_i(B)-\lambda_i(\mathsf D)|\le\|E\|$, and
$\lambda_i(\mathsf D)\ge0$, so $|\lambda_i(B)|\le\lambda_i(\mathsf D)+\|E\|$; apply $\varphi$ and sum.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-deformed
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-deformed}
Let $a>0$ and $\rho\in\mathcal{P}([0,\infty))$ with $\int\log(1+y)\,\rho(dy)<\infty$. Let $N_k\to\infty$,
$a_k\to a$, and let $\mathsf D^{(k)}=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_{N_k})$ be deterministic, with $d_i\ge0$,
empirical laws converging weakly to $\rho$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-tails}
 \lim_{K\to\infty}\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac1{N_k}\sum_i\log_+\frac{d_i}K=0,\qquad
 \frac1{N_k}\log\bigl(1+\max_id_i\bigr)\to0 .
\end{equation}
Then $\int\log(1+|\lambda|)\,\check\nu[a,\rho](d\lambda)<\infty$, and for every continuous $\varphi$ with
$|\varphi(\lambda)|\le C_\varphi(1+\log(1+|\lambda|))$,
\[
 \frac1{N_k}\mathbb{E}\sum_{i=1}^{N_k}\varphi\bigl(\lambda_i(\mathsf D^{(k)}-\sqrt{a_k}\,W_{N_k})\bigr)
 \longrightarrow\int\varphi\,d\check\nu[a,\rho] .
\]
head: environment
name: Logarithmic law of large numbers

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\lambda_i=\lambda_i(\mathsf D^{(k)}-\sqrt{a_k}W)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison}\ref{lem:matrix-comparison-a}, $\mathbb{P}(\|W\|>6)\le2e^{-4N}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a}, the expected empirical spectral distribution of
$\mathsf D^{(k)}-\sqrt aW$ converges weakly to $\check\nu[a,\rho]$; by Weyl's inequality its
eigenvalues move by at most $|\sqrt{a_k}-\sqrt a|\,\|W\|$ when $a$ is replaced by $a_k$, so the
expected empirical spectral distribution $\bar\mu_k$ of $\mathsf D^{(k)}-\sqrt{a_k}W$ has the same
limit.

For $R\ge1$ let $\mathfrak t_R(y)=\log(1+y)\mathbf{1}\{y>R\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-ld}\ref{lem:kr-ld-c},
$\frac1N\sum_i\mathfrak t_R(|\lambda_i|)\le\frac1N\sum_i\mathfrak t_R(d_i+\sqrt{a_k}\|W\|)$. Take
$R\ge\max(12\sqrt{\bar a},18)$, $\bar a=\sup_ka_k$, and work on $\{\|W\|\le6\}$. If
$d_i+6\sqrt{a_k}>R$, then $d_i>R/2$ and $d_i+6\sqrt{a_k}\le2d_i$, and with $K=\sqrt{R/2}\ge3$ and
$d_i>K^2$, $\log(1+2d_i)\le3\log(d_i/K)$. So the right side is at most $3N^{-1}\sum_i\log_+(d_i/K)$. On
$\{\|W\|>6\}$ it is at most $\log(1+\max_id_i)+\log(1+\sqrt{a_k}\|W\|)$, and
$\mathbb{E}\log^2(1+\sqrt{a_k}\|W\|)\le a_k\mathbb{E}\|W\|_{\rm HS}^2=a_k(N+1)$. By Cauchy--Schwarz and
\eqref{eq:kr-tails},
\[
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac1{N_k}\mathbb{E}\sum_i\mathfrak t_R(|\lambda_i|)=0,\qquad
 \sup_k\frac1{N_k}\mathbb{E}\sum_i\log(1+|\lambda_i|)<\infty .
\]
Weak lower semicontinuity of integrals of nonnegative continuous functions gives the logarithmic
moment of $\check\nu[a,\rho]$. Finally, let $\mathsf k_R$ be continuous, $0\le\mathsf k_R\le1$, equal to
one on $[-R,R]$ and to zero off $[-R-1,R+1]$. Then
$\int\varphi\mathsf k_R\,d\bar\mu_k\to\int\varphi\mathsf k_R\,d\check\nu[a,\rho]$, while
$|\varphi|(1-\mathsf k_R)\le2C_\varphi\mathfrak t_R(|\cdot|)$ for $R\ge e$, which is small uniformly in large
$k$ for both measures.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-edge
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-edge}
Let $a>0$ and $\rho\in\mathcal{P}([0,\infty))$ with $\int\log(1+y)\,\rho(dy)<\infty$, and let $w_0\in\mathbb{R}$
satisfy
\[
 \inf\operatorname{supp}\rho\ge w_0+1,\qquad a\int\frac{\rho(dy)}{y-w_0}=w_0,\qquad
 a\int\frac{\rho(dy)}{(y-w_0)^2}\le1 .
\]
Then $\check\nu=\check\nu[a,\rho]$ satisfies $\check\nu((-\infty,0])=0$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kr-edge}
 \int\log\lambda\,\check\nu(d\lambda)=\int\log(y-w_0)\,\rho(dy)+\frac{w_0^2}{2a}\in\mathbb{R} .
\end{equation}
head: environment
name: Logarithmic potential at the edge

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $y_\rho=\inf\operatorname{supp}\rho>w_0$, $\mathfrak g(w)=\int\rho(dy)/(y-w)$ and $\mathcal Z(w)=w-a\mathfrak g(w)$,
holomorphic off $[y_\rho,\infty)$. On $(-\infty,y_\rho)$, $\mathfrak g,\mathfrak g',\mathfrak g''>0$, so
$\mathcal Z'=1-a\mathfrak g'$ is strictly decreasing and less than one. By hypothesis $\mathcal Z(w_0)=0$
and $\mathcal Z'(w_0)\ge0$, so $0<\mathcal Z'<1$ on $(-\infty,w_0)$, and $\mathcal Z$ is an increasing
homeomorphism of $(-\infty,w_0]$ onto $(-\infty,0]$. Let $\Omega$ be its inverse, which is $C^1$ on
$(-\infty,0)$ with $\Omega'=1/\mathcal Z'(\Omega)>1$, and put $\mathsf m(z)=(\Omega(z)-z)/a=\mathfrak g(\Omega(z))$
for $z\le0$.

\emph{No mass below zero.} Fix $E<0$. Since $\mathcal Z'(\Omega(E))>0$, the holomorphic inverse
function theorem gives a disc $U_E$ about $E$ and a holomorphic $\Omega_E$ on $U_E$, with values in
a disc about $\Omega(E)$ that avoids $[y_\rho,\infty)$, such that $\mathcal Z\circ\Omega_E=\mathrm{id}$ and
$\Omega_E=\Omega$ on $U_E\cap\mathbb{R}$. Then $\widetilde{\mathsf m}=(\Omega_E-z)/a=\mathfrak g(\Omega_E)$ solves
\eqref{eq:kr-pastur} on $U_E$, is real on $U_E\cap\mathbb{R}$ with $\widetilde{\mathsf m}'=(\Omega'-1)/a>0$
there, and after shrinking $U_E$, $\operatorname{Re}\widetilde{\mathsf m}'\ge\kappa_E>0$ on $U_E$. By the
Cauchy--Riemann equations $\operatorname{Im}\widetilde{\mathsf m}(t+\mathrm iv)\ge\kappa_Ev>0$ for
$t+\mathrm iv\in U_E$, $v>0$, so by uniqueness $\mathsf s=\widetilde{\mathsf m}$ on $U_E\cap\mathbb{C}^+$. Hence
$\operatorname{Im}\mathsf s(\lambda+\mathrm iv)\to0$ as $v\downarrow0$, uniformly on an interval $I_E$
about $E$. Since $\frac1\pi\operatorname{Im}\mathsf s(\lambda+\mathrm iv)$ is the density of $Y+v\mathsf C$,
with $Y\sim\check\nu$ and $\mathsf C$ an independent standard Cauchy variable, and $Y+v\mathsf C\to Y$ in law,
$\check\nu(I_E)\le\liminf_{v\downarrow0}\mathbb{P}(Y+v\mathsf C\in I_E)=0$. Countably many $I_E$ cover
$(-\infty,0)$, so $\check\nu((-\infty,0))=0$, and for real $z<0$, by dominated convergence,
$\int\check\nu(d\lambda)/(\lambda-z)=\mathsf m(z)$.

\emph{Two potentials.} For $z<0$ put $\mathcal L(z)=\int\log(\lambda-z)\,\check\nu(d\lambda)$ and
$\widetilde{\mathcal L}(z)=\int\log(y-\Omega(z))\,\rho(dy)+(\Omega(z)-z)^2/(2a)$. Both are finite
($y-\Omega(z)\ge1$ on $\operatorname{supp}\rho$, and $\check\nu$ has a logarithmic moment by
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-b} applied to the reflection,
$\check\nu((2\sqrt a+s,\infty))\le\rho([s,\infty))$, and the hypothesis
$\int\log(1+y)\,\rho(dy)<\infty$), and
differentiation under the integrals gives $\mathcal L'=-\mathsf m$ and
$\widetilde{\mathcal L}'=-\Omega'\mathfrak g(\Omega)+\mathsf m(\Omega'-1)=-\mathsf m$. As $z\to-\infty$,
$\mathcal L(z)-\log(-z)\to0$ by dominated convergence; also $0<\Omega(z)-z=a\mathfrak g(\Omega(z))\le a$
and $\mathfrak g(\Omega(z))\to0$, so $(y-\Omega(z))/(-z)\to1$ with values in $[\frac12,1+y]$ for
$|z|\ge\max(2a,1)$, and $\widetilde{\mathcal L}(z)-\log(-z)\to0$. So $\mathcal L=\widetilde{\mathcal L}$ on
$(-\infty,0)$.

\emph{The edge.} As $z\uparrow0$, $\log(\lambda-z)\downarrow\log\lambda$ on $[0,\infty)$, and monotone
convergence gives $\mathcal L(z)\to\int\log\lambda\,d\check\nu\in[-\infty,\infty)$. Also
$\Omega(z)\uparrow w_0$, $\log(y-\Omega(z))\downarrow\log(y-w_0)\ge0$ on $\operatorname{supp}\rho$, and
$(\Omega(z)-z)^2\to w_0^2$. So $\widetilde{\mathcal L}(z)$ converges to the right side of \eqref{eq:kr-edge},
which is finite. In particular $\check\nu(\{0\})=0$.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-susywindow
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Window facts

title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout, $W_1(\pi_x,\pi_0)\le W_2(\pi_x,\pi_0)\le\varepsilon$, and $r=q_x$.
\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-a} Under an optimal coupling,
$(N^{-1}|b|^2)^{1/2}\le\varepsilon+(\mathbb{E}_0b^2)^{1/2}$, and $|b_i|\le|b|$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-contact}\ref{lem:kr-contact-d} and Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints},
$u(r,x_i)^{-1}\le c_1^{-1}e^{2|b_i^{(r)}|}\le c_1^{-1}e^{2|b_i|+C\varepsilon}$.
\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-b} $\log U$ is $C_{34}$-Lipschitz and $\Phi(q,\cdot)$ is $1$-Lipschitz; integrate
over an optimal coupling. \ref{lem:kr-susywindow-c} By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints},
$|u(r,x_i)-U(b_i)|\le C|r-q|$ and $|b_i^{(r)}-b_i|\le C|r-q|$; $U$ is $C_{34}$-Lipschitz and $b\mapsto bM(b)$
is $C$-Lipschitz, since $|M+bU|\le1+C|b|e^{-2|b|}$; and
$\bigl||b^{(r)}|^2-|b|^2\bigr|\le\sum_i|b_i^{(r)}-b_i|(2|b_i|+C\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon N$ by
\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-a} and Cauchy--Schwarz. \ref{lem:kr-susywindow-d} This is
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-correction}\ref{lem:kr-correction-a} at $\eta=0$, together with
$h_0+V_\zeta(q,M_\#\pi_0)=f_0=f$ from \eqref{eq:kr-feta}.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-susystructure
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Structure of the conditional Hessian

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $e=x/|x|$ and complete it to an orthonormal basis $e,f_2,\dots,f_N$, the columns of $O$. The
covariances in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-block}, at radius $r$, show that the transverse
family $(f_j^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2H_N(x)f_k)$ has GOE covariance with off-diagonal variance $a_r/N$ and
is uncorrelated with $H_N(x)$, $\nablaH_N(x)$, the cross entries and the radial entry; so in these
coordinates it is $\sqrt{a_r}$ times the lower right block of a GOE matrix $W'$, which we complete
by independent entries that $\mathsf K$ ignores. The radial row is conditionally Gaussian with
covariance at most the unconditional one, of operator norm at most $C/N$; this gives
\ref{lem:kr-susystructure-a} for the Hamiltonian part and \ref{lem:kr-susystructure-b}. Its
conditional mean is $\frac{a_r\sqrt r}{c_r\sqrt N}Pb^{(r)}$ for the cross part and a linear
combination of $h$ and $d_x$ for the radial entry, with coefficients bounded on $\mathcal J_0$ because
$\det S_0(r)>0$ there (Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy}); and $|d_x|\le|b^{(r)}|/\sqrt N+C$. The
deterministic part of $\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)-\nabla^2H_N(x)$ is read off from \eqref{eq:kr-hessian}: its
compression to $x^\perp$ is that of $-\mathsf D_x$, and its norm is at most $\max_iu_i^{-1}+C$, since
$|\mathbf v_x|\le C_{34}\sqrt N$ and the scalar coefficient of $xx^{\mathsf T}$ is bounded.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-susydiag
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-susydiag}
Let $\varepsilon_k\downarrow0$, $N_k\to\infty$ and $x^{(k)}\in\mathcal W_{\varepsilon_k}\subset(-1,1)^{N_k}$, with
radii $r_k$. Then $a_{r_k}\to a$, and the matrices $\mathsf D_{x^{(k)}}$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-deformed} with $\rho=\rho_{q_f}$.
head: environment
name: Diagonals in shrinking windows

title: Proof
body_md:
We have $r_k\to q$, the diagonal entries are at least one, and $\chi_{x^{(k)}}\to\chi_0$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susywindow}\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-c}. Since
$|\log(A+B)-\log(A'+B')|\le|\log A-\log A'|+|B-B'|$ for $A,A'\ge1$, $B,B'\ge0$, and $\log u$ is
Lipschitz in the radius (Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-endpoints}),
$\max_i|\log d_i^{(k)}-\log(U(b_i)^{-1}+a\chi_0)|\le C|r_k-q|+|a_{r_k}\chi_{x^{(k)}}-a\chi_0|\to0$. The
empirical field laws converge weakly to $\pi_0$, so the empirical laws of the $d_i^{(k)}$ converge to
$\rho_{q_f}$. Next, $\log d_i^{(k)}\le C_2+2|b_i|$, so $\log_+(d_i^{(k)}/K)\le(C_2+2|b_i|-\log K)_+$, a
$2$-Lipschitz function of $b_i$ whose $\pi_0$-mean tends to zero as $K\to\infty$; and
$\log(1+\max_id_i^{(k)})=O(\sqrt{N_k})$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susywindow}\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-a}.
head: environment

label: lem:kr-susydet
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:kr-susydet}
For $H_0<\infty$ and $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ let $\mathfrak D_N(\varepsilon,H_0)$ be the supremum of
$N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\bigl[|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\bigm|\nablaH_N(x)=\mathbf g(x),\ H_N(x)=Nh\bigr]$ over
$x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ$ and $|h|\le H_0$. Then
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\mathfrak D_N(\varepsilon,H_0)\le-\mathbb{E}_0\log U+\frac a2\chi_0^2 .
\]
head: environment
name: An annealed determinant bound without a spectral gap

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\iota\in(0,1]$ and let $\mathbf A$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susystructure}. By
Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-ld}\ref{lem:kr-ld-a} and~\ref{lem:kr-susystructure}\ref{lem:kr-susystructure-b},
$\Psi(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\mathbf A_0+\mathsf K\mathbf y)$ is $L_\iota$-Lipschitz with
$L_\iota=\sqrt{C_{\mathsf K}}/\iota$. For a smooth $L_\iota$-Lipschitz function, Gaussian concentration
\cite[pp.~135--136]{Ledoux} gives $\mathbb{E} e^{\Psi(\mathbf Y)}\le e^{\mathbb{E}\Psi(\mathbf Y)+L_\iota^2/2}$; a
mollification $\Psi*\phi_\tau$, which is $L_\iota$-Lipschitz and within $L_\iota\tau$ of $\Psi$, extends
this to $\Psi$. Hence $\mathbb{E}|\det\mathbf A|\le\exp\{\mathbb{E}\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\mathbf A)+C_{\mathsf K}/(2\iota^2)\}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susystructure}\ref{lem:kr-susystructure-a}, the compression of $\mathbf A$ to
$x^\perp$ is that of $-\mathbf B_x$, $\mathbf B_x=\mathsf D_x-\sqrt{a_r}W$, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-ld}\ref{lem:kr-ld-b}, applied twice, and the evenness of $l_\iota$,
\[
 \operatorname{ld}_\iota(\mathbf A)\le\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\mathbf B_x)+2\log\tfrac1\iota
 +2\log\max(\|\mathbf A\|,1).
\]
By Jensen's inequality and Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-susystructure}\ref{lem:kr-susystructure-b}--\ref{lem:kr-susystructure-c}
and~\ref{lem:kr-susywindow}\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-a}, $\mathbb{E}\log\max(\|\mathbf A\|,1)\le C(1+H_0+\sqrt N)$.
Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak D_N(\varepsilon,H_0)\le\sup_{x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon}\frac1N\mathbb{E}\operatorname{ld}_\iota\bigl(\mathsf D_x-\sqrt{a_{q_x}}W\bigr)
 +\frac{C_{\mathsf K}/(2\iota^2)+2\log(1/\iota)+C(1+H_0+\sqrt N)}N .
\]
We claim that
$\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_N\sup_{x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon}N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\operatorname{ld}_\iota(\mathsf D_x-\sqrt{a_{q_x}}W)\le\int l_\iota\,d\check\nu_{q_f}$,
where $\check\nu_{q_f}=\check\nu[a,\rho_{q_f}]$. Otherwise there are $\epsilon_*>0$, $\varepsilon_k\downarrow0$,
$N_k\uparrow\infty$ and $x^{(k)}\in\mathcal W_{\varepsilon_k}$ with the normalized expectation at least
$\int l_\iota\,d\check\nu_{q_f}+\epsilon_*$; but by Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-susydiag} and~\ref{lem:kr-deformed},
with $\varphi=l_\iota$, which is continuous with $|l_\iota|\le\log(1/\iota)+\log(1+|\lambda|)$, the normalized
expectations converge to $\int l_\iota\,d\check\nu_{q_f}$. So the left side of the lemma is at most
$\int l_\iota\,d\check\nu_{q_f}$ for every $\iota\in(0,1]$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-edge} with $\rho=\rho_{q_f}$ and
$w_0=a\chi_0$: $\inf\operatorname{supp}\rho_{q_f}\ge w_0+1$, $a\int\rho_{q_f}(dy)/(y-w_0)=a\mathbb{E}_0U=w_0$, and
$a\int\rho_{q_f}(dy)/(y-w_0)^2=a\mathbb{E}_0U^2=1-\Delta_0\le1$. So $\check\nu_{q_f}$ lives on $(0,\infty)$ and
$\int\log\lambda\,d\check\nu_{q_f}=-\mathbb{E}_0\log U+\frac a2\chi_0^2$. As $\iota\downarrow0$,
$l_\iota\downarrow\log|\lambda|$ and $l_1$ is integrable, so monotone convergence finishes the proof.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-marked} on the compact shells
$\{x\in[-1+1/n,1-1/n]^N:|q_x-q|\le\varepsilon\}$ with the mark
$\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal W_\varepsilon}(x)\mathbf{1}\{|F_\zeta(x)/N-f|\le\varepsilon\}$, which drops the condition on $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$, and
let $n\to\infty$. Disintegrating over $H_N(x)=Nh$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\le\int_{\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ}\Upsilon(x)\,dx,\qquad
 \Upsilon(x)=p_{\nablaH_N(x)}(\mathbf g(x))\int_{I_x}Np_x(Nh)\,
 \mathbb{E}_{x,h}\bigl|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)\bigr|\,dh,
\]
where $p_x$ is the conditional density of $H_N(x)$ given $\nablaH_N(x)=\mathbf g(x)$, $\mathbb{E}_{x,h}$ the
conditional expectation given in addition $H_N(x)=Nh$, and
$I_x=[f-V_\zeta(q_x,\mu_x)-\varepsilon,\,f-V_\zeta(q_x,\mu_x)+\varepsilon]\subset[-H_0,H_0]$, since the
conjugates and the Onsager integral are bounded.

\emph{Gaussian factors.} As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count},
\begin{gather*}
 \log p_{\nablaH_N(x)}(\mathbf g(x))\le-\frac N2\log(2\pi c_r)-\frac{|b^{(r)}|^2}{2c_r}-N\mathcal Q_r(\chi_x,k_x),\\
 \mathcal Q_r(\chi,k)=\frac{a_r\chi k}{c_r}+\frac{a_r^2r\chi^2}{2c_r}-\frac{a_r(k+a_rr\chi)^2}{2c_r(c_r+a_rr)},
\end{gather*}
and $p_x(Nh)=(2\pi N\sigma_H^2(r))^{-1/2}\exp\{-N(h-h^\star_x)^2/(2\sigma_H^2(r))\}$ with
$h^\star_x=c_rd_x/(c_r+a_rr)$. Hence, for $x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ$,
\[
 \int_{I_x}Np_x(Nh)\,\mathbb{E}_{x,h}|\det\nabla^2F_\zeta(x)|\,dh
 \le\frac{2\varepsilon N}{\sqrt{2\pi N\sigma_H^2(r)}}\exp\Bigl\{N\mathfrak D_N(\varepsilon,H_0)
 -N\inf_{h\in I_x}\frac{(h-h^\star_x)^2}{2\sigma_H^2(r)}\Bigr\}.
\]

\emph{Change of variables.} With $x_i=M(b_i)$ and the density
$\pi_0'(b)=(2\pi c)^{-1/2}\exp\{-b^2/(2c)+\theta[\Phi(q,b)-\Phi(0,0)]\}$ of \eqref{eq:kr-law},
\[
 \int_{\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ}\Upsilon(x)\,dx=\int\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ}(x)\,\Upsilon(x)
 \prod_i\frac{U(b_i)}{\pi_0'(b_i)}\,\pi_0^{\otimes N}(db)
 \le\exp\Bigl\{N\sup_{x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ}\Xi_N(x)\Bigr\},
\]
where, for $x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ$,
\begin{align*}
 \Xi_N(x)\le{}&\mathfrak D_N(\varepsilon,H_0)+\frac1N\sum_i\log U(b_i)-\mathcal Q_r(\chi_x,k_x)
 -\theta\Bigl[\frac1N\sum_i\Phi(q,b_i)-\Phi(0,0)\Bigr]\\
 &+\frac12\log\frac c{c_r}+\frac{|b|^2}{2Nc}-\frac{|b^{(r)}|^2}{2Nc_r}
 -\inf_{h\in I_x}\frac{(h-h^\star_x)^2}{2\sigma_H^2(r)}+\frac{C\log N}N .
\end{align*}

\emph{Limits in the window.} Put $h^\star_0=cd_0/(c+aq)$. By \eqref{eq:kr-k0} and \eqref{eq:kr-h0},
$h_0-h^\star_0=\theta\sigma_H^2>0$, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-normalization}. For $h\in I_x$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susywindow}\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-c}--\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-d} and the continuity of
$c_r,a_r$ give $|h-h^\star_x|\ge\theta\sigma_H^2-o_\varepsilon(1)$ uniformly in $x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon$, and
$\sigma_H^2(r)\to\sigma_H^2$. With Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susywindow}\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-b}--\ref{lem:kr-susywindow-c}
for the other terms and Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-susydet} for the first, in which $-\mathbb{E}_0\log U$ cancels the
average of $\log U(b_i)$,
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal W_\varepsilon^\circ}\Xi_N(x)
 \le\frac a2\chi_0^2-\mathcal Q_q(\chi_0,k_0)-\theta\bigl[\mathbb{E}_0\Phi(q,b)-\Phi(0,0)\bigr]-\frac{\theta^2\sigma_H^2}2 .
\]
Finally, $\frac a2\chi^2-\mathcal Q_q(\chi,k)=a(k-c\chi)^2/(2c(c+aq))$, which is the quadratic identity
in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count}, and $\theta[\mathbb{E}_0\Phi(q,b)-\Phi(0,0)]=D(\pi_0\Vert\mathcal N(0,c))$
by \eqref{eq:kr-law}. So the right side is $\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_0,h_0)=\Sigma(f)$, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-normalization}.
head: environment

label: prop:kr-retained
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:kr-retained}
Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main}. Let $\eta$ be admissible and
$\delta\in(0,q/2)$, choose the parameters~\ref{step:kr-par1}--\ref{step:kr-par6}, and write
$\widehat C_N=\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)$ and $s_w=\delta'/(q-2w)$. We put
$\widehat C_N^{\,0}=\mathbf{1}\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:kr-retained-a} \textup{(Deterministic bounds.)} For every choice of
 $\mathcal W_N(w)$, $w\in(0,w_1]$, $N\ge3\gamma^{-1/2}$ and $\lambda\ge0$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)\le\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}\le n_N(s_w)^\lambda\,\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1),
 \]
 and, if $\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)>0$, then $1\le\mathbb{E}[\widehat C_N\mid\widehat C_N\ge1]\le n_N(s_w)$.
\item\label{prop:kr-retained-b} \textup{(Exponents.)} Let $L_\lambda^-$ and $L_\lambda^+$ be
 $\liminf_{w\downarrow0}\liminf_N$ and $\limsup_{w\downarrow0}\limsup_N$ of
 $N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}$. For every choice of $\mathcal W_N(w)$,
 \[
  L_\lambda^+\le\Sigma(f)+\theta\bigl(|f_\eta-f|+C_V\eta\bigr)-\frac\lambda2\log\Bigl(1-\frac{\delta'}q\Bigr),
 \]
 and for the choice of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count},
 $L_\lambda^-\ge\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta)+\frac12\log(1-\delta'/q)$, where the last term may be
 omitted when $\lambda\ge1$.
\item\label{prop:kr-retained-c} \textup{(Limits.)} For the choice of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count} there is
 $C_{\mathrm{ret}}$, independent of $\eta$, $\delta$ and $\lambda$, with
 \[
  \bigl|L_\lambda^\pm-\Sigma(f)\bigr|\le C_{\mathrm{ret}}\eta+\frac{1\vee\lambda}2\log\frac1{1-\delta'/q}\qquad(\lambda\ge0).
 \]
 So every iterated limit of $N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}$, with $N\to\infty$ innermost and then
 $w\downarrow0$, tends to $\Sigma(f)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$ and then $\eta\downarrow0$, uniformly for
 $\lambda$ in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$. Moreover, at every admissible $\eta$,
 $\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)>0$ for all sufficiently small $w$ and all large $N$, and
 \[
  \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\limsup_{w\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
  \log\mathbb{E}\bigl[\widehat C_N\bigm|\widehat C_N\ge1\bigr]=0 .
 \]
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Retained states are subexponentially many given existence

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{prop:kr-retained-a} By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-separation}, $\widehat C_N\le n_N(s_w)$ for every
realization. Since $\widehat C_N$ is a nonnegative integer,
$\mathbf{1}\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}\le\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}\le n_N(s_w)^\lambda\mathbf{1}\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}$; take
expectations, and divide by $\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)$ for $\lambda=1$.

\ref{prop:kr-retained-b} Let $M_N=\max_{[-1,1]^N}F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$. As in the proof of~\ref{step:stab-k2},
every retained point $x$ has
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)/N\ge f-|f_\eta-f|-C_V\eta-2C_V\varrho(w)-N^{-2},
\]
so
$\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}\subset\{M_N\ge N(f-\varepsilon_N)\}$ with
$\varepsilon_N=|f_\eta-f|+C_V\eta+2C_V\varrho(w)+N^{-2}$. By Markov's inequality at $\theta=\theta_f$,
$\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)\le e^{-\theta N(f-\varepsilon_N)}\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} and Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}\ref{prop:max-fm-a},
$\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\le\Lambda(\theta)$, and $\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f=\Sigma(f)$. With
\ref{prop:kr-retained-a}, Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-code} and $s_w\to\delta'/q$ as $w\downarrow0$, this gives the
bound on $L_\lambda^+$; only the deterministic facts of Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-separation} were used. For the
lower bound, \ref{prop:kr-retained-a} with $\lambda=1$ gives
$\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}\ge\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)\ge\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N/n_N(s_w)$; apply
Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-count} and~\ref{lem:kr-code}. For $\lambda\ge1$, $\widehat C_N^{\,\lambda}\ge\widehat C_N$.

\ref{prop:kr-retained-c} By Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-normalization} and \eqref{eq:kr-feta},
$|\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta)-\Sigma(f)|\le C_\Sigma\eta$ and $|f_\eta-f|\le(L+C_V)\eta$; put
$C_{\mathrm{ret}}=C_\Sigma+\theta(L+2C_V)$. Substituting in~\ref{prop:kr-retained-b}, using
$\frac\lambda2\le\frac{1\vee\lambda}2$ on the upper side, the fact that the logarithmic term appears on
the lower side only for $\lambda<1$, and $L_\lambda^-\le L_\lambda^+$, gives the two-sided bound. Its right
side is nondecreasing in $\lambda$, which gives the uniformity on compact sets, and $\delta'=\delta$ for
small $\delta$. The number $\Sigma_{\rm KR}(\pi_\eta,h_\eta)$ is finite, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count}
there is $w_2\in(0,w_1]$ such that, for $w\le w_2$, $\mathbb{E}\widehat C_N>0$, hence
$\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N\ge1)>0$, for all large $N$. For such $w$ and $N$,
\ref{prop:kr-retained-a} and Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-code} give
$0\le\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}[\widehat C_N\mid\widehat C_N\ge1]\le-\frac12\log(1-s_w)$, which tends to
$-\frac12\log(1-\delta'/q)$ as $w\downarrow0$, and to zero as $\delta\downarrow0$.
head: environment

label: rem:kr-retained
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:kr-retained}
At a strictly Plefka-stable first contact, Boursier's isolated count $\widehat N$ satisfies
$\mathbb{E}\widehat N\le n_N\,\mathbb{P}(\widehat N\neq0)$ (Step~(2) of \cite[Section~3.2]{Bou26b}, with
\cite[Lemma~3.11 and Section~3.7]{Bou26b}), which with \cite[Proposition~3.6]{Bou26b} and the proof
of \cite[Proposition~3.3]{Bou26b} gives the analogue of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-retained}. Here
the contact may be marginal, the data are tilted, and $\Sigma(f)$ is reached only as
$\eta\downarrow0$. Part~\ref{prop:kr-retained-c} covers the moments $0<\lambda<1$ behind the
heuristic $\log n=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}(n^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ of \cite[p.~2]{Bou26b}. At a
fixed cutoff the bound of~\ref{prop:kr-retained-a} is exponential, with rate $-\frac12\log(1-\delta'/(q-2w))$.
Nothing is claimed about all critical points of $F_{\zeta_f}$ in the windows (without the
marks~\ref{step:kr-ret4}--\ref{step:kr-ret5}) or all TAP states given that one exists.
head: environment

label: rem:kr-window
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:kr-window}
Convexity of $\xi$ on $[-1,0]$ enters the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} only in
\eqref{eq:kr-bregman}, whose left side
is $2N\mathcal D_\xi(R,q_{\alpha\beta})$, $q_{\alpha\beta}\in\{q,r\}$, with
$\mathcal D_\xi(R,Q)=\xi(R)-\xi(Q)-\xi'(Q)(R-Q)$, since $K_r-\xi$ is affine. On the slice
$\{q_y=q,\ R(x,y)=r\}$, $R(y,z)\ge2r^2/q-q>-q$ (decompose along $x$ and $x^\perp$), and for
$R\le0\le Q\le1$, $\partial_Q\mathcal D_\xi(R,Q)=\xi''(Q)(Q-R)\ge0$, so
$\mathcal D_\xi(R,Q)\ge\mathcal D_\xi(R,0)=\xi(R)$. Hence
Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-comparison}\ref{lem:kr-comparison-a} holds whenever $\xi\ge0$ on $[-q,0]$,
and~\ref{lem:kr-comparison-b} on $I=[\delta,q-\delta]$ once also $\omega\le\delta^2/(4q)$, which
keeps the overlaps of the net points above $-q$. So the lower bound of
Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} extends to a level $f$ of a mixture with two active degrees that is
not convex on $[-1,1]$ but has $\xi\ge0$ on $[-q_f,0]$, provided the variational inputs of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:kr-contact} and~\ref{lem:matrix-band}, proved or cited only under \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, hold at
$f$; for $\xi(t)=\beta_2^2t^2+\beta_3^2t^3$ this reads $q_f\le\beta_2^2/\beta_3^2$, while convexity
on $[-q_f,0]$ would need $q_f\le\beta_2^2/(3\beta_3^2)$. The matching upper bound needs a positivity
principle in the spirit of \cite{PanPos}, and the corresponding step of \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CGKLM}
is only sketched there, so we state no two-sided result for non-convex mixtures.
head: environment
name: A sign window instead of convexity

label: rem:kr-summable
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:kr-summable}
Besides the variational inputs and convexity on $[-1,0]$ (Remark~\ref{rem:kr-window}), $\xi$ enters
through two active degrees and bounded derivatives. Two active degrees give $\det S_0>0$ and
$\sigma_H^2>0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy}), hence the energy shift, the strict signs of $A_2$ and
$\tau$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-block}, the nondegeneracy in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-c3} and the conditional
density of the energy in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-count}. Derivatives of $\xi$ on $[-1,1]$ of order at
most eight bound the pointwise variance and the canonical metric of $D^3H_N$
(Lemmas~\ref{lem:matrix-third} and~\ref{lem:kr-c3}). The class $\mathcal{C}$ enters only through the
cited facts on the Parisi equation and on the TAP correction (Remark~\ref{rem:rpde}); a time change reducing them to a
polynomial covariance is a natural route to replacing $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ in
Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} by $\sum_pp^8\beta_p^2<\infty$, under strict convexity and two active
degrees. We do not claim this extension: a complete proof must also revisit the uses of the power
series of $\xi$ (as in Lemma~\ref{lem:kr-energy}) and the regularity of $H_N$ behind the Kac--Rice
formula. No statement of this paper depends on it.
head: environment
name: Where the covariance enters

label: prop:nc-example
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:nc-example}
There is $\varepsilon_*\in(0,\frac12]$ such that every covariance
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-family}
 \xi(t)=bt^2+et^4,\qquad b>\tfrac12,\qquad e>0,\qquad b-\tfrac12+e<\varepsilon_*,
\end{equation}
has the following properties, where $a_0=\xi''(0)=2b$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:nc-example-a} \textup{(Equilibrium.)} $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=[0,v_{\mathrm P}]$ for some
 $v_{\mathrm P}\in(0,1)$, $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})=0$, and $U_{\mathrm P}:=\Phi_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}},xx}(0,0)=a_0^{-1/2}$.
\item\label{prop:nc-example-b} \textup{(Marginal first contact.)} There is $\theta_0\in(0,1)$ such
 that for every $\theta\in(0,\theta_0)$
 \[
  \zeta_\theta(\{0\})=\theta,\qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_\theta=\{0\}\cup[q_\theta,v_\theta],\qquad 0<q_\theta<v_\theta<1,
 \]
 $q_\theta$ is the first positive contact of $\zeta_\theta$, and it is marginal:
 \[
  \xi''(q_\theta)\,\mathbb{E}\,\Phi_{\zeta_\theta,xx}(q_\theta,X_{q_\theta})^2=1,
 \]
 where $X$ is the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta_\theta$.
\item\label{prop:nc-example-c} \textup{(Levels.)} The number $f_0:=p(\theta_0)$ satisfies
 $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f_0<f_1$, and $\theta_f\in(0,\theta_0)$ for every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_0)$. Hence, for every
 such $f$, $\zeta_f=\zeta_{\theta_f}$ and its first positive contact $q_f=q_{\theta_f}$ has $\Delta(q_f)=0$.
\item\label{prop:nc-example-d} \textup{(Onset.)} Put
 $D_{\mathrm P}=\xi''''(0)\,U_{\mathrm P}^2+a_0^3\,\Phi_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}},xxxx}(0,0)^2$. Then
 $D_{\mathrm P}>0$, and
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-onset}
  \lim_{\theta\downarrow0}\frac{q_\theta}{\theta}=\frac{3\sqrt{a_0}}{D_{\mathrm P}},\qquad
  \lim_{\theta\downarrow0}\frac{\zeta_\theta(\{q_\theta\})}{\theta}=\frac12 .
 \end{equation}
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Marginal first contacts near criticality

label: rem:nc-hyp
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:nc-hyp}
The covariances \eqref{eq:nc-family} are polynomials with $\xi''(t)=2b+12et^2>0$ on $[-1,1]$, so
they satisfy \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, lie in $\mathcal{C}$ and have two active degrees: the hypotheses of
Theorems~\ref{thm:exist}, \ref{thm:struct} and~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-a}. The condition
$b>\frac12$, that is $\xi''(0)>\xi_{\mathrm c}''(0)=1$, forces $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\neq\delta_0$; $e>0$ gives
$\xi'''>0$ on $(0,1]$, which puts the origin in $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$, and $\xi''''(0)>0$, which makes
$D_{\mathrm P}$ positive.
head: environment
name: The hypotheses

title: Outline of the proof
body_md:
We perturb the critical pair $(\xi_{\mathrm c},\delta_0)$; write
$\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta}$. At the critical pair $\Gamma<\mathrm{id}$ on $(0,1]$, so near criticality every contact
lies in a small-time region $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$. On a plateau of $\zeta$ (an open interval of zero
mass), $\Gamma'''$ is an explicit expectation of the spatial derivatives of $\Phi_\zeta$ of orders
two to four along the Auffinger--Chen process (Appendix~\ref{app:nc-plateau}); at the critical pair
and at the origin it is at least $4$, because the third and fourth derivatives of $\log\cosh$ at $0$
are $0$ and $-2$. So near criticality $\Gamma'$ is strictly convex on every plateau below
$t_{\mathrm c}$. At a contact $t$, $\Gamma(t)=t$ and $\Gamma'(t)\le1$; if two contacts $t_1<t_2$
enclosed a plateau, the mean of $\Gamma'$ over $(t_1,t_2)$ would equal one and would be strictly
smaller than $\frac12(\Gamma'(t_1)+\Gamma'(t_2))\le1$. This adapts the near-critical gap-exclusion
mechanism of Zhou \cite{Zho26a} to contacts that may carry no mass (Appendix~\ref{app:nc-gap}), and
it applies to every constrained minimizer, since all of them stay close to $\delta_0$
(Appendix~\ref{app:nc-confine}). So the positive support of $\zeta_\theta$ is an interval
$[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ of contacts, whence $\Gamma'(q_\theta)=1$; the onset limits
\eqref{eq:nc-onset} come from the cubic behaviour of $\Gamma-\mathrm{id}$ on $(0,q_\theta)$
(Appendix~\ref{app:nc-proof}).
head: manual

label: eq:nc-K
title: Notation
body_md:
In Appendices~\ref{app:nc-plateau}--\ref{app:nc-confine} the covariance varies
in the set
\[
 \mathcal K=\bigl\{\xi_{b,e}(t)=bt^2+et^4:\ \tfrac12\le b\le1,\ 0\le e\le1\bigr\},\qquad
 d(\xi_{b,e})=\bigl(b-\tfrac12\bigr)+e .
\]
It contains $\xi_{\mathrm c}=\xi_{1/2,0}$ and, since $\varepsilon_*\le\frac12$, the family
\eqref{eq:nc-family}, on which $d(\xi)<\varepsilon_*$. Every $\xi\in\mathcal K$ lies in $\mathcal{C}$, and
on $[0,1]$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-K}
 1\le\xi''\le14,\qquad |\xi''-1|\le12\,d(\xi),\qquad 0\le\xi'''\le24\,d(\xi),\qquad
 \xi''''=24e\le24\,d(\xi).
\end{equation}
For $\xi\in\mathcal K$ and $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ let $\Phi=\Phi^\xi_\zeta$, $X$, $\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta}^\xi$,
$\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}^\xi_\zeta$ and $P^\xi_\zeta$ be the objects of
Sections~\ref{sec:intro-setting}--\ref{sec:intro-structure} computed with the covariance $\xi$, and
write
\[
 a=\xi'',\qquad \alpha=\bar{\zeta},\qquad u=\partial_x\Phi,\qquad
 U_t=\partial_x^2\Phi(t,X_t),\quad V_t=\partial_x^3\Phi(t,X_t),\quad W_t=\partial_x^4\Phi(t,X_t).
\]
A tilde marks the same objects for a second pair $(\tilde\xi,\tilde\zeta)$. Let
$m_1(\zeta)=\int t\,\zeta(dt)=\|1-\alpha\|_{L^1}$, the Wasserstein distance from $\zeta$ to
$\delta_0$. A \emph{plateau} of $\zeta$ is an open interval $I\subset(0,1)$ with $\zeta(I)=0$; on
it $\alpha$ is constant, and the constant is the \emph{height} of $I$.
head: manual

label: lem:nc-jets
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Jets and their stability

label: eq:nc-u
title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:nc-jets-a} The continuity of $\partial_x^j\Phi$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}. For a fixed covariance, its uniform
convergence along weakly convergent sequences of measures is \cite[Proposition~1(i)]{AC15a}; here
$\Phi$ is the solution of \cite{AC15a} by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}.
Evenness is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}, and $|u|\le1$,
$0<\partial_xu\le1$ are Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a} and, for general $\zeta$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}, with
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a} for the strict positivity (see also \cite[Proposition~2]{AC15a}). By the
uniform convergence it suffices to prove the bounds of \ref{lem:nc-jets-a}
and~\ref{lem:nc-jets-b} for finitely supported $\zeta$ and $\tilde\zeta$, which we now assume. Then
$\Phi$ is given on each step of $\alpha$ by the Cole--Hopf formula \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf}, all
$\partial_x^ju$ are continuous across the steps, and $u$ solves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-u}
 \partial_tu+\tfrac a2\,\partial_x^2u+a\alpha\,u\,\partial_xu=0,\qquad u(1,x)=\tanh x .
\end{equation}
For $k\ge2$, differentiating \eqref{eq:nc-u} $k$ times in $x$ gives a linear backward equation for
$\partial_x^ku$ with second-order coefficient $a/2$, drift $a\alpha u$, zeroth-order coefficient
$(k+1)a\alpha\,\partial_xu$, and a forcing term that is a polynomial in
$\partial_xu,\dots,\partial_x^{k-1}u$ whose coefficients are bounded in terms of $k$. Its terminal value
$\partial_x^k\tanh$ is bounded. The Feynman--Kac formula along the Auffinger--Chen process started
at $(t,x)$, chained over the steps (the maximum principle), bounds $\partial_x^ku$ in terms of $k$,
$\|a\|_\infty$ and $C_1,\dots,C_{k-1}$, and induction on $k$ gives \ref{lem:nc-jets-a}.

\ref{lem:nc-jets-b} The difference $w=u-\tilde u$ vanishes at $t=1$ and solves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-w}
 \partial_tw+\tfrac a2\,\partial_x^2w+a\alpha\,u\,\partial_xw+a\alpha\,(\partial_x\tilde u)\,w
 =-\tfrac{a-\tilde a}2\,\partial_x^2\tilde u-(a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha)\,\tilde u\,\partial_x\tilde u .
\end{equation}
Its drift and zeroth-order coefficients are bounded, and by \ref{lem:nc-jets-a} the supremum over
$x$ of the right side at time $s$ is at most $C_2|a-\tilde a|(s)+|a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha|(s)$.
The maximum principle bounds $\|w\|_\infty$ by a constant times the time integral of this
supremum, which is \eqref{eq:nc-jet} for $k=0$. Differentiating \eqref{eq:nc-w} $k$ times gives an
equation of the same form for $\partial_x^kw$, with bounded coefficients, whose forcing is
$\partial_x^k$ of the right side of \eqref{eq:nc-w}, bounded as before by \ref{lem:nc-jets-a},
plus products of $\partial_x^jw$, $j<k$, with derivatives of $u$ and $\tilde u$. Induction on $k$
gives \eqref{eq:nc-jet}. All constants depend only on $k$ and on the bounds \eqref{eq:nc-K}.

\ref{lem:nc-jets-c} This follows from $X_t=\int_0^ta\alpha\,u(s,X_s)\,ds+\int_0^t\sqrt a\,dB_s$ and
$|\alpha u|\le1$.

\ref{lem:nc-jets-d} Drive $X$ and $\tilde X$ by the same Brownian motion and let
$D=\sup_{t\le1}|X_t-\tilde X_t|$. Since $|\partial_xu|\le1$, $\alpha\le1$ and $|\tilde u|\le1$,
\[
 \bigl|a\alpha\,u(s,X_s)-\tilde a\tilde\alpha\,\tilde u(s,\tilde X_s)\bigr|
 \le\|a\|_\infty\bigl(|X_s-\tilde X_s|+\|u-\tilde u\|_\infty\bigr)+|a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha|(s).
\]
Gronwall's inequality, applied pathwise, and Doob's inequality for the martingale
$\int_0^t(\sqrt a-\sqrt{\tilde a})\,dB_s$ give
\[
 (\mathbb{E} D^2)^{1/2}\le e^{\|a\|_\infty}\Bigl(\|a\|_\infty\|u-\tilde u\|_\infty
 +\|a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha\|_{L^1}+2\|\sqrt a-\sqrt{\tilde a}\|_{L^2}\Bigr),
\]
and $|\sqrt a-\sqrt{\tilde a}|\le\frac12|a-\tilde a|$ because $a,\tilde a\ge1$. Now
$|\Gamma(t)-\tilde\Gamma(t)|\le2\mathbb{E}|u(t,X_t)-\tilde u(t,\tilde X_t)|\le2(\|u-\tilde u\|_\infty+\mathbb{E} D)$.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}, $\Gamma'=a\,\mathbb{E} U_t^2$, and since
$0<U\le1$ and $|\partial_x^2u|\le C_2$,
$|\Gamma'(t)-\tilde\Gamma'(t)|\le|a-\tilde a|(t)+2\|a\|_\infty(\|\partial_x(u-\tilde u)\|_\infty+C_2\mathbb{E} D)$.
For the Parisi functional, integrating the Parisi equation in time at $x=0$ (on each step for
finitely supported $\zeta$, and in general by approximation, Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}) gives
\[
 P^\xi_\zeta=\frac12\int_0^1a(t)\bigl(\partial_xu(t,0)+\alpha(t)\,u(t,0)^2-t\,\alpha(t)\bigr)\,dt ,
\]
whose integrand changes by at most
$|a-\tilde a|+\|a\|_\infty(\|\partial_x(u-\tilde u)\|_\infty+2\|u-\tilde u\|_\infty)+2|a\alpha-\tilde a\tilde\alpha|$.
Together with \eqref{eq:nc-jet} for $k=0,1$, these bounds give \eqref{eq:nc-continuity}.
head: environment

label: lem:nc-plateau
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Calculus of $\Gamma$

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:nc-plateau-a} The first claim is
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}. Since $X_0=0$ and $\Phi(0,\cdot)$ is even
(Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-jets}\ref{lem:nc-jets-a}), $\Gamma(0)=u(0,0)^2=0$ and
$V_0=\partial_x^3\Phi(0,0)=0$, and $U_0>0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-jets}\ref{lem:nc-jets-a}.

\ref{lem:nc-plateau-b} On $I$ the Parisi equation has the constant coefficient $\omega$. Taking, in
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}, step approximations of $\alpha$ that equal $\omega$ on a compact
subinterval $[s,t']\subset I$, one sees that on $[s,t']\times\mathbb{R}$ the function $\Phi$ is the
Cole--Hopf solution \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} with coefficient $\omega$ and terminal value
$\Phi(t',\cdot)$. So $u$ and its spatial derivatives are $C^1$ in $t$ on $I$; $u$ solves
\eqref{eq:nc-u} with $\alpha=\omega$, and its spatial derivatives solve the differentiated
equations, classically. It\^o's formula
gives, on $I$,
\[
 dU_t=-\omega\xi''(t)\,U_t^2\,dt+\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,V_t\,dB_t,\qquad
 dV_t=-3\omega\xi''(t)\,U_tV_t\,dt+\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,W_t\,dB_t,
\]
with bounded integrands, so
\[
 \frac{d}{dt}\mathbb{E} U_t^2=\xi''\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(V^2-2\omega U^3\bigr),\qquad
 \frac{d}{dt}\mathbb{E}\bigl(V_t^2-2\omega U_t^3\bigr)=\xi''\,\mathbb{E}\bigl(W^2-12\omega UV^2+6\omega^2U^4\bigr).
\]
The right sides are continuous in $t$, by the continuity of $\partial_x^j\Phi$, the continuity of
the paths of $X$ and bounded convergence. Differentiating $\Gamma'=\xi''\,\mathbb{E} U^2$ twice gives
\eqref{eq:nc-second} and \eqref{eq:nc-third}. The statement at the endpoints follows from the mean
value theorem.

\ref{lem:nc-plateau-c} This is \cite[Proposition~3, (21)--(22)]{AC15a}. There the expectations are
taken along the time-changed Brownian motion $M(t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{\xi''(s)}\,dB_s$, with the
exponential weight of \cite[(13)]{AC15a}. By It\^o's formula and the Parisi equation, the logarithm
of that weight is the Girsanov exponent of the drift $\xi''\bar{\zeta}\,\Phi_x$, so by Girsanov's
theorem the weight is the density of the law of $(X_s)_{s\le t}$ with respect to that of
$(M(s))_{s\le t}$. Hence the statements of \cite{AC15a} hold along $X$; in particular $\Gamma$ is
the function of \cite[(18)]{AC15a}. Subtracting the two one-sided derivatives gives
\eqref{eq:nc-jump}.
head: environment

label: lem:nc-near
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Two estimates near the critical pair

label: eq:nc-near-jets
title: Proof
body_md:
We compare with the critical pair, for which $\tilde a\equiv1$, $\tilde\alpha\equiv1$ and
$\tilde u=\tanh$. By \eqref{eq:nc-K}, $\|a-1\|_\infty\le12\,d(\xi)$ and
$\|a\alpha-1\|_{L^1}\le\|a-1\|_\infty+\|\alpha-1\|_{L^1}\le12\,d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta)$, so
\eqref{eq:nc-jet} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-near-jets}
 \|\partial_x^ku-\partial_x^k\tanh\|_\infty\le C\bigl(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta)\bigr),\qquad k=1,2,3,
\end{equation}
where here and below $C$ depends only on $\mathcal K$.

\ref{lem:nc-near-a} Let $t\in I\cap(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, where $I$ has height $\omega\in[0,1]$, and
put $R_\omega(y_1,y_2,y_3)=y_3^2-12\omega y_1y_2^2+6\omega^2y_1^4$, so that the last expectation in
\eqref{eq:nc-third} is $\mathbb{E} R_\omega(U_t,V_t,W_t)$. At the critical values,
$R_\omega(1,0,-2)=4+6\omega^2\ge4$. On the cube $[-C_\sharp,C_\sharp]^3$ with
$C_\sharp=\max\{C_1,C_2,C_3,2\}$, which contains $(U_t,V_t,W_t)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-jets}\ref{lem:nc-jets-a}, $R_\omega$ is Lipschitz with a constant $L$ that does
not depend on $\omega\in[0,1]$. By \eqref{eq:nc-critical}, $(1,0,-2)$ is the value at $x=0$ of
$(\partial_x\tanh,\partial_x^2\tanh,\partial_x^3\tanh)$, and these functions are Lipschitz. So
\eqref{eq:nc-near-jets} and Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-jets}\ref{lem:nc-jets-c} give
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl|(U_t,V_t,W_t)-(1,0,-2)\bigr|\le C\bigl(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta)+\mathbb{E}|X_t|\bigr)
 \le C_\flat\bigl(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta)+\sqrt t\bigr)
\]
for a constant $C_\flat$. Hence $\mathbb{E} R_\omega(U_t,V_t,W_t)\ge4-LC_\flat(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta)+\sqrt t)$.
The other two terms of \eqref{eq:nc-third} are at most $Cd(\xi)$ in absolute value, by
\eqref{eq:nc-K}. Choose $t_{\mathrm c}\in(0,1)$ with $LC_\flat\sqrt{t_{\mathrm c}}\le1$, and then
$\varepsilon_2>0$ with $2LC_\flat\varepsilon_2+C\varepsilon_2\le1$. Then
$\mathbb{E} R_\omega(U_t,V_t,W_t)\ge2$, so $\xi''\ge1$ gives
$\xi''(t)^3\,\mathbb{E} R_\omega(U_t,V_t,W_t)\ge4-1-LC_\flat(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta))$, and
$\Gamma'''(t)\ge3-LC_\flat(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta))-Cd(\xi)\ge2$.

\ref{lem:nc-near-b} By \eqref{eq:nc-critical-gamma}, $\kappa_F:=\min_{[t_{\mathrm c},1]}(t-\Gamma_{\mathrm c}(t))>0$.
By \eqref{eq:nc-continuity} with the critical pair,
$\sup_{[0,1]}|\Gamma-\Gamma_{\mathrm c}|\le C(d(\xi)+m_1(\zeta))$. Decreasing $\varepsilon_2$ so that
$2C\varepsilon_2<\kappa_F$, we get $\Gamma(t)<t$ on $[t_{\mathrm c},1]$, and then
$\mathcal{O}'=\frac12\xi''(t-\Gamma)>0$ there.
head: environment

label: lem:nc-contact
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Contact conditions

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}, $\mathcal{O}\in C^2([0,1])$ with
$\mathcal{O}'=-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma-t)$ and $\mathcal{O}''=-\frac12\xi'''(\Gamma-t)-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma'-1)$. At a
local minimum $t\in(0,1)$, $\mathcal{O}'(t)=0\le\mathcal{O}''(t)$, and $\xi''(t)>0$ gives \eqref{eq:nc-contact}.
At $0$, $\Gamma(0)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-plateau}\ref{lem:nc-plateau-a}, so
$\Gamma(s)-s=(\Gamma'(0)-1)s+o(s)$ and
\[
 \mathcal{O}(t)-\mathcal{O}(0)=-\frac12\int_0^t\xi''(s)\bigl(\Gamma(s)-s\bigr)\,ds
 =-\frac{\xi''(0)}4\bigl(\Gamma'(0)-1\bigr)t^2+o(t^2).
\]
A local minimum at $0$ makes the coefficient of $t^2$ nonnegative, and $\xi''(0)>0$ gives
$\Gamma'(0)\le1$.
head: environment

label: lem:nc-gap
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nc-gap}
Let $\xi\in\mathcal K$, $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $t_{\mathrm c}\in(0,1)$, and assume that
$\Gamma'''\ge2$ at every point of $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$ that lies in a plateau of $\zeta$. Then there
are no $0\le t_1<t_2<t_{\mathrm c}$ with $\zeta((t_1,t_2))=0$ such that \eqref{eq:nc-contact} holds
at $t_1$ and at $t_2$.
head: environment
name: Gap exclusion

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that such $t_1,t_2$ exist. Then $(t_1,t_2)$ is a plateau contained in $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$,
so $\Gamma'''\ge2$ on it and $\Gamma'$ is strictly convex on $(t_1,t_2)$. Since $\Gamma'$ is
continuous on $[t_1,t_2]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-plateau}\ref{lem:nc-plateau-a}), it is strictly convex
on $[t_1,t_2]$ and lies strictly below its chord on $(t_1,t_2)$. By \eqref{eq:nc-contact} at both
ends,
\[
 1=\frac{\Gamma(t_2)-\Gamma(t_1)}{t_2-t_1}
 =\frac1{t_2-t_1}\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\Gamma'(t)\,dt
 <\frac{\Gamma'(t_1)+\Gamma'(t_2)}2\le1,
\]
a contradiction.
head: environment

label: lem:nc-confine
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Confinement

label: eq:nc-trial
title: Proof
body_md:
For $\xi\in\mathcal K$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$ the measure $\delta_0$ is feasible at $\theta$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nc-trial}
 \inf_{\zeta}P^\xi_\zeta\le P^\xi_{\zeta^\xi_\theta}\le P^\xi_{\delta_0}.
\end{equation}
Suppose that the lemma fails for some $\varepsilon>0$. Then there are $\xi_n\in\mathcal K$ with
$d(\xi_n)\to0$ and $\theta_n\in[0,1]$ such that $\zeta_n:=\zeta^{\xi_n}_{\theta_n}$ has
$m_1(\zeta_n)\ge\varepsilon$. By compactness a subsequence converges weakly to some $\zeta_\infty$,
and $m_1(\zeta_\infty)\ge\varepsilon$, so $\zeta_\infty\ne\delta_0$. Weak convergence on $[0,1]$
gives $\|\bar{\zeta_n}-\bar{\zeta_\infty}\|_{L^1}\to0$, and $\|\xi_n''-1\|_\infty\to0$ by
\eqref{eq:nc-K}. By \eqref{eq:nc-continuity},
$P^{\xi_n}_{\zeta_n}\to P^{\xi_{\mathrm c}}_{\zeta_\infty}$ and
$P^{\xi_n}_{\delta_0}\to P^{\xi_{\mathrm c}}_{\delta_0}$ along the subsequence. The right half of
\eqref{eq:nc-trial} gives in the limit $P^{\xi_{\mathrm c}}_{\zeta_\infty}\le
P^{\xi_{\mathrm c}}_{\delta_0}=\min_\zeta P^{\xi_{\mathrm c}}_\zeta$, so $\zeta_\infty$ is a Parisi
measure of $\xi_{\mathrm c}$, and $\zeta_\infty=\delta_0$ by uniqueness. This is a contradiction.
head: environment

label: cor:nc-standing
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:nc-standing}
Let $t_{\mathrm c}$ and $\varepsilon_2$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-near}, let $\varepsilon_3$ be
given by Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-confine} for $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_2$, and put
$\varepsilon_*=\min\{\frac12,\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3\}$. Let $\xi\in\mathcal K$ with
$d(\xi)<\varepsilon_*$, let $\theta\in[0,1]$, and let $\zeta=\zeta^\xi_\theta$, with $\Gamma$ and
$\mathcal{O}$ its second-moment function and obstacle. Then the following hold.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{cor:nc-standing-a} $\Gamma'''\ge2$ at every point of $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$ that lies in a
 plateau of $\zeta$; and $\Gamma<\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal{O}'>0$ on $[t_{\mathrm c},1]$.
\item\label{cor:nc-standing-b} Every minimum point of $\mathcal{O}$ over $(0,1]$ lies in
 $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, and every minimum point of $\mathcal{O}$ over $[0,1]$ lies in $[0,t_{\mathrm c})$.
\item\label{cor:nc-standing-c} No two points $t_1<t_2$ of $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}$ satisfy
 $\zeta((t_1,t_2))=0$. If $\theta=0$, the same holds for any two points of $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}$.
\end{thmlist}
head: environment
name: Standing estimates

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{cor:nc-standing-a} By Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-confine}, $m_1(\zeta)<\varepsilon_2$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-near} applies.
\ref{cor:nc-standing-b} The obstacle is strictly increasing on $[t_{\mathrm c},1]$ by
\ref{cor:nc-standing-a}. So at every $t\in[t_{\mathrm c},1]$ it takes smaller values just below $t$,
at points of $(0,1]$; hence $t$ is not a minimum point over $(0,1]$ or over $[0,1]$.
\ref{cor:nc-standing-c} By \ref{cor:nc-standing-b}, the points of $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}$ are local
minima in $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, and a point of $\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}$ is either such a local minimum
or the point $0$, at which $\mathcal{O}$ restricted to $[0,1]$ is minimal. By Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-contact},
\eqref{eq:nc-contact} holds at all these points, and Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-gap}, whose hypothesis is
\ref{cor:nc-standing-a}, excludes the configuration.
head: environment

label: rem:nc-onset
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:nc-onset}
As $\zeta_\theta((0,q_\theta))=0$, Step~5 gives $\zeta_\theta([0,q_\theta])=\frac32\theta+o(\theta)$.
Parisi and Rizzo \cite[Section~IV and Appendix~B, (B2)]{PR} found this picture for the
Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model in a perturbative replica computation, with the replica number $n$
for $\theta$: their order parameter $q(x)$ has a first plateau of height $\frac32n\dot q(0)+o(n)$
ending at $x_{\mathrm c}=\frac32n+O(n^2)$, where $\dot q(0)$ is the equilibrium slope at $x=0$. For
that model at low temperature, the companion paper \cite{PeiB}, not used here, shows by the same
calculus that the first positive contact is marginal for small $\theta$, with position and atom
given to leading order by \eqref{eq:nc-onset} at $\xi''''(0)=0$.
head: environment
name: The onset and its prediction

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\xi$ be as in \eqref{eq:nc-family}, $\theta\in(0,\theta_0)$ and $\zeta=\zeta_\theta$, and write
$\Gamma=\Gamma_{\zeta}$, $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_\zeta$, $q=q_\theta$, $v=v_\theta$ and $h=\Gamma-\mathrm{id}$. We use the
following facts.
\begin{itemize}
\item By Proposition~\ref{prop:nc-example}\ref{prop:nc-example-b} and Step~2 of its proof,
 $\operatorname{supp}\zeta=\{0\}\cup[q,v]$, every point of $[q,v]$ minimizes $\mathcal{O}$ over $(0,1]$, $\Gamma'(q)=1$,
 and $\mathcal{O}(r)>\mathcal{O}(q)$ for $0\le r<q$.
\item By Corollary~\ref{cor:nc-standing}, $q,v\in(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, $h'''\ge2$ at every point of
 $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$ that lies in a plateau of $\zeta$, and $h<0$ on $[t_{\mathrm c},1]$.
\item By Lemma~\ref{lem:nc-plateau}, $h\in C^1([0,1])$, $h(0)=0$, and $h$ is $C^3$ on every
 plateau. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-c}, $\mathcal{O}'=-\frac12\xi''h$ and
 $\mathcal{O}''=-\frac12\xi'''h-\frac12\xi''(\Gamma'-1)$, with $\xi''>0$.
\end{itemize}

\emph{The middle.} Every point of $[q,v]$ is a minimum point of $\mathcal{O}$ over $(0,1]$ and lies in
$(0,1)$, so $\mathcal{O}'=0$ there, that is $h=0$ on $[q,v]$. Hence $h'=0$ on $(q,v)$ and, by the
continuity of $\Gamma'$, at $q$ and $v$.

\emph{The left plateau.} The interval $(0,q)$ is a plateau inside $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, so
$h'''\ge2$ on it, and $h(0)=h(q)=h'(q)=0$. Suppose that $h(r)=0$ for some $r\in(0,q)$. Rolle's
theorem gives zeros of $h'$ at some $s_1\in(0,r)$ and $s_2\in(r,q)$, besides the zero at $q$; then
zeros of $h''$ in $(s_1,s_2)$ and in $(s_2,q)$; then a zero of $h'''$ in $(0,q)$, which is
impossible. ($h'$ is continuous on $[0,q]$ and $h''$ is $C^1$ on the open plateau, which is all
Rolle's theorem needs.) So $h$ has no zero in $(0,q)$ and has constant sign there. Since
$\mathcal{O}(r)-\mathcal{O}(q)=\frac12\int_r^q\xi''h>0$ for $r\in(0,q)$, the sign is positive: $h>0$ on $(0,q)$.

\emph{The right plateau.} On $(v,1]$ the distribution function of $\zeta$ equals one, so
$(v,t_{\mathrm c})$ lies in a plateau inside $(0,t_{\mathrm c})$, where $h'''\ge2$; also
$h(v)=h'(v)=0$, and $h(t_{\mathrm c})<0$. Two distinct zeros $r<r'$ of $h$ in $(v,t_{\mathrm c})$
would give zeros of $h'$ at $v$, in $(v,r)$ and in $(r,r')$, hence two zeros of $h''$ and one of
$h'''$, which is impossible. If $h$ had exactly one zero $r\in(v,t_{\mathrm c})$ with $h'(r)=0$, then
$h'$ would vanish at $v$, in $(v,r)$ and at $r$, with the same contradiction. If $h$ had exactly one
zero $r\in(v,t_{\mathrm c})$ with $h'(r)\ne0$, then $h$ would change sign at $r$, and $h(t_{\mathrm c})<0$
would force $h>0$ on $(v,r)$; then $\mathcal{O}(t)-\mathcal{O}(v)=-\frac12\int_v^t\xi''h<0$ for $t\in(v,r)$,
contradicting the minimality of $\mathcal{O}(v)$. So $h$ has no zero in $(v,t_{\mathrm c})$, and
$h(t_{\mathrm c})<0$ gives $h<0$ on $(v,t_{\mathrm c})$, hence on $(v,1]$.

\emph{Conclusion.} Since $\mathcal{O}'=-\frac12\xi''h$ with $\xi''>0$, the obstacle is strictly decreasing
on $[0,q]$, constant on $[q,v]$ and strictly increasing on $[v,1]$. Hence
$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}=[q,v]=\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$, and also $\{t\in(0,1]:\Gamma(t)=t\}=[q,v]$. On
$[q,v]$ one has $h=0$ and $\Gamma'=1$, so $\mathcal{O}''=0$ there.
head: environment

label: lem:moments-guerra
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Guerra's bound for fractional moments

title: Proof
body_md:
Talagrand works with a Gaussian Hamiltonian on $\{-1,1\}^N$ whose covariance is $N\xi(R(\sigma,\tau))$,
under the summability condition $\sum_pp^2\beta_p^2<\infty$, and allows an external field
\cite[(3.1)--(3.4) and Theorem~3.1]{Tal07}; we take the field to be zero. The summability
condition holds under \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, and $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta$ depends only on the law of the centered
Gaussian vector $(H_N(\sigma))_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N}$, whose covariance is $N\xi(R(\sigma,\tau))$. So
\cite[Theorem~6.1]{Tal07}, which assumes $\xi$ convex, applies. Its parameters are numbers
$\theta=m_0<m_1<\dots<m_k<1$ and $0=q_0<q_1<\dots<q_k<q_{k+1}=1$; let $\alpha$ be the probability
measure on $[0,1]$ with $\alpha([0,t])=m_l$ for $t\in[q_l,q_{l+1})$, $0\le l\le k$. Talagrand's
partition function is $2^NZ_N$, and the terminal value of his Parisi recursion is $\log\cosh$. In
our normalization his bound therefore reads
\[
 \frac1{N\theta}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le X_0-\frac12\sum_{l=0}^km_l\bigl(\vartheta(q_{l+1})-\vartheta(q_l)\bigr),
\]
where $X_{k+1}=\log\cosh(z_0+\dots+z_k)$ for independent centered Gaussian variables $z_l$ of
variance $\xi'(q_{l+1})-\xi'(q_l)$, and $X_l=m_l^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}_l\exp(m_lX_{l+1})$ for
$l=k,\dots,0$, with $\mathbb{E}_l$ the expectation in $z_l$ \cite[(5.4)--(5.5)]{Tal07}. By the
Cole--Hopf formula \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}, $X_l=\Phi_\alpha(q_l,z_0+\dots+z_{l-1})$
for every $l$, so $X_0=\Phi_\alpha(0,0)$. Since $\vartheta'(t)=t\xi''(t)$, the sum equals
$\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\alpha([0,t])\,dt$. The right-hand side is therefore $P_\alpha$, which proves
\eqref{eq:moments-guerra} for this $\alpha$.

Now let $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with $\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta$, and put $c(t)=\alpha([0,t])$, so
that $c\ge\theta$ on $[0,1)$. For $n>1/(1-\theta)$ let $c_n=\theta$ on $[0,1/n)$ and
\[
 c_n(t)=\min\Bigl\{1-\tfrac1n,\ \max\bigl\{\theta,\ n^{-1}\lfloor nc(t)\rfloor\bigr\}\Bigr\}
 \qquad\text{for } t\in[1/n,1).
\]
Then $c_n$ is a nondecreasing step function with finitely many values in $[\theta,1-1/n]$, equal to
$\theta$ on $[0,1/n)$. Its distinct values and its jump points are parameters as above, so
\eqref{eq:moments-guerra} holds for the measure $\alpha_n$ with distribution function $c_n$ on
$[0,1)$. Since $c\ge\theta$, we have $|c_n-c|\le1/n$ on $[1/n,1)$, hence
$\|c_n-c\|_{L^1}\le2/n$. By the Lipschitz bound
$|P(c_1)-P(c_2)|\le\frac12\xi''(1)\|c_1-c_2\|_{L^1}$ of
Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}\ref{cor:pde-step-c}, which holds for measurable coefficients by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iii}, and since $P(\bar{\zeta})=P_\zeta$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}), $P_{\alpha_n}\to P_\alpha$. This
proves \eqref{eq:moments-guerra}. The last claim follows by taking the infimum over $\alpha$,
because $\Lambda(\theta)=\theta\inf\{P_\alpha:\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta\}$.
head: environment

label: rem:moments-interpolation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:moments-interpolation}
For $\alpha$ with finitely many atoms, the time derivative of Guerra's interpolation equals
$-\frac12\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\alpha([0,t])\,dt$ minus averages of $\xi(R)-\xi(q)-\xi'(q)(R-q)$ over
overlaps $R$, with weight $\frac12(\alpha(\{0\})-\theta)\ge0$ at $q=0$ and $\frac12\alpha(\{q\})$ at
the atoms $q>0$; convexity on $[-1,1]$ makes these
remainders nonnegative. For non-convex $\xi$ a remainder at a negative overlap can be negative, and
the upper half of \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ needs another proof (for $\xi$ that is not convex on $[-1,1]$ this step
is sketched in \cite[proof of Theorem~2.1]{CGKLM}; we do not rely on it).
head: environment
name: Convexity and $\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta$

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall the setting: $\xi$ satisfies \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, and $\theta\in(0,1)$.

\ref{prop:max-fm-a} This is Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-guerra}.

\ref{prop:max-fm-b} Let $\theta\le\theta_*$. The Parisi measure satisfies
$\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})=\theta_*\ge\theta$, so it is admissible in the constrained problem and
$\Lambda(\theta)=\theta P_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$. By \eqref{eq:max-crude-M}, $M_N\ge Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ for every
realization. On the event $B_t=\{M_N\le\logZ_N+tN\}$ we therefore have
$Z_N^\theta\ge e^{\theta(M_N-tN)}\ge e^{\theta N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)}$, so that
$\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge e^{\theta N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)}\mathbb{P}(B_t)$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:max-upper},
$\mathbb{P}(B_t)\to1$. Hence $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge\theta(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)$ for every $t>0$. This
part uses only \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.

\ref{prop:max-fm-c} Let $\xi$ be even. If $\xi$ is a polynomial, \eqref{eq:moments-talagrand} is
the claim. In general, truncate $\xi$ and $H_N$ at degree $D$ as in
Appendix~\ref{app:gauss-bounds}, with $D$ at least the smallest active degree. Then
$\xi_{\le D}$ is a nonzero even polynomial, so \eqref{eq:moments-talagrand} holds for the
truncated model:
$\lim_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta=\Lambda^{(D)}(\theta)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds}\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d3} and~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1},
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta
 \ge\Lambda^{(D)}(\theta)-\theta\varepsilon_D-\frac{\theta^2}2\xi_{>D}(1)
 \ge\Lambda(\theta)-\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)-\theta\varepsilon_D-\frac{\theta^2}2\xi_{>D}(1),
\]
and the right-hand side tends to $\Lambda(\theta)$ as $D\to\infty$. No Kac--Rice argument enters.

\ref{prop:max-fm-d} Let $\xi$ be convex on $[-1,1]$ but not even. Then $\xi$ has two active
degrees (see the beginning of Appendix~\ref{app:kr}), and Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} applies.
If $\theta_*=1$, part~\ref{prop:max-fm-b} covers every
$\theta\in(0,1)$. Otherwise, by Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-b}, every
$\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$ equals $\theta_f$ for the level $f=\Lambda'(\theta)\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, and
$\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$. Fix such $\theta$ and $f$, and let $\varepsilon>0$. Every
witness $(\zeta,x)$ of $\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$ has $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$, and
$M_N\geF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$, so $\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\subset\{M_N\ge N(f-\varepsilon)\}$ and
\[
 \mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\ge e^{\theta N(f-\varepsilon)}\,\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\bigr).
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} gives, at this $\varepsilon$,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f).
\]
Hence
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\ge\theta(f-\varepsilon)+\Sigma(f)
 =\Lambda(\theta)-\theta\varepsilon .
\]
Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$; Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} turns the bound for
$\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}$ into the same bound for $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta$. Part~\ref{prop:max-fm-b} covers
$\theta\le\theta_*$. The lower bound of Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} is proved in
Appendix~\ref{app:kr} by a first-moment count of critical points and a deterministic
spherical-code bound; it uses neither \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ nor
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-c}--\ref{thm:exist-e}, so the argument is not circular.

Finally, part~\ref{prop:max-fm-a} together with~\ref{prop:max-fm-c} for even $\xi$, and
with~\ref{prop:max-fm-b} and~\ref{prop:max-fm-d} otherwise, gives \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}.
head: environment

label: prop:moments-pure
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:moments-pure}
Let $\xi(t)=\beta^2t^p$ with $\beta>0$ and $p\ge2$ even, and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. For every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f).
\]
head: environment
name: Pure even covariances

label: cor:moments-pure-all
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:moments-pure-all}
Let $\xi$ be as in Proposition~\ref{prop:moments-pure}. Then \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds. Consequently
$\lim_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}=\Lambda(\theta)$ for every $\theta\in(0,1)$, and the conclusions
of Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} hold at every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. These statements
are thereby proved without \cite[Section~7]{Tal07}.
head: environment
name: A second route to the fractional-moment formula

title: Proof
body_md:
The upper half of \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ is Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}\ref{prop:max-fm-a}, and the lower half
for $\theta\le\theta_*$ is Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}\ref{prop:max-fm-b}. Let
$\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-b}, $\theta=\theta_f$ for
$f=\Lambda'(\theta)\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, and $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$. For $\varepsilon>0$,
$\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\ge e^{\theta N(f-\varepsilon)}\mathbb{P}(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon)$, so
Proposition~\ref{prop:moments-pure} gives
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\ge\theta(f-\varepsilon)+\Sigma(f)
 =\Lambda(\theta)-\theta\varepsilon .
\]
Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b}. This proves \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}};
the other statements are Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-c}, \ref{thm:exist-d}.
head: environment

label: lem:moments-cov
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moments-cov}
Let $\xi_a$ and $\xi_b$ satisfy \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, and assume that $\kappa=\xi_b-\xi_a$ has nonnegative
coefficients. For all $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, $r\in[0,1]$, $y\in\mathbb{R}$ and
$\mu\in\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:moments-pde-compare}
 0\le\Phi^{\xi_b}_\alpha(r,y)-\Phi^{\xi_a}_\alpha(r,y)\le\kappa'(1)-\kappa'(r),
\end{equation}
and each of $|V^{\xi_b}_\alpha(r,\mu)-V^{\xi_a}_\alpha(r,\mu)|$,
$|V^{\xi_b}_{\mathrm{TAP}}(r,\mu)-V^{\xi_a}_{\mathrm{TAP}}(r,\mu)|$ and
$|P^{\xi_b}_\alpha-P^{\xi_a}_\alpha|$ is
at most $\kappa'(1)$.
head: environment
name: Comparison of covariances

title: Proof
body_md:
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds}\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1} uses only that $\xi$ and
$\xi_{\le D}$ satisfy \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}\ and that $\xi_{>D}=\xi-\xi_{\le D}$ has nonnegative coefficients.
With $(\xi,\xi_{\le D},\xi_{>D})$ replaced by $(\xi_b,\xi_a,\kappa)$, its representation
\eqref{eq:gauss-delta} reads, for $\alpha$ with finitely many atoms and $u=\Phi^{\xi_b}_\alpha$,
\[
 \Phi^{\xi_b}_\alpha(r,y)-\Phi^{\xi_a}_\alpha(r,y)
 =\frac12\,\mathbb{E}\int_r^1\kappa''(s)\bigl(u_{xx}+\bar{\alpha}\,u_x^2\bigr)(s,X_s)\,ds ,
\]
where $X$ is a diffusion started at $(r,y)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class} with $G=1$,
$0\le u_{xx}+\bar{\alpha}\,u_x^2\le2$, which gives \eqref{eq:moments-pde-compare} for such $\alpha$.
For general $\alpha$, approximate $\bar{\alpha}$ in $L^1$ by distribution functions of measures with
finitely many atoms; by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i},
\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}, applied to each covariance, the solutions converge uniformly, and
\eqref{eq:moments-pde-compare} passes to the limit.

If two functions satisfy $\psi_a\le\psi_b\le\psi_a+K$, their concave conjugates
$m\mapsto\inf_y\{\psi(y)-my\}$ satisfy the same inequalities. So
$0\le\Phi^{\xi_b,*}_\alpha-\Phi^{\xi_a,*}_\alpha\le\kappa'(1)$ on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$, and at
$m=\pm1$ by continuity. The integral terms of $V$ differ by
$\frac12\int_r^1t\kappa''(t)\alpha([0,t])\,dt\in[0,\frac12(\kappa'(1)-\kappa(1))]$. Hence
$V^{\xi_b}_\alpha-V^{\xi_a}_\alpha\in[-\frac12\kappa'(1),\kappa'(1)]$, which gives the bound for $V$;
the bound for $V_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ follows by taking infima over the common set $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$.
Finally,
$\Phi^\xi_\alpha(0,\cdot)$ is even and convex, so $\Phi^{\xi,*}_\alpha(0,0)=\Phi^\xi_\alpha(0,0)$ and
$P^\xi_\alpha=V^\xi_\alpha(0,\delta_0)$.
head: environment

label: lem:moments-perturb
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moments-perturb}
In the setting \eqref{eq:moments-perturbation}:
\begin{romanlist}
\item\label{lem:moments-perturb-i} For every realization and every $x\in[-1,1]^N$,
 $|F^\gamma_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-\gamma H^{(l)}_N(x)|\le d_\gamma N$. Hence
 $|M^\gamma_N-M_N|\le\gamma S_N+d_\gamma N$.
\item\label{lem:moments-perturb-ii} $|P^\gamma_\zeta-P_\zeta|\le d_\gamma$ for every
 $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. Moreover $|f_{\mathrm{eq}}^\gamma-f_{\mathrm{eq}}|\le d_\gamma$,
 $|\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma-\overline{\Lambda}|\le d_\gamma$ on $[0,1]$, and $|\Sigma_\gamma-\Sigma|\le d_\gamma$
 on $\mathbb{R}$.
\item\label{lem:moments-perturb-iii} $\liminf_{\gamma\downarrow0}f_1^\gamma\gef_1$.
 Consequently, for every $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ there is $\gamma_0(f)>0$ such that
 $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}}^\gamma,f_1^\gamma)$ for all $\gamma\in(0,\gamma_0(f))$.
\end{romanlist}
head: environment
name: The perturbed models

title: Proof
body_md:
\ref{lem:moments-perturb-i} By \eqref{eq:moments-identities} for both models,
$F^\gamma_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-\gamma H^{(l)}_N(x)
=N[V^{\xi_\gamma}_{\mathrm{TAP}}-V^\xi_{\mathrm{TAP}}](q_x,\mu_x)$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-cov} with $(\xi_a,\xi_b)=(\xi,\xi_\gamma)$, for which $\kappa(t)=\gamma^2t^l$
and $\kappa'(1)=d_\gamma$.
Taking maxima over $[-1,1]^N$ gives the bound on $|M^\gamma_N-M_N|$.

\ref{lem:moments-perturb-ii} The first bound is Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-cov}. The quantities $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$
and $\Lambda(\theta)/\theta$, $0<\theta<1$, are infima of $P_\zeta$ over sets of order
parameters that do not depend on the covariance, so $|f_{\mathrm{eq}}^\gamma-f_{\mathrm{eq}}|\le d_\gamma$ and
$|\Lambda_\gamma-\Lambda|\le\theta d_\gamma\le d_\gamma$ on $[0,1)$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-c}, $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=\xi(1)/2$ and
$\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma(1)=\xi_\gamma(1)/2$, which differ by $\gamma^2/2\le d_\gamma$. Taking infima of
$\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma(\theta)-\theta f$ and $\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$ over $\theta\in[0,1]$ gives the
bound for $\Sigma$.

\ref{lem:moments-perturb-iii} By Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-b}, \ref{thm:exist-c},
applied to $\xi$ and to $\xi_\gamma$, the functions $\overline{\Lambda}$ and $\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma$ are convex and
finite on $[0,1]$: $\Lambda$ is continuously differentiable on $(0,1)$ with nondecreasing
derivative, $\Lambda(\theta)\to0$ as $\theta\downarrow0$ because
$f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le\Lambda(\theta)/\theta\le P_{\delta_0}$, and $\overline{\Lambda}(1)$ is finite. For a convex function
$g$ that is finite on $[0,1]$, the chord slope $(g(1)-g(1-h))/h$ is nonincreasing in
$h\in(0,1]$, and $g'_-(1)=\sup_{0<h\le1}(g(1)-g(1-h))/h$. By~\ref{lem:moments-perturb-ii}, for
every $h\in(0,1]$,
\[
 f_1^\gamma\ge\frac{\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma(1)-\overline{\Lambda}_\gamma(1-h)}h
 \ge\frac{\overline{\Lambda}(1)-\overline{\Lambda}(1-h)}h-\frac{2d_\gamma}h .
\]
Let $\gamma\downarrow0$, then take the supremum over $h$. For the last claim,
$f_{\mathrm{eq}}^\gamma\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+d_\gamma<f$ once $d_\gamma<f-f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and $f_1^\gamma>f$ for all
small $\gamma$ because $\liminf_{\gamma\downarrow0}f_1^\gamma\gef_1>f$.
head: environment

label: lem:moments-field
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moments-field}
Let $c_l=2l\sqrt{2/\pi}$. For every $N$ and every $u\ge0$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(S_N\ge(c_l+u)N\bigr)\le e^{-u^2N/2}.
\]
head: environment
name: The perturbing field

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:gauss-sup-p} with $p=l$ and $\rho=1$, $\mathbb{E} S_N\le c_lN$. The variable $S_N$ is the
supremum of the centered Gaussian process $(x,s)\mapsto sH^{(l)}_N(x)$ on $[-1,1]^N\times\{-1,1\}$,
whose variance $Nq_x^l$ is at most $N$, so \eqref{eq:gauss-conc} gives
$\mathbb{P}(S_N-\mathbb{E} S_N\ge uN)\le e^{-u^2N/2}$.
head: environment

label: eq:moments-gamma
title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ and $\varepsilon>0$, and put $\theta=\theta_f$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-b}, $\theta\in(0,1)$ and $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$;
also $-\infty<\Sigma(f)\le\overline{\Lambda}(0)=0$. Choose $\gamma\in(0,\gamma_0(f))$, with $\gamma_0(f)$ from
Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-perturb}\ref{lem:moments-perturb-iii}, so small that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:moments-gamma}
 d_\gamma\le\min\Bigl\{1,\frac{\theta\varepsilon}8\Bigr\},\qquad
 \frac\varepsilon{4\gamma}>c_l,\qquad
 \frac12\Bigl(\frac\varepsilon{4\gamma}-c_l\Bigr)^2>1-\Sigma(f).
\end{equation}
Put
\[
 a_N=\mathbb{P}\bigl(M^\gamma_N\ge N(f-\tfrac\varepsilon2)\bigr),\qquad
 b_N=\mathbb{P}\bigl(M^\gamma_N>N(f+\tfrac\varepsilon2)\bigr),\qquad
 p_N=\mathbb{P}\bigl(\gamma S_N>\tfrac{\varepsilon N}4\bigr).
\]
Inside the first event and outside the other two, $|M^\gamma_N-Nf|\le\varepsilon N/2$ and
$\gamma S_N\le\varepsilon N/4$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-perturb}\ref{lem:moments-perturb-i}
with $d_\gamma<\varepsilon/4$ gives $|M_N-Nf|\le\varepsilon N$. Hence
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge a_N-b_N-p_N .
\]
We bound the three terms.
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{The existence term.} Every witness $(\zeta,x)$ of
 $\mathcal E^\gamma_{N,\varepsilon/2}(f)$ has $F^\gamma_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon/2)$, so
 $a_N\ge\mathbb{P}(\mathcal E^\gamma_{N,\varepsilon/2}(f))$. Since $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}}^\gamma,f_1^\gamma)$,
 Proposition~\ref{prop:kr-main} applies to $\xi_\gamma$ at the level $f$, and it gives
 $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(\mathcal E^\gamma_{N,\varepsilon/2}(f))\ge\Sigma_\gamma(f)$. With
 Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-perturb}\ref{lem:moments-perturb-ii},
 $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log a_N\ge\Sigma(f)-d_\gamma$.
\item \emph{The overshoot term.} Markov's inequality gives
 $b_N\le e^{-\theta N(f+\varepsilon/2)}\mathbb{E} e^{\theta M^\gamma_N}$. By
 Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} and Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-guerra} for $\xi_\gamma$, and by
 Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-perturb}\ref{lem:moments-perturb-ii},
 \[
  \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta M^\gamma_N}
  =\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E}(Z^\gamma_N)^\theta
  \le\Lambda_\gamma(\theta)\le\Lambda(\theta)+d_\gamma .
 \]
 Hence, by~\eqref{eq:moments-gamma},
 \[
  \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log b_N\le\Lambda(\theta)+d_\gamma-\theta f-\frac{\theta\varepsilon}2
  =\Sigma(f)+d_\gamma-\frac{\theta\varepsilon}2\le\Sigma(f)-d_\gamma-\frac{\theta\varepsilon}4 .
 \]
\item \emph{The field term.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-field} with
 $u=\varepsilon/(4\gamma)-c_l>0$ and by~\eqref{eq:moments-gamma},
 $\limsup_NN^{-1}\log p_N\le-\frac12(\varepsilon/(4\gamma)-c_l)^2<\Sigma(f)-1\le\Sigma(f)-d_\gamma$.
\end{itemize}
Put $s_\gamma=\Sigma(f)-d_\gamma>-\infty$. Then $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log a_N\ge s_\gamma$ and
$\limsup_NN^{-1}\log(b_N+p_N)<s_\gamma$. So for every sufficiently small $\eta>0$ and all large
$N$, $a_N\ge e^{N(s_\gamma-\eta)}$ and $b_N+p_N\le e^{N(s_\gamma-2\eta)}$, whence
$a_N-b_N-p_N\ge e^{N(s_\gamma-\eta)}(1-e^{-\eta N})$ and
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log(a_N-b_N-p_N)\ge s_\gamma-\eta$.
Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f)-d_\gamma .
\]
The left-hand side involves $H_N$ alone and does not depend on $\gamma$. Letting
$\gamma\downarrow0$ proves the proposition.
head: environment

label: rem:moments-pure-scope
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:moments-pure-scope}
Corollary~\ref{cor:moments-pure-all} and Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-a} yield
generalized TAP critical points at rate $\Sigma(f)$ at every level, of the kind in
Remark~\ref{rem:exist-points}. Boursier uses this perturbation \cite[Section~3.2]{Bou26b} but
transfers retained critical points, by \cite[Proposition~B.1]{Bou26b} under the strict Plefka
condition, false at marginal first contacts; our transfer of $M_N$ needs no
Hessian estimate, only the deterministic comparison of
Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-perturb}\ref{lem:moments-perturb-i} and the Gaussian tail of
Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-field}.
